items.s: THE " SOUTHERN." Report of the Southern Counties Cross Country Championship at Shenfield on February 28th: Arthur Allum second to L. H. Weatherill (S.L.H.), Belgrave third team with 159 points and, for the first time, winners of the Guildford Cup for closing in a full team of twelve; with Junior (5 miles) and Senior results. The junior team scores print "1. South London H." twice (60 and 61 pts.). The senior team scores run onto page 9, where the heading and South London's line are printed misplaced inside the Forthcoming Fixtures text. The Southern Counties Cross Country Championship was held this year at Shenfield and we can look back upon the date, February 28th, with a certain amount of satisfaction. The Ten Miles Championship, the 43rd of the series, was preceded by a race over five miles, open to Juniors under 21 years of age on the date of the race. Our team did not shine in finishing 17th, but A. Kench once again gave signs of developing into a very useful runner. In the Senior race we had great hopes of seeing Arthur Allum head the field, but at the half-distance it was apparent that he had undergone a "bad time" in the early stages, for he was in the fifth position, about 200 yards behind the leader, Weatherill, of South London Harriers. In the second lap, however, Arthur made a really great effort and in fact caught Weatherill with a little over a mile to go, but then had to let the S.L.H., runner get away to win by thirty yards. This running places Arthur in the front rank and next year we expect to acclaim him as Southern Champion. Our next men home were Warboys (16th), Penny (18th), Footer (33rd) (a really wonderful effort this, after a very short preparation), Jack Flower (38th), and Duffett (52nd). These gave us a total of 159pts., and although we did not improve upon last year's third position, we certainly confirmed it, and with a lower score than that at Brighton. Aldershot Command A.C., who finished twelve points behind us last year, by slightly better packing beat us by the same margin on this occasion and took second place. The winners, South London Harriers, who were without Oddie and Thompson of last year's team, ran amazingly well to finish 6 men in the first 17 positions. They are to be heartily congratulated upon such a fine performance. Our remaining six men ran well, our 12th man finishing 120th. South London's 12th man was 133rd, and so we became holders for the first time of a trophy which has been in the possession of S.L.H. for many years past : "The Guildford Cup," presented by Mr. Odling-Smee for the first Club, with Surrey Headquarters, finishing their complete team of twelve men. The twelve men concerned will receive a Club medal as a souvenir of this occasion, and next year we hope that "The Frank Wynne Cup" will follow the " Guildford Cup" to its new home. It will be of interest, no doubt, to compare our showing this year with that of 1928, when the Championship was held over the same course. On that occasion our first man home was Footer (33rd). This year Footer was again 33rd, but fourth man for the Club. Our sixth man in 1928 was A. Clark, 133rd, whereas our 12th man was 120th this year. We were placed 10th three years ago with 422 points, this year 3rd with 159 points. Thus in the course of three years we have shown considerable progress, and it is almost certain that this rate of improvement will be maintained or even accelerated. JUNIOR RACE RESULT (5 MILES). items.label: February 1931
items.sum: Preview of the road and track season: the 5 Miles Road race and handicap from Wimbledon on March 28th, the London to Brighton Relay on April 11th, the first Club track meeting at Battersea Park on May 2nd, the match with the London Athletic Club, the Southern Amateur Athletic League and the Kinnaird Trophy. items.s: FORTHCOMING FIXTURES. Preview of the road and track season: the 5 Miles Road race and handicap from Wimbledon on March 28th, the London to Brighton Relay on April 11th, the first Club track meeting at Battersea Park on May 2nd, the match with the London Athletic Club, the Southern Amateur Athletic League and the Kinnaird Trophy. Also an Inter-Club field events competition; entries to the Running Hon. Sec., E. A. Duffett. "Well, thank goodness that's over," I can imagine our cross country men saying now that another strenuous season has just finished. We now come to what we might term the Road season, the ultimate aim being, of course, the London to Brighton Relay race. On March 28th we are holding a 5 Miles Road race, with Handicap in conjunction, from our headquarters at Wimbledon. The team to represent the Club in the Relay race is selected on the form shown here, so all budding aspirants for a place in the team should make a point of turning out on the 28th. For those whose thoughts do not fly so high there is the Handicap to be considered and long marks must be expected from such a Club Champion as Arthur Allum. April 11th is the great day, the London to Brighton Relay race starts from Westminster at 11 a.m., on the first stroke of Big Ben. As usual the Club will have its own Private Bus going down, this being for the team and supporters. Book your seats now. See note elsewhere in this issue. Our team should be a very strong one and we should improve many minutes on our last performance. We come then to the opening day of our Track Season. The first Club meeting will be at Battersea Park Track on Saturday, May 2nd. As last year we shall have an Inter-Club match with the London Athletic Club, a very attractive fixture when one considers the celebrities the L.A.C. can field. Then there will be the usual handicaps for Club members, and kindly note to let me have your entries and fees as early as possible. We have secured the use of Battersea Park Track for a number of evening meetings during the Summer, and will give fuller particulars in the next issue of our Gazette. We shall again be competing in the 1st Division of the Southern Amateur Athletic League, and have also received an invitation to compete in the "Kinnaird Trophy" competition at Stamford Bridge on May 30th. There will also be an Inter-Club competition for Field Events, on much the same lines as last year, when each Club held an event at one of their meetings. Dates of these meetings have yet to be fixed, so of them more anon. All entries and enquiries to E. A. Duffett, Running Hon. Sec., 1 Raymead Avenue, Thornton Heath. items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes: the scratch team's run of eight successive road walking wins and the walkers who took part, a lecture on "Walking" by W. W. Webb on March 23rd, and plans for world record attempts in Battersea Park. Our scratch teams have continued in the victorious vein and have brought the number of successive wins to eight—without doubt a unique feat in the history of road walking. The successes are as follows :— Road Walking Association's Open " 7." Enfield A.C. Open " 7." Highgate H. Open " 7." Belgrave H. Open " 7." Surrey W.C. Godstone and Back Walk (18¾ miles). Cambridge H. Open " 7." L.C.C. Tramways S.A. Open " .7" Ashcombe A.C. Open " 10." * * * * * Len Fletcher and Frank Elson have assisted the Club in seven of these eight wins ; Tommy Green six times ; Fred Rickards on three occasions ; Harold King, Frank Thorn and Ted Saunders each twice ; and Joe King and Jack Field once each. And always behind these have been others to take on the responsibilities and maintain the Club's record should the leaders falter. * * * * * Attention is drawn to the lecture on "Walking" to be given by Mr. W. W. Webb at the London Day Training School, Southampton Row, W.C.1., on March 23rd, at 7 p.m. This is one of the series of lectures arranged by the A.A.A., and admission to a single lecture is free. All walkers are welcome. * * * * * Further to the remarks which appeared in our last issue regarding the possibility of an attempt upon World's records in Battersea Park during the Summer season, we are now able to give the date allotted to us by the London County Council. It is Monday, June 8th, and proceedings will start at 12-30 p.m. and continue until 9 p.m. Further information will appear next month. e: L.C.C. Tramways S.C. Open 7 Miles Walk
items.s: THE OPEN WALKS. Report on three Open walks (Cambridge Harriers 7 miles at Eltham, L.C.C. Tramways S.C. 7 miles and Ashcombe A.C. 10 miles), with results, Len Fletcher winning each; the scratch team placings print "22, Valentines S.C." for second. Since the last "Belgravian" saw the light three Open walks have been held. In the 7 miles event promoted by the Cambridge Harriers, our "A" team easily won the scratch team event, while the "B" team annexed the handicap team first prizes. In addition, Harry Larman, a persevering and improving walker, was placed second in the individual handicap. With Fletcher (1st) beating C. W. Hyde in clear-cut fashion, and Green third, we again took away the bulk of the awards, a pleasing habit we have cultivated in the course of our yearly visits to Eltham. In the L.C.C. Tramways S.C. Open 7 Miles Walk, the judges were more than usually busy, but the fair style of our walkers did not call for disqualifications, and we finished five men in the first seven. Needless to say, we were easy winners of the scratch team event, with the low score of 14 pts., and the "A" team also took second honours in the handicap race. We entered three teams in the Ashcombe A.C. Open 10 Miles Race and supplied the first two men home, three in four, and six in eight! The "A" team took double first honours, with the "C" team third. Although our members were unplaced in the individual handicap, we had fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh places, and six in twelve. Altogether, from our point of view, three most successful "Opens," with three scratch team wins, two handicap team wins, one second and one third; and Len Fletcher heading the field each time! items.sum: Report and results of the R.W.A. Junior Championship 10 miles walk at Luton on March 7th (date as printed in this February issue), won by W. G. Richardson, with Enfield A.C. first team and Belgrave's teams 11th and 22nd.
items.s: THE " JUNIOR." Report and results of the R.W.A. Junior Championship 10 miles walk at Luton on March 7th (date as printed in this February issue), won by W. G. Richardson, with Enfield A.C. first team and Belgrave's teams 11th and 22nd. The eagerly awaited R.W.A. Junior Championship, over a ten miles course at Luton, arrived on March 7th, and although we started out with a quiet feeling of confidence that we should make a fair showing, it must be admitted that we returned to London disappointed. We had hardly expected to win, with five of last year's team no longer eligible, but had hoped that the Club's habit of getting placed in this race year after year would be maintained. However, it was not to be, and we congratulate whole-heartedly Enfield A.C. upon their first win. Two years ago they were third (we were second); last year they finished second to us and on this occasion they stepped up another place. The race was started, with bitterly cold winds blowing, by the Mayor of Luton. Frank Thorn took the lead and was always well-placed, until the six mile mark, where he suffered disqualification. Reg. Elson also came under the judges' ban and with C. W. Redgrave, whose walking has shown great improvement this year, having an off day and eventually dropping out, our chances had gone. This combination of misfortunes allowed the Hon. Secretary, A. A. Harley, to be the first Club man home, filling 31st position. The Arctic weather affected various members of our two teams and when final scores were made out, it was found that our teams had finished 11th and 22nd. Our pangs of disappointment (they were only fleeting, of course, the Belgrave disposition will not allow of anything else !) have now turned to determination to gain the Club's fourth win next year. Our record of three wins has yet to be equalled and we always hope to be one (or more) in front of our nearest rivals ! m. s. 1. W. G. Richardson Woodford Grn. A.C. 79 8 31. A. A. Harley A 84 42 44. items.sum: Article by O. Horwood giving advice on race-walking style and training, citing Len Fletcher as an example; the closing sentence appears to have lost words in printing ("successes and I honours in the future").
items.s: WALKING—TRAINING AND TECHNICAL POINTS. Article by O. Horwood giving advice on race-walking style and training, citing Len Fletcher as an example; the closing sentence appears to have lost words in printing ("successes and I honours in the future"). Race-walking requires many months of slow walking to create perfect style. Style in the most essential thing of all and must be natural to suit each individual. Speed is the last thing to be thought of. Style and fitness create the speed and enable the walker to maintain it throughout a race. All walkers should try to possess that which is so essential—the stride of the legs from the hips—always providing that this is not overdone. When speeding up, the stride should be slightly shortened, and a quicker arm action used. The rear leg should stride out perfectly straight from the toe to the heel, always bearing in mind to keep the feet close together and the shoulders down when swinging the arms. Avoid, above all, any outward turn of the feet. Practice on a chalked or marked line will create a close and even stride, but this can be spoilt by a bad arm action, which is essential to give perfect balance. Slight inward arching of the back gives the hips free play, but stiffening or straining on the legs should be avoided. Let your movements be free and easy, and as natural as possible, and always start slowly when training. A good arm action can easily be practised at home with a towel, by the simple action of drying your back after a bath, keeping the elbows close to the hips, but do not let the hands come up too high, only in line with the chest. Not only is walking natural and healthy, but it creates an upright carriage and does away with those unsightly drooping and round shoulders. No hard and fast rule can be laid down as to when to train. This must be discovered by the individual, who should find out what suits him best, and, of course, as his business hours will permit. Personally, I do not favour night training. In my opinion, it is better to get in a Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning training walk on the road; for, remember, all races take place during the afternoon and not at night. A comfortable stroll, say once or twice a week, is beneficial. For Summer training "little and often" is a good motto and to be preferred to "occasionally and too much." When training, concentrate on what you are doing, and when racing, be determined. Be a good loser or winner and respect the judges should you come under their decision. Walking, at times, may be heartbreaking, for such reasons as disqualifications, or trying to hold on to a competitor who deserves to be ruled out, but is allowed to go on and finish—a very trying experience. On such occasions, overcome your disappointment, and come up smiling for the next race. Some walkers are quicker than others in finding their form and this at times may subject the temperament to a severe test. However, persevere and your training will meet with its due reward. Remember our present champion, Len Fletcher, as an example of one who had a very trying season, but stuck to it, and has now come into his own. We are very proud of our walkers' wonderful successes and I honours in the future ; and as a final word to our younger walkers, assure them that we look to them in the future to take the place of the Seniors and maintain their reputation. O. Horwood O. Horwood Len Fletcher Len Fletcher "our present champion"; had a very trying season but has now come into his own

items.s: THE LIGHTER SIDE OF THE CLUB. Social notes: the social for the Metropolitan Police walkers and Herne Hill runners, a social for Godiva Harriers on March 21st, the last dance, and the Club Annual Dinner on May 2nd at Carr's Restaurant, Victoria. The Social held on the occasion of the visit of the Metropolitan Police walkers, and Herne Hill runners, proved one of the brightest of the season. True we did not have overwhelming numbers, but the Band was the best yet engaged and our "turns" were really first-class. Jack Rathbone with his sax, and Charlie Redgrave and friend with some very witty songs, pleased everybody. Another Social has been arranged for March 21st, when the Godiva Harriers, of Coventry, visit us. It is hoped that everybody will make it a real Belgrave social and give our Midland friends a hearty welcome. Our last Dance of the season did not prove such a financial success as the others, clashes and the "flu" probably being to blame. However, smaller numbers seemed to make for a brighter and more convivial gathering and many present remarked that it was the most enjoyable of the season. Now a word regarding the Club Annual Dinner. This will be held on Saturday, May 2nd, following our first track meeting of the Summer, at Carr's Restaurant, over "The Windsor Castle," Victoria. This is the ideal place for a Club function, for it is accessible from all parts. Trams, buses and trains (both District and Southern) are all within a minute's walk of the door. First-class artistes are being engaged and it only requires a truly representative Belgrave gathering to ensure the best Belgrave dinner yet. Tickets (6/- each) may had upon application to W. A. items.s: Club notes: Arthur Allum's ninth place in the International cross-country championship at Dublin, Belgrave successes at the Gravesend meeting and a call to attend the Annual Club Dinner. In the International cross-country championship decided at Baldoyle Racecourse, Dublin, Arthur Allum finished ninth in the actual race and was the sixth Englishman to score. Thus England scored a very easy win and we are proud to have supplied one of the victorious team. Well run, Arthur ! * * * * * The Summer Season opened very auspiciously for us at Gravesend, where A. Allum won the Two Miles race and our team was second. Other successes were the double win of A. H. Shannon in the sprints, C. Cook's win in the Veteran's 100 yards, E. H. Jarvis's victory in the 440 yards handicap and the third of H. E. Larman in the Walk. If our successes continue at this rate there will be little left for other Clubs. * * * * * It is hoped that all members will make an effort to attend the Annual Club Dinner, particulars of which appear elsewhere. items.label: May 1931
items.sum: Walking notes by the Walking Hon. Secretary: preview of the National Championship at Enfield on May 9th, the Surrey County Championship at Mitcham Common (Fletcher and Thorn disqualified, team third), the Bishop of Birmingham's Cup (Tommy Green first, Belgrave second to Derby W.C.), Green's Sunderland—Darlington record, a planned 50 miles record attempt and walking fixtures.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes by the Walking Hon. Secretary: preview of the National Championship at Enfield on May 9th, the Surrey County Championship at Mitcham Common (Fletcher and Thorn disqualified, team third), the Bishop of Birmingham's Cup (Tommy Green first, Belgrave second to Derby W.C.), Green's Sunderland—Darlington record, a planned 50 miles record attempt and walking fixtures. Our walkers have not been too busy, in the racing sense, during the past month. The shorter distance men are resting prior to resuming on the track, whilst the longer distance walkers are training steadily for the big event of the year—the National Championship—when we hope to regain our title. This Championship will take place on May 9th, at Enfield, and every Club man should make an effort to attend and cheer on our team. A few cheers are wonderfully refreshing in the course of a twenty miles race, and it is hoped that our walkers will have no cause for complaint in this direction. So, turn up in your hundreds, and do a little towards bringing the National Shield back to the South. Enfield Town station is conveniently reached from Liverpool Street station and cheap return fares are available. * * * * * The Surrey County Championship—always an unlucky race for us—again lived up to its reputation when held over Mitcham Common on March 21st. Fletcher, the County champion, and Thorn, both suffered disqualification and this put paid to our hopes of winning the championship for the first time. Field walked well to finish fifth and our eventual team placing was third. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. * * * * * On the same day as the County championships were being held in London, we defended "The Bishop of Birmingham's Cup" over a twenty miles course on the outskirts of Birmingham. Tommy Green won the individual race—incidentally his first win in an Open 20 Miles race—and our four men finished in the first ten places and yet we were only second. Derby W.C., by splendid walking, finished 2, 3, 4, 5, and so took the Cup from us. Birmingham W.C. finished nine men in the first twenty; and these two examples of packing give an idea of what we shall be up against in the National Championship. However, our men will have trained on by May 9th, and a stern struggle may be expected. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. On Easter Monday, Tommy Green broke the record (made by himself last year) for the Sunderland—Darlington course (32¼ miles) by nearly seven minutes. This augurs well for the attempt on the 50 miles record which we are promoting on June 8th, in Battersea Park. Three approved timekeepers have promised their assistance, and I hope to give detailed information in our May issue. * * * * * Attention is drawn to the 2 miles track handicap on Saturday, May 2nd, and at the evening meetings detailed in "Forthcoming Events." Entries (1/-) should be sent to me at least seven days before the event. items.s: THE NATIONAL CROSS-COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIP. Report of the National cross-country championship at Wickstead Park, Kettering, on March 14th: Belgrave ninth of 37 teams and Arthur Allum fifth, earning his England selection; heading misprinted 'CROSS-COUNTY'. On March 14th, our team made its way to Wickstead Park, Kettering, for the cross-country race of the year—the National Championship. Our team hardly hoped to improve upon last year's sixth position, in view of the strength of the entry, and eventually our six totalled fifteen points more than last year, and were placed ninth—a creditable performance in a field of 37 teams comprising the strongest clubs in the country. Our greatest hopes, however, were vested in Arthur Allum's ability to gain a prominent position in the individual race, and our belief in his prowess was fully justified by the result. In the first mile Arthur led, at four miles he was sixth, at seven miles he had dropped back to eighth, and recovered to finish fifth. This wonderful running—the best performance yet by a Belgrave man in this race—deservedly resulted in Arthur being selected to represent England in the International cross-country race in Ireland. Our congratulations and thanks go out to Allum for the honour conferred upon our Champion and his Club. Arthur was the first Southerner to finish, which enhances his feat. Our other men ran well, without calling for particular mention; and we must congratulate our Southern rivals, South London Harriers, upon being placed second, and showing us that it can be done. If our team can show the same improvement by next season as Arthur Allum has shown this year, it will be done. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. 1. J. H. Potts Saltwell H. 57 16 4-5 2. J. Winfield Derby and Cty. items.s: MATCH v. OLD EMANUEL A.C. AND THE COLLEGE OF ST. MARK AND ST. JOHN. Report of the reserve team's five-mile cross-country match at home against Old Emanuel A.C. and the College of St. Mark and St. John combined, won by Belgrave 74 pts. to 104 with Joe Flower first. Whilst our first team were away competing in the National Championship at Kettering, our reserve team entertained Old Emanuel A.C., with whom we had a pleasant fixture last Summer, and the College of St. Mark and St. John. It was intended that this contest should be a three-cornered one, but as our guests turned up short in numbers, they combined to run against us. Our five miles course was used and Joe Flower won from A. Kench, who was running for Old Emanuel A.C., and is, of course, a members of our Club. Another member, W. Lowden, was to be found in the St. Mark's team. George Still ran prominently for a man whose best running was done thirty years ago; and the final scoring gave us a win, as shown below. items.s: FIVE MILES ROAD HANDICAP. Report and result of the club's end-of-season five miles road handicap on March 28th, also a trial for the London to Brighton Relay team: A. W. Penny fastest of 32 finishers, A. H. Traquair first on handicap. The usual end-of-the-season road handicap was held on March 28th and also acted as a trial for selecting the London to Brighton Relay Race team. In the absence of Arthur Allum on International duty in Dublin, Penny and Warboys shared the post of honour. The course was a little over five miles in length and on the re-appearance of the runners, Penny was seen to be leading, followed by Jack Flower. A surprise was caused by the prominent position (5th) occupied by Alfred Kench, one of our younger runners whose promise has been commented upon from time to time in these columns. Another to show up well was C. Mains, a comparative newcomer and Kent County runner, who finished seventh. Mains, who arrived late, was forced to run to St. John's Hall from the station and arrived in a distressed condition. His running under this handicap must be considered satisfactory. Carter again showed that he is a distinct acquisition, and his forward running gained him second prize in the handicap. Alec Traquair upheld the tradition of the "long markers" by taking first prize in the handicap, whilst third prize went to A. Kench. RESULT. Pos'n Name All'ce Actual Time H'cay Time H'cap Pos'n 1. A. items.label: May 1931
items.sum: Report of the London to Brighton Relay on April 11th, in which Belgrave finished fifth behind Birchfield H. after Arthur Allum's ankle gave way on the fourth stage, with Club records for J. E. Flower, T. J. Flower and H. E. Footer, the team's stage result and the full team placings.
items.s: THE BRIGHTON RELAY. Report of the London to Brighton Relay on April 11th, in which Belgrave finished fifth behind Birchfield H. after Arthur Allum's ankle gave way on the fourth stage, with Club records for J. E. Flower, T. J. Flower and H. E. Footer, the team's stage result and the full team placings. April 11th—the day appointed for the London to Brighton Relay—now one of the most popular sporting events in the South—proved to be a very fine day with glorious sunshine; and was in distinct contrast to the weather we have had to endure on some past occasions. Our 'bus arrived at Westminster at 10-15 a.m., and was soon transformed into a combined dressing-room and moving grandstand. Posters in Club colours invoked "Up the Bels." and the claret and gold rosettes, ties and scarves (not forgetting the beret of our Running Hon. Secretary's wife !) gave our 'bus a very colourful appearance. Several bells also made their presence known, and if it had been possible to transform the energy used by the ringers into running power, we should have been in Brighton before the other teams reached Crawley ! Our 'bus left Westminster shortly after 10-30 a.m. and we made for Clapham Common, where Jack Flower, our first man, would hand on to Alfred Kench. Eventually the runners came into sight and it was seen that we had made a very good start, for Jack was lying fourth. He had run very well indeed and was only four seconds outside last year's record for this stretch of 4 miles 176 yards. South London H. led at this point. Kench carried on and quickly found that he was running in the highest class. In fact, his first appearance for the Club in an important race took the form of an "ordeal by fire," but he performed quite creditably. He lost places to men many years his senior and of far greater experience, but none surpassed him for plucky running. And so he arrived at Mitcham, still fighting gallantly and almost "all-in," in the tenth position, but well within striking distance of those in front, now led by Tipton H., due to a fine run by their International, T. Kay. Duffett now ran for us, and for the greater part of the stretch ran neck and neck with an old friend and member of our Club, Harold Wills, of the Herne Hill Harriers. Our man picked up three opponents but had to sacrifice two positions and so handed over ninth. There was still very little in the race, although Birchfield H. had now taken the lead and, as was afterwards proved, were not to be headed again. We were far from dismayed at our position, for our best men were still to run, and those in front of us were spread out at intervals of twenty or thirty yards. This looked like helping Arthur Allum to smash the record for the fourth stage, and to bring us up to second or third position. This he would assuredly have done, but for an unfortunate re-currence of ankle trouble, sustained in the International race in Ireland. He had covered 2½ miles and picked up four positions when his ankle gave way, and from this point it was a case of gritting teeth and struggling on in pain. Two of those he had passed earlier managed to repass Arthur in the last ten yards and so we were now seventh. Arthur had to be carried to the 'bus, for he was unable to put his foot to the ground after finishing the run, and later, Dr. H. B. Stallard prescribed a month's rest. Despite this accident, Allum had accomplished very fast time compared with other runners over the stretch, and but for this unfortunate occurrence we should have been on the heels of the leaders. However, it is all part of the race, and we wish Arthur a speedy recovery and quick return to the form which has made him one of the most talked-of runners during the past season. Sid Warboys carried on for us over the fifth stage, and here most Clubs had placed their best man, but Sid pegged back the Hallamshire and Surrey A.C. men and handed over fifth. We were now led by :— Joe Flower carried on the good work, overhauling the Highgate and Tipton representatives and bringing us up to third position. Joe's run was a very fine one and a Club record for this stage. Behind, R. H. Thomas, the A.A.A. and Air Force Champion, running for Surrey A.C., succeeded in gaining thirteen seconds on us, but Flower's time was the second best over this stage. Bert Footer ran next and although he ran faster than any other Belgrave man has done in the past over this stretch, he was forced to surrender places to Tipton H. and Surrey A.C. Langley, another R.A.F. runner competing for Surrey A.C., ran exceptionally well and took his Club up to third position. Thus, we were fifth when Arthur Penny took over and this remained our position to the end. Penny put up his usual good show and at the conclusion of his run we were only 24 seconds behind South London H., and were over three minutes ahead of Hallamshire H., who were sixth. We were now less than two minutes behind Birchfield H. C. Mains, a young man of twenty, running his first race for us, did very well over what is, perhaps, the most difficult stage of the lot, involving, as it does, the gradual ascent of the South Downs, culminating in the climb of Dale Hill. Only once has a Belgrave man beaten Mains' time over this stage, and that was Footer, last year, when running at his best. Mains is, therefore, deserving of our congratulations upon a fine performance, and has shown that we have another runner of class to strengthen our teams. He gained 19 seconds upon Tipton Harriers and increased our lead over the sixth club to over 3½ minutes. Well run ! C. T. Carter, one of our first-year runners, was entrusted with the last stage, and as the two International runners, E. Harper (Hallamshire H.) and H. Bignall (Highgate H.) were over three and a half minutes behind, there was little to worry about. So we finished fifth, a creditable performance and one which confirms our high position among Southern Clubs. Actually, our time was seventeen seconds slower than last year, but comparisons of time from year to year may be very deceptive, owing to change of conditions, winds, etc. The last stage proved very exciting, for here it was that South London H. beat Surrey A.C. for second place, eventually finishing 33 seconds behind Birchfield H. The race as a whole was most exciting for there were continual changes of position between second and sixth place in the second half of the race and never before has the race been so open. For our part, we derive much satisfaction from the result, for the gap between the winning club and ourselves is gradually decreasing. This year, Surrey A.C. and Tipton H. greatly improved and beat us, while Hallamshire H. on this occasion finished behind us. Next year we may well be fighting out the lead with South London Harriers. Time will show. Some words of praise are due to our reserves, who continued to train conscientiously up to the day of the race in order that they might give of their best if called upon. This is just another little indication of the team spirit which is carrying us forward, and we thank them. After tea, our 'bus started on the return journey, the bell-ringers still busy, and dusk falling. Eventually London and off home, conscious of a good running performance, a fine day's outing, and wondering if next year's race would see our team gaining first medals; and, if so, how many people would be deafened by our bell-ringing "fans" on the homeward journey? Surely questions would be asked in Parliament about it and . . . Well, time will show. RESULT. C.R.—Club Record. items.s: FIELD EVENTS. Notice urging field events men to train for the coming representative matches, dropping the rule that Harry Wright Shield competitors must take part in all four field events, and drawing attention to the Long Jump Handicap on May 2nd. All field events men should now be out training seriously, for representatives will be required for the L.A.C. Match, the "Kinnaird Trophy" Competition, and the various Southern Amateur Athletic League events. J. E. Mackie and G. H. Powell are always pleased to advise newcomers to this branch of athletics. It has been decided that in future it will not be necessary for competitors to take part in all four field events, as hitherto, in the "Harry Wright Shield" Competition. Attention is drawn to the Long Jump Handicap included in our opening programme of May 2nd, and a good entry is anticipated. J. E. Mackie J. E. Mackie pleased to advise newcomers to field events G. H. Powell G. H. Powell pleased to advise newcomers to field events Kinnaird Trophy Southern Amateur Athletic League Harry Wright Shield L.A.C.

items.label: May 1931
items.sum: The Running Hon. Secretary's May 1931 programme: the opening meeting at Battersea Park on May 2nd with an Inter-Club match v. the London Athletic Club, handicaps and a novices' mile, inter-club contests, Southern Amateur Athletic League events, open fixtures, club nights and promising juniors.
items.s: FORTHCOMING EVENTS. The Running Hon. Secretary's May 1931 programme: the opening meeting at Battersea Park on May 2nd with an Inter-Club match v. the London Athletic Club, handicaps and a novices' mile, inter-club contests, Southern Amateur Athletic League events, open fixtures, club nights and promising juniors. We have now arranged our Summer programme and Club fixture cards will be sent to all members as soon as possible. On May 2nd we are holding our opening meeting at Battersea Park Track, at 3 p.m. We have an Inter-Club match v. the London Athletic Club, on the same lines as last year, and the teams to represent our Club in the various events will be selected by the Committee. There will be the following Handicaps for Club members: 100 yards, 300 yards, 880 yards, 2 Miles Walk, and Long Jump. Also we are staging the Southern Amateur Athletic League 3 Miles Team race (4 to run and count) and as this league embraces the pick of the Southern Clubs the race will be an event worth watching. We are also having a 1 Mile scratch run for Novices only, Unattached and also open to Belgrave H. Any Club novices who might wish to enter this event, will they please give their names to me. Also, if you know of any Unattached men who wish to compete kindly ask them to get in touch with me, and oblige. Entries for the above events should be sent in as early as you can, entry fee 1/- each event, no reduction for quantity. May 9th we have an Inter-Club contest v. Ealing Harriers, Slough A.C. and Ashcombe A.C., on the former's ground at West Ealing. Team men will be advised in due course re travelling arrangements, etc. On May 11th will be held the S.A.A.L. High Jump contest at the Surrey A.C., meeting in Battersea Park. Also during May we are holding two further meetings at Battersea Park, one on May 13th, which will be an Inter-Club Relay contest between Croydon H., Mitcham A.C., Epsom H. and ourselves. Club Handicaps for the night are a 220 yards for Juniors under 19 years of age, 2 miles Walk and the Javelin. Then on the 29th we have a Club Handicap night, as follows: 100 yards (under 19), 100 yards (Veterans, over 40), 100 yards, 220 yards, 880 yards, 1 Mile, 2 Miles Walk, and Putting the Shot. There will also be a 100 yards scratch race for Unattached Novices only for "News of the World" medals. Entry to this event is free, so please advise your friends to come along and compete. Entries from Aberdeen are welcomed. May is also a busy month as regards Open Fixtures. On the 16th is the Geneva meeting at Stamford Bridge, which includes a 2 Miles Team race, a 1 Mile Medley Relay, and a 13 Miles Road race, also there are Handicaps at all distances. On the 23rd, also at the Bridge, the S.A.A.L. 4 x 440 yards and 4 x 880 yards contests will be held in connection with the L.A.C. meeting. We are hoping to improve on our last year's position in the League and can only do this by the co-operation of our members in turning out to assist the Club in these races. May 27th there will be held at Finsbury Park Track the S.A.A.L. Long Jump contest in connection with the Highgate H. meeting. In the Southern Amateur Athletic League events points will be scored, 6 for a win down to 1 point for sixth place. This will also apply to the Field events in which 3 men from each club compete with 2 to score, with the exception of the Hurdles race which will be a relay between teams of two. The Field events, however, will form a separate competition, as distinct from the track events. It will be seen from the above that our men will have plenty of competition to keep them busy during this month and all members, young and old, should now be out training at Battersea Park Track. Club nights are Tuesday and Thursday and any new members who are doubtful as to their procedure should get in touch with our Club Captain, W. G. Webb, who is always in attendance at the track on these nights. We have further encouraged our Juniors by putting on an additional handicap event for them, besides which we are again holding the Junior Inter-Club Relay contest v. Croydon H., Epsom H. and Mitcham A.C. It is to the Junior strength of our club that we look for continued success for the "Bels." and judging by members like W. A. Fox, G. H. Pamment, S. Garland and F. H. C. White, to mention just a few, we shall not be disappointed in this respect. All enquiries to E. A. Duffett, Running Hon. Sec., 1 Raymead Avenue, Thornton Heath. W. G. Webb W. G. items.s: Club notes: Tom Scrimshaw's A.A.A. selection against Cambridge University, a long list of spring new members and the promise of some of them, Paul Khlopin's marriage, field-event equipment at Battersea Park and a subscription reminder. We hasten to congratulate Tom Scrimshaw upon the honour accorded to him in being one of the A.A.A. team to compete against Cambridge University. There are many more honours in store for Tom yet, unless we are greatly mistaken. * * * * * The Spring always brings us a big influx of new members and we extend a very hearty welcome to the following: R. W. Farrington, T. Wakem, A. E. Brown, A. T. A. Jordan, W. F. G. L. Goodman, A. D. Purdy, F. A. Arrowsmith, F. J. Green, L. F. Bailey, G. F. A. Attwood, F. Stroud, E. R. Turner, L. Griffiths, C. E. Widdows, A. Gourfinkel, C. J. Hayden, A. E. Holder, J. Hewett, C. C. Redman, E. Sampietro, R. Hayes, F. E. Bentley. * * * * * Some of the above have already been prominent and no doubt the others will be in the limelight in due course. Arrowsmith has represented London University and F. Stroud has shown us that he is a sprinter of more than ordinary promise. Turner is well known as the British Javelin record-holder and was a member of the team to visit Canada last year. Other field-events men of prominence included in the list above are J. Conroy, Essex Shot Putt Champion, and D. D. Ivall, who was placed second in a similar event in the Surrey Championships; Pack has already shown form which justifies us in predicting a "future" for him and another well-built sprinter is Doggett, who should develop considerably. Others to have made their mark are H. Jones, F. Walker and F. E. Bentley, who recently finished third in the Police Barking—Southend Walk. We are glad to welcome all these new friends and wish them a long and happy association with the Club. * * * * * Congratulations to Paul Khlopin upon his marriage. We wish Mr. and Mrs. Khlopin long life and happiness. * * * * * Another reminder: The attention of members is called to the fact that there are available for use at Battersea Park, four javelins, two shots, a discus and a vaulting pole. These are supplied for the use of members only and particular care should be taken in using the javelins. * * * * * And last, but not least, the Hon. Treasurer wishes to again remind all the members who have not yet paid their subscription to do so at once. Eight months of the year have gone and in another four months another 6/- will be due. items.sum: Report on the early-season open meetings: Sid Warboys' record 13½ miles road win at the Geneva S.C. meeting, S.A.A.L. relays, Whit Monday wins including E. R. items.s: ROUND THE OPEN MEETINGS Report on the early-season open meetings: Sid Warboys' record 13½ miles road win at the Geneva S.C. meeting, S.A.A.L. relays, Whit Monday wins including E. R. Turner's javelin and Tom Scrimshaw's 880yds. at the British Games, the Kinnaird Trophy (sixth of nine clubs) with its S.A.A.L. relay and team walk, the Southern Counties steeplechase and the Marathon. The first Open Meeting of any consequence of the season was that promoted by the Geneva S.C. at Stamford Bridge. Sid Warboys delighted us all by the easy way in which he won the 13½ miles road race in record time. To beat men like Slaney, Harry Payne, Gretton and Norris and smile all the while would not appear to be an easy task, but Sid did so as a matter of course, and one day he may well do a performance entitling him to a prominent place in the history of distance running. Another good performance was that of our team in the two miles race, to finish second to Birchfield H., only three points away. With Arthur Allum out (unfortunately he is still nursing a sprained ankle) we should probably have won, and another Cup would be on the Club sideboard! Our team consisted of A. W. Penny (6), who ran a fine race, J. E. Flower (8), and T. J. Flower (14). Scrimshaw ran well in the 600yds. scratch race, but could only manage second place to M. Carr, of the Polytechnic H., and D. E. Jordan was second in the 120yds. Veterans. Two Southern Amateur Athletic League fixtures were included in the L.A.C. meeting on May 23rd, at Stamford Bridge. Rain poured throughout the afternoon and the first fixture in which we had an active interest was the 4 x 440yds. relay. Our team was Titherley, Michael, Jarvis and Tosh, and they were unlucky enough to be drawn on the outside. From the first bend we were behind and remained there until Tosh, running the last "leg," picked up one position and so we finished fifth. In the 4 x 880yds. Fred Ford started for us and handed over third or fourth close behind the leader. Scrimshaw took us into the lead by means of a splendid run. The S.L.H. representative passed our man, Joe Flower, on the next stage and this remained our position to the end, Jim Tosh running last. Thus we gained seven points during the afternoon, which consolidated our position in the League. May 27th. On this evening our representatives, Clemens and Fleming, won the S.A.A.L. Inter-Club Long Jump Competition, and so earned the Club's congratulations. Whit Monday. On this day our members, as usual, were distributed throughout the South and numerous wins were reported. At the British Games, E. R. Turner won the Javelin event with a throw of 167ft. 9½in. and Powell was third, throwing 161ft. 7½in.; Tom Scrimshaw was successful in the scratch 880yds. race in 2min. 0 4-5sec. In the Special Four Miles Handicap framed to help Paavo Nurmi in his attempt upon the record, Arthur Penny finished third, never being caught by the "Flying Finn." Our 6 x 440yds. team was fourth and our Junior 4 x 110yds. team occupied the same position. At Woking, S. T. Ring won the Walk, and G. Basford was second in the 100yds. at Luton. At Reading, Norman Dewberry and A. H. Shannon won the mile and 220yds. respectively, and Jack Flower was second in the Steeplechase handicap; F. Stroud won the 300yds. and was second in the 100yds. at Ilford, a creditable performance. On the following day, J. E. Read won the 220yds. at Wolverton, much to the delight of the other "Bels" assembled there. May 30th. We received our usual invitation to participate in "The Kinnaird Trophy Competition," confined to the nine strongest Clubs in the country, and our men acquitted themselves creditably. T. Scrimshaw ran like a seasoned veteran in the final of the 880yds. race, but found T. Hampson a little to strong for him in the last few yards. Our man's running gave the crowd a great thrill, for it gripped the imagination to see a young runner not yet 21 giving Hampson a keen tussle and making men like Gutteridge and Ellis look like "selling-platers." Our other man to do well was Clemens, who finished third in the Long Jump with a leap of 20ft. 11¾in. These two excellent performances by two of our younger members, scored five points in the Competition for us, and enabled us to finish sixth of the nine competing clubs. This is most creditable in a competition in which only men of the very highest class can hope to score. The 4 x 220yds. S.A.A.L. fixture was included at this meeting and we did well to finish third to South London H. and the Polytechnic H., with Ilford A.C., Highgate H. and Surrey A.C. behind us. Jarvis led for us, passing on to Read. Then McKay, finishing with Odell, and this quartet are to be congratulated. Read has certainly strengthened our team. The programme also included a 2 miles Team Walk to which we received an invitation, together with Woodford Green A.C., Enfield A.C., Highgate H., Surrey A.C. and the promoting club, Polytechnic H., Hyde, of Enfield, won, followed by Cooper and Pope, of Woodford Green, and Fletcher, of our Club. With three to score, Woodford took team honours. Enfield were second and our team (Fletcher, F. Elson, Scamell) third. Jack Flower finished second to Binfield, of Slough A.C., in the Southern Counties 2 miles Steeplechase Championship. G. F. Easton was our only representative in the Marathon and he did well to finish 16th in 3hrs. 8min. 41sec., beating Standard time. On the same day at the Crystal Palace, T. N. Wilcock was second in the 300yds. and F. Arrowsmith second in the 880yds. items.sum: Report of the Club 20 Mile walking championship at Wimbledon on April 19th, won by Tommy Green from Joe King and H. F. King, with A. H. Field winning the handicap.
items.s: THE 20 MILES CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP. Report of the Club 20 Mile walking championship at Wimbledon on April 19th, won by Tommy Green from Joe King and H. F. King, with A. H. Field winning the handicap. In spite of the sun's brilliant effort to provide us with a fine afternoon, the conditions were rather trying for the 15 walkers who faced the starter in the race for the Club 20 Mile Championship at Wimbledon on April 19th. The sun shone brilliantly for the early part of the race but later a cold wind, together with rain, made us wonder whether we were not getting too much of a good thing—March winds and April showers. Tommy Green went to the front at the start and at the end of the first mile led by a yard or two from Harold and Joe King, walking together, with Jack Field 80yds. behind. By the time the "Green Man" was reached, Green had increased his lead to 25yds., whilst Field had dropped further behind. On coming back past the Memorial (8 miles) H. F. King with an effort caught Tommy, but would probably have been wiser to have saved himself until the second time round. The course was then over the single circuit of our "Open," bringing in the drop down Combe Hill and the stiff pull up Pepy's Road. It was here that Green drew away from Harold King and he led by 150yds. at the "Green Man" (13 miles): Joe followed 50yds. behind. Hillier, who was walking with Knifton in 7th position, appeared to be walking very strongly at this point and seemed certain to win the handicap if he could last. Saunders retired at 17 miles when walking strongly, owing to blisters which he had no desire to irritate in view of the National Championship three weeks later. Tommy Green eventually broke the tape 2mins. 34 sec. ahead of Joe King, who had passed Harold having a bad time at 15 miles. Jack Field walked splendidly over the last 4 miles and only failed by 100yds. to beat H. F. King for third place. Jack Rathbone gave a good account of himself by finishing fifth, whilst Elson and Knifton, both of whom started very steadily, finished full of walking. The Handicap resulted in a well-deserved win for A. H. Field; Joe King was second and our old stager (?), Charlie Speechley, third. RESULT. The course was about half a mile short. C.W.R. Posn. items.label: June 1931
items.sum: Report and results of the R.W.A. National Championship walk at Enfield on May 9th, which Belgrave contested without the injured Tommy Green, finishing seventh (A) and twelfth (B) while Derby W.C. took team honours.
items.s: THE R.W.A. NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP. Report and results of the R.W.A. National Championship walk at Enfield on May 9th, which Belgrave contested without the injured Tommy Green, finishing seventh (A) and twelfth (B) while Derby W.C. took team honours. About ten days before this Championship was to be decided we received a setback from which we never seemed to recover. News came from Eastleigh that our Champion, Tommy Green, from whom we were expecting a really fine performance, had had the misfortune to lose a thumb in the course of his work. He was immediately taken to hospital and given the best of attention, but the nature of the injury and the shock sustained had robbed us of Tommy's services for the National Championship. We extend our sympathy to Tommy, and are glad to say that he is making good progress, and that in a month or so he hopes to be as well as ever. May 9th arrived and we assembled at Enfield for the most important race of the year. Tommy Green was present as a spectator and despite our undoubted handicap we appeared to have a very strong team, capable of maintaining the tradition the Club has built up in this particular race. This view was upheld by the positions at eight and a half miles. Here Derby were prominent but we had Joe and Harold King in sixth and seventh positions, Field 12th, and several of our men walking easily in the thirties. At fifteen miles, although we were not doing nearly as well as we should have liked, our chances of a place were still quite good. It was obvious by this time that nothing less than a miracle could rob Derby of team honours. Our positions were now: H. F. King, 17, J. F. King 18, J. Rathbone 32, J. E. Field 34, E. Saunders 36. It was in the last five miles that our position weakened, all these men losing places, with the exception of E. Saunders. Joe King was attacked by cramp, causing him to lose many places, and Rathbone also had to stop. Saunders from being our fifth man at 15 miles became our second man to finish and accomplished his best performance over twenty miles. Harold King struggled on pluckily during the closing stages and becomes the holder of the "S. Bayliss" Cup awarded to the first Club man to finish. Thus our four scoring men finished 24, 34, 35 and 45, giving us seventh position. If this result is disappointing, we obtain a certain measure of satisfaction at the form shown by our second team men. Our "B" team was placed 12th of the 25 competing teams, which must be considered a very creditable performance. Hillier and Field (A.H.) showed very promising form in their first National Championship. Derby W. Club's excellent performance of placing their men 5, 6, 7 and 13 is deserving of the highest praise and we congratulate them upon winning the Championship for the first time. Next year we must make a spirited effort to regain our lost honours, and the Championship for the South. It will not be an easy task, but I am confident that we have the men capable of doing it. When May, 1932, comes round, we should have Tommy Green, fit and well; Fred Rickards, who was sorely missed this year, but expects to be out again next Winter; and our other men showing their real form. In addition, we shall probably have the assistance of F. E. Bentley, who finished third in the recent Police Barking to Southend Walk—a performance of high merit—and has since become a member of our Club. Also, our younger members may be expected to strengthen the teams, and so the future looks quite bright. In fact, one year ahead you may well be reading of a Belgrave victory in place of this year's reverse! We have every confidence in the swing of pendulum, and in the knowledge that you can't keep so many undoubtedly good men down all the time. And so we must leave it till May, 1932. RESULTS. H. F. items.label: June 1931
items.sum: Review of Capt. F. A. M. Webster's book of action photographs, "Athletes in Action".
items.s: REVIEW. Review of Capt. F. A. M. Webster's book of action photographs, "Athletes in Action". Capt. F. A. M. Webster, the well-known athletic coach, has sent us a copy of his latest book, "Athletes in Action," for review and we can confidently recommend it to our runners and field events men as being certain to effect improvements in their form, if the instructions and advice contained in the book are carried out. As the title suggests, the book consists of hundreds of action photographs illustrating the various stages of sprinting, distance running, hurdling and the field events. Thus, for example, there are 28 photographs illustrating sprinting from the "On the Mark" position to striding, and on the opposite page to the photograph appears the text matter emphasising the particular points to be studied. This particularly happy method has been adopted throughout the book, and among the celebrated athletes who are so photographed are A. Jonath, one of Germany's fastest sprinters; Guy Butler (440yds.); D. G. A. Lowe (880yds.); P. Nurmi (Distance); H .Trossbach, the German Record-holder for the Hurdles; J. Simpson (440yds. Hurdles); C. Hoff, Norwegian and ex-World's Pole Vault Champion; Dr. Honner (Long Jump); E. Hirschfield, the World's Shot Putt Record-holder; B. Szepes, Hungarian Javelin Champion; and many others. It is the author's intention that the book should be taken on the track by the athlete and then, either by himself or with the assistance of a friend, the methods exemplified in the action photographs imitated. In this way, correct style is inculcated and improvement assured. To conclude, the athlete is bound to find much of interest in this well-written book and the majority would surprise themselves if the principles laid down by Capt. Webster were followed out in full. "Athletes in Action" is published by John F. Shaw (1928) & Co., Ltd., 3 Pilgrim Street, E.C., and is priced at 6/-. Capt. F. A. M. Webster Capt. F. A. M. items.h: INTER-CLUB MATCH AT EALING ON MAY 9th.
items.sum: Report and results of a four-club match with Ealing, Slough and Ashcombe at Drayton Green Track, Ealing, won by Belgrave.
items.s: INTER-CLUB MATCH AT EALING ON MAY 9th. Report and results of a four-club match with Ealing, Slough and Ashcombe at Drayton Green Track, Ealing, won by Belgrave. A very interesting four-cornered contest was held at Drayton Green Track, Ealing, on Saturday, May 9th. The competing clubs were: Ealing H., Belgrave H., Slough H. and Ashcombe A.C. Points were scored in each event and the "Bels" emerged good winners after a capital afternoon's sport. W. L. Vincent won both sprints for the home club, with Jock McKay running him close on each occasion. J. C. Robbins, the S.L.H. runner, won the Mile for Slough H. in fine style, with Joe Flower and Norman Dewberry scoring for us. Somebody said our mile Champion started in this race, but at all events he was missing at the finish, so we make this statement with reserve. Slough also secured first place in the 880yds., S. E. Binfield showing a clean pair of heels to the other competitors. In the 3 Miles Team our four men finished 1, 3, 5, 7, and with three to score we thus had an easy win in the team race. Arthur Penny had a fine fight with Cohen, of Ashcombe, while Vic Harman, of Slough, found the pace a little too hot for him. Bert Footer ran his usual dogged race, while our Captain, Bill Webb, just strode round enjoying the beauty of this pleasantly-situated track. For the last event, the 1 mile Medley Relay, we had to field a more or less experimental team, owing to the fact of all our men having already raced in one or more events. The team, however, all ran splendidly and we won in fine style, with Slough H. second. It was a fixture which all our boys enjoyed very much and we look forward to next year's meeting. items.h: MATCH v. THE LONDON ATHLETIC CLUB ON MAY 2nd.
items.sum: Report and results of the opening match against the London Athletic Club at Battersea Park Track on May 2nd (a 30-all tie), with the S.A.A.L. 3 Miles Team Race and Club handicap events held at the same meeting.
items.s: MATCH v. THE LONDON ATHLETIC CLUB ON MAY 2nd. Report and results of the opening match against the London Athletic Club at Battersea Park Track on May 2nd (a 30-all tie), with the S.A.A.L. 3 Miles Team Race and Club handicap events held at the same meeting. Our opening meeting at Battersea Park Track on May 2nd was blessed with fine weather and a huge crowd enjoyed the fine racing between the London Athletic Club and our own Club. Scoring points, 4, 3, 2, 1, for each event; the result of the match was a tie, 30 all. As usual, the L.A.C. won the 100yds., although this time we did manage to gain third and fourth places. Tommy Scrimshaw gained a fine victory for us in the 880 yds. match after a good tussle with Firebrace, the Cambridge runner, while our other men came along and filled the minor placings. In the 1 Mile, Jack Flower scored an easy win, although Frank Tame on his first team appearance for the Club did well to finish third. The Long Jump saw us gain the first two places through the agency of Clemens and Fleming, although Basford in winning the club Long Jump Handicap did so well that it was a pity he did not count in the match event. The L.A.C. turned out a very hot trio in the 440yds. and Jim Tosh just managed to split their last two men. Simpson, a big strong runner, forced the pace throughout and successfully resisted a challenge from Tommy Hampson, the A.A.A. half-mile Champion. In the 2 Miles Team Race we had to have the individual winner in order to secure the match honours, as at this stage we were leading by two points. Despite a good effort on the part of C. T. Carter, Mellish, of the L.A.C., finished first, with another clubmate third, and so they scored 5 points to our 3, thus making the totals level. Much to our disappointment the Javelin event had to be cancelled owing to the inability of the L.A.C. to field a team. With E. R. Turner and George Powell throwing for us, we can safely say the honours here would have been ours. Nevertheless, it was a fine sporting match, enjoyed by all, and our boys are to be congratulated on holding our visitors to a draw. Also at this meeting was held the Southern Amateur Athletic League 3 Miles Team Race, and a very classy field was seen out for this race. Tomlin, of Highgate, won in quite good time for so early in the season, while Penny, of our own Club, ran well to finish 5th. Our team was not at full strength owing to the necessity of fielding strong teams for the match events and so did well to finish fourth in the team race. The Club handicaps found the Handicapper out of form, and we saw a runaway win in the 100yds. H. Morgan, who was second in this race, completed a place double by again being second in the 300yds., which was won by a promising newcomer in F. Stroud. In the 2 Miles Walk one of our younger members, H. Latter, finished a good winner, with H. E. Larman and A. A. Harley, our Walking Hon. Sec., next to him. The Club 880yds. Handicap resulted in a win for Frank Tame in fast time with Tom Cotton, who ran a dogged race, second, and R. W. Martin third. For the 1 Mile Scratch Novice race a good field was seen out and another member of the Penny family showed great promise in being placed second to F. A. Sandell, who is also sure to improve with experience. RESULTS. MATCH EVENTS. 100 Yards.—L. F. Wright, L.A.C., 1; J. Simpson, L.A.C., 2; T. N. Wilcock, B.H., 3; E. H. items.h: INTER-CLUB RELAY MEETING AT BATTERSEA PARK TRACK.
items.sum: Report of the first Inter-Club Relay meeting at Battersea Park Track on May 13th, with a Club 220yds. Juniors handicap and a Javelin handicap.
items.s: INTER-CLUB RELAY MEETING AT BATTERSEA PARK TRACK. Report of the first Inter-Club Relay meeting at Battersea Park Track on May 13th, with a Club 220yds. Juniors handicap and a Javelin handicap. On May 13th we held the first of the Inter-Club Relay meetings at Battersea Park Track. In the first event, the 4 x 100yds., Croydon Harriers scored a good win, with ourselves second and Mitcham third. I must say that the method of running this race, by touch on the shoulder, is very unsatisfactory, and a 4 x 110yds. round the track would be much preferable and give everyone satisfaction. The 4 x 880yds. provided us with an easy win, although Evans of Mitcham ran a fine leg for his team. For the 4 x 300yds. we were in a quandary as Jim Tosh was unable to run owing to sickness and so we brought in Stroud, who had already raced twice on that evening. He, however, ran a strong race and well backed up by Jarvis and Titherley, enabled our last man, J. E. Read, to get away level with the Croydon runner. Read put in a fine finish and so won us yet another event. In the Mile Team race our men finished 1, 2, 4, 5, with Jack Flower shewing the way home, and so we only dropped one point on the evening's racing. It is to be hoped our men support the away fixtures in this competition as well as they did this one and so ensure the Club retaining possession of the Shield. There was only one Club running Handicap on this evening, a 220yds. for Juniors under 19, and in this event we saw some promising material. L. L. Hyde, the winner, is a newcomer, while F. Stroud continued his successes by being second with another newcomer in A. A. Doggett, third. E. H. Pack, the scratch man, qualified for the final and was only inches outside the placed men. In fact, on this showing, our Junior sprinters will soon be forcing their way into our Senior teams, and that at a very early date. In the Javelin Throw handicap, Turner, the scratch man was unable to compete and B. W. Fleming was successful in winning on handicap with Noble second, and our Field Events Vice-Captain, George Powell, third. The Walk provided Harley with his initial "first," although he has been placed second and third on several occasions in the past. Jackman gained his first prize and should develop into a class walker, with perseverance, whilst Larman's continued gradual improvement gained for him third position. items.s: EVENING MEETING—MAY 20th. Report and results of the Club's evening meeting of eight handicaps on May 20th (the report gives J. Conroy's putt as 39ft. 8in.; the handicap results, where he owed 1ft., give 38ft. 8in.). At our evening meeting on May 20th, eight Club handicaps were held, and a noticeable feature was the double successes of three members, G. Basford, B. W. Hayman and A. W. Penny. Basford filled first position in both the 100yds. and 220yds. handicaps; Hayman was second in the Shot Putt and second in the 100yds.; whilst Penny's successes were first in the "half" and third in the mile. A popular win was that of Charlie Cook, who ran away with the Veteran's 100yds. handicap off 15yds. And this at the age of 68! The final of the 100yds. (under 19) was contested by six very promising juniors, all of whom seem likely to make their mark. The scratch man, E. H. Pack, was narrowly beaten in this heat, but one cannot be far wrong in prophesying for him high honours in the future. The Shot Putt was won by J. Conroy (owe 1ft.), the Essex Champion, who putt 39ft. 8in. The Walk was won by S. T. Ring, who is another one of our younger walkers showing great improvement, but the race was chiefly noticeable for the excellence of the handicapping. Although there was a fair gap between first and second men, practically all those who finished the course were in the straight at the conclusion. Larman managed to beat Jackman for second place, so reversing their positions of the previous Wednesday. Len Fletcher finished fourth from the scratch mark, having covered the two miles in 14min. 25sec. and showed excellent form. After him came the rest of the field close together, providing an excellent race. The Mile went to a newcomer, F. Walker, with the Penny brothers second and third. items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes: sympathy for Tommy Green after his accident, county 2 miles titles for A. L. Fletcher and J. F. King, W. J. Titt of Portsmouth, a novice walk, new walkers and forthcoming walking events. We must commence these paragraphs with an expression of sympathy to Tommy Green upon his accident. Not only did it rob him of an excellent chance of winning the National 20 miles Championship, and retaining his 50 kilometres title, but the attempt upon the 50 miles and intermediate records had to be abandoned. However, Tommy is now entering races again and we hope he will soon be back in record-breaking form. Congratulations to A. L. Fletcher and J. F. King upon winning the 2 miles Championships of Surrey and Sussex respectively. Joe King is also County Champion at 10 and 20 miles and was also first Sussex man to finish in the Hastings—Brighton Walk (38 miles), and must be acclaimed as a very versatile walker. He hopes to atone for his somewhat disappointing National Walk by being well placed in the London—Brighton in September. Another man who, like Joe King and Tommy Green, is always bringing the Belgrave name before the provincial sporting public, is W. J. Titt. He resides at Portsmouth, and his name is often in the prize winners in South-Western England. He should be of assistance to our "Junior" team next Winter, now that he is qualified to represent us in team races. * * * * * Attention is drawn to our One Mile Novice Walk included in our programme for June 24th. This race is open to Belgrave and unattached novices and I should appreciate early entries (Fee 1/-). So, if you have any novice friends, tell them to send their entries in at once. * * * * * Walkers to join us recently are: L. F. Bailey, J. F. Dempsey, W. F. A. Newby, H. Sloan, J. H. Martin and F. E. Bentley. * * * * * Future events include Club 2 mile Handicaps on June 24th and July 9th; the latter being on Richmond Athletic Club ground and is held in conjunction with Ashcombe A.C. and Thames Valley H. * * * * * In addition, there will be a team walk over two miles (6 to start, 3 to score) at the Ravensbourne Club Meeting at New Eltham on June 27th. The following week-end the A.A.A. Championships take place, when we hope our representatives will do well. items.sum: Forthcoming fixtures from the Hon. Running Secretary: a warning that late entries will not be accepted, then the June and July club, inter-club, Doris Shield and championship meetings.
items.s: FORTHCOMING FIXTURES. Forthcoming fixtures from the Hon. Running Secretary: a warning that late entries will not be accepted, then the June and July club, inter-club, Doris Shield and championship meetings. Before commencing on the forthcoming fixtures, I should like to draw members' attention to the question of entering Club events. It states on our fixture cards that entries close 7 days prior to the event. This has, I am afraid, been sadly overlooked in the past and I have received entries as late as the day before the race. In future I shall not be at Battersea Park on Sunday mornings, so members who have been in the habit of leaving it till then will now be too late. What I would like members to realize is that not only does it give the Handicapper no chance of compiling his handicaps in an orderly manner (with these last-minute entries he naturally has to rush them through), also it is not fair to our groundsman, who has to wait for the marks before he can do anything. Then there is the printer to be considered, so that you can see it is a question of many people being involved. Therefore, will all members please note that in future NO LATE ENTRIES WILL BE ACCEPTED and that entries must be sent to me AT LEAST 7 DAYS BEFORE THE MEETING. Just a postcard will do; you can pay me the fee on the day, although, of course, I would prefer the money with the entry. We now come to the first of our track Championships, namely, the 3 Miles for the "Griffin" Cup, holder Arthur Allum. This will be held at our meeting in Battersea Park on June 24th, and there will also be the following Club Handicaps: 100yds. (under 16), 150yds. (Vets. 40), 100yds., 880yds., High Jump and 2 Miles Walk. I might mention that in connection with the 3 Miles Race, Club Standard medals will be awarded to those who attain the following times: 1st class, 16min.; 2nd class, 16min. 30sec. In addition, we are staging the S.A.A.L. Javelin Throw contest, while for Novice Walkers, either Unattached or Belgrave H., we have a 1 Mile Scratch Walk. Entry fee for all these events is 1/- each event, and entries should be sent to me at once. June 27th, the Club will be supporting the Ravensbourne Club meeting at Eltham, where a series of team races at varying distances will be held. Entries for these events are made by the Committee. On July 1st we have the third Inter-Club Relay meeting between Mitcham A.C., Croydon H., Epsom H., and ourselves at the "News of the World" Track, Mitcham. The meeting will commence at 7 p.m. and anyone who cares to go along will witness a good evening's sport. On July 3rd and 4th the A.A.A. Championships will be held at Stamford Bridge. We are hopeful of having a few Club members representing us in the Championships and while we do not expect any winners we are sure our boys will bring credit to our colours. I strongly advise all our younger members and others to indulge in a "bob's" worth and see some really fine running at this meeting. It will leave a lasting impression on their minds and will do them the world of good in encouraging them to persevere with their athletics. At Battersea Park on July 8th we have a Junior (under 19) Inter-Club Relay contest versus Croydon H., Mitcham A.C. and Epsom H. The events will be: 3 x 100yds., 3 x 200yds., 880yds. Team race (4 to run, 3 to score), and with the promising Juniors at present in our colours, we should turn out some very strong teams in these events. Handicaps open to all Club members will be held at: 300yds., 880yds. and Long Jump. I may say that the latter has been put on owing to many requests from members for an additional Jumping event and I hope the entries will justify its inclusion. Kindly note that entries will close on July 1st, and send yours along in good time. The following evening, July 9th, we have the Doris Shield competition between Ashcombe A.C., Thames Valley H. and ourselves, which will be held at Richmond on the Rugby Club's ground. In addition to the Shield events, entries for which are made by our Committee, there will be the following Handicaps open to members of the three competing clubs: 100yds., 1 Mile run, 2 Miles Walk. It is to be hoped our members will support these Handicaps; good prizes are given and we are naturally keen that our members will swamp the other clubs. Entry fee, 1/- each event, should be sent along with your entry form and please let me have them early, as a Joint Handicap Committee has to meet in order to arrange the marks. On July 15th we have the final Inter-Club Relay Competition contest, to be held at Wandle Park, Croydon. In addition to the usual Inter-Club events, there will be staged at this meeting several A.A.A. Open Handicaps. The first Open will be at 6 p.m. and here is an opportunity for our members to have a go at a "quiet one." On this same evening, at Battersea Park, the S.A.A.L. 2 x 120 yds. Hurdles race will be held, and I trust our two representatives will garner in some more points for us. In the Southern Amateur Athletic League, 1st Division, we are well placed at present and so far the relegation bogey has not troubled us. We are indebted to the members who have so worthily represented the Club in these events and are sure that in the remaining few we shall again give our opponents a strong tussle for supremacy. items.h: THE LIGHTER SIDE OF THE CLUB.
items.sum: Account of the club's Annual Dinner after the match against the L.A.C., with its guests, speeches, music and a presentation to W. H. Hare on his marriage.
items.s: THE LIGHTER SIDE OF THE CLUB. Account of the club's Annual Dinner after the match against the L.A.C., with its guests, speeches, music and a presentation to W. H. Hare on his marriage. This year's Annual Dinner, following on our match v. L.A.C. in the afternoon, appealed to many as the best yet held. We had a record attendance, well over a hundred being present, and found the venue to be well suited for the Club's most important social function. Our chief guest was, of course, Mrs. Ricketts, whose husband did so much for our Club a few years back and sowed the seed from which we are now reaping the benefit. Included among the guests were: Mr. J. Binks, Mr. and Mrs. W. J. Pepper, Mr. and Mrs. H. W. Brockhouse, Mr. F. T. Summerfield, Mr. F. W. Blackmore, Mr. and Mrs. W. C. Jewell, and representatives of Mitcham A.C., Epsom A.C. and Croydon H. We were very pleased to see so many ladies present; and happy to have with us three Past-Presidents of the Club in Mr. A. W. Macher, Mr. R. Murphy and Mr. W. H. Hare. The lay-out of the menu card, depicting several of the giants of the Club, created great interest, and whether it will inspire our members to an onslaught upon the County titles remains to be seen! Speeches, as usual, and justifiably so, were on the optimistic side, and judging from the remarks passed, other Clubs are in for a very poor time! After the leader which Arthur Allum has given our men this year, we may well justify all that was said. The musical programme was most enjoyable. The topical songs sung by Charlie Redgrave and friend ("Bros. Gay") were deservedly encored, and the musical quartet, which included our President's daughters, also pleased the gathering. An interesting event was the presentation made to Mr. W. H. Hare, to mark the Club's esteem, upon the occasion of his recent marriage. In response to the ovation accorded to his wife and himself, Harry made an humorous little speech which caused general merriment among the married folk, but I understand his wife has since forgiven him! At last came "Auld Lang Syne," and closed one of the most memorable Club nights. Mrs. Ricketts Mrs. Ricketts chief guest at the Annual Dinner; her husband did much for the Club a few years back J. items.sum: Notice of the club's annual summer outing to Earlswood Common on Sunday, July 5th.
items.s: SUMMER OUTING. Notice of the club's annual summer outing to Earlswood Common on Sunday, July 5th. Now, I should like to know that a measure of support for our Annual "go-as-you-please" Outing will be forthcoming. It has been arranged for Sunday, July 5th, and it is thought that we cannot improve upon Earlswood Common as a venue. Here we have plenty of grassland, where all sorts of games can be indulged in, a swimming pool, and a near-by hostelry where an excellent tea is obtainable at a reasonable charge. And (base thought!) we have somewhere to go should the Clerk of the Weather prove unkind. So make a note of the date and the place, July 5th, Earlswood Common, and let's have a record crowd. Your friends are welcome and will enjoy a day out in the open with the "Bels." Those who intend going should advise me as to the size of their party in order that I may make the necessary arrangements for tea-time (bring your own lunch). Further particulars may be had from W. A. RICE, 36 Ascalon Street, S.W.18. W. A. Rice W. A. RICE organiser of the Summer Outing; address in the issue W. A. RICE Summer Outing Earlswood Common
