items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Club notes: Tommy Scrimshaw's England selection, Fred Rickards' Guildford Cup win, Olympic 50 km walk hopes, the Surrey County Relay title, J. W. Clemens' long jumping, A. L. Fletcher's A.A.A. walk, S. L. King's marriage and the month's new members.
items.s: Club notes: Tommy Scrimshaw's England selection, Fred Rickards' Guildford Cup win, Olympic 50 km walk hopes, the Surrey County Relay title, J. W. Clemens' long jumping, A. L. Fletcher's A.A.A. walk, S. L. King's marriage and the month's new members. Our very heartiest congratulations are accorded to Tommy Scrimshaw upon his very fine showing in the A.A.A. Championpionships and consequent selection to represent England v. France in Paris on August 2nd. He is the latest addition to our growing list of "Internationals" and as he is not yet twenty-one, should continue to appear in similar contests for many years to come. We wish him the best of luck in his first International race and trust that next year there will be other "Bels." in the English team with him. * * * * * Congratulations also to Fred Rickards upon his very fine win in the "Guildford Cup" race, decided over a fifty kilometres (30¼ miles) course, embracing several stiff climbs. His time was wonderfully good and a reproduction of this form next season should ensure for him a place in the Olympic team visiting Los Angeles next summer. * * * * * It is understood that each country will be allowed three representatives in the 50 kilometres Walk included in the Olympic Games programme for the first time next year. With Fred Rickards and Tommy Green bearing English colours (as seems very probable) England can be sure of being worthily represented and, of course, there still remains the third place! We can also fill this vacancy from our ranks, if needs be, and the coming season's racing will be followed with an added interest and in the hope that we provide England's three Olympic walkers! * * * * * At long last we have managed to win the Surrey County Relay Championship and for this we have to thank T. Hampson, T. N. Wilcock, J. E. Read and E. H. Jarvis. Tommy Hampson, running as befits an A.A.A. champion, gained a twenty yards lead for us over the first stage of half a mile; and this was nearly doubled by Read and Wilcock (220 yards each) and Jarvis, running the final quarter-mile. Well done! We hope to retain this championship for many years. * * * * * J. W. Clemens, by winning the Southern Counties Long Jump Championship, and being one of the final six in the A.A.A. Long Jump Championship (with only one other Englishman to keep him company, the remaining four coming from abroad) has proved himself to be in the front rank of England's jumpers, and he should achieve representative honours before long. Well done, Clemens, and may you find two feet (in the jump, of course) during the winter! * * * * * Another Belgrave man to do well in the A.A.A. Championships was A. L. Fletcher, who finished fourth in the Seven Miles Walk. The race was won by Frigerio, of Italy, with Danlisch, a Latvian, second. This places Len as the second-best Englishman in the race—a very fine performance meriting our congratulations. * * * * * Our heartiest congratulations are extended to S. L. King, who was recently married to Miss Redgrave. Syd has served the Club well as runner, walker (not at the same time, of course!), Walking Hon. Secretary and Committee man during his many years with the Club, and we wish Mr. and Mrs. King a very happy married life. Business has taken Syd some way out of London, but we can be sure that his wife's and his own good wishes will follow the Club, and that we shall see them from time to time. * * * * * We cordially welcome the following new members this month: F. A. P. Horton, C. J. Kelly, L. E. Alp, S. Huggins, W. J. Roberts, J. A. Grimwade, A. M. Dyke, R. L. Bowles, G. W. McCarthy, C. F. Armstrong, G. Leviten, D. Martin, A. F. Mitchell, H. W. F. Harris, H. H. Rumsey, E. Pointer, A. H. M. Kew, W. J. French, C. H. James, and one omitted from last month's list, A. Deacon. A long and happy career with the Club is our sincere wish to the above named. * * * * * Of the above, C. J. Kelly has already proved himself a capable long-jumper by winning our recent handicap; G. W. McCarthy is a brother of T. McCarthy, who is serving the Club well by looking after our interests in South East London. J. A. Grimwade (introduced to the Club by old friends in A. L. Spendlove and E. L. Reeve) is a young walker of considerable promise; and we may be sure that among our new recruits this month there are several others with talent which will soon be revealing itself. items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's Sixth Annual Inter-Club Walking Contest at Battersea Park on June 15th, won by Belgrave Harriers by 11 points from the Surrey Walking Club.
items.s: INTER-CLUB WALKS. Report and results of Belgrave's Sixth Annual Inter-Club Walking Contest at Battersea Park on June 15th, won by Belgrave Harriers by 11 points from the Surrey Walking Club. We were favoured with fine weather on the evening of June 15th, when eight clubs sent teams to Battersea Park to compete in our Sixth Annual Inter-Club Walking Contest. The rules governing this sporting event are so well known to all members and, indeed, to all Metropolitan walkers, that there is no need to re-state them in the "Belgravian." The splendid quality of the teams that accept our invitation each year and the keenness with which the issue is invariably fought out, tell convincingly that the rules governing this event are widely known and appreciated to a remarkable degree. Counting team men and reserves, one hundred or more athletes attend this meeting year after year, full of enthusiasm and bringing a following of supporters. There are no cups or medals to be won, yet they give us of their very best; and there is no other track fixture in the country possessing the power of luring out such a muster of walkers. The programme opened with the 5 miles race, and here A. A. Webb, of the Polytechnic Harriers, enhanced his brilliant record in this race by his customary display of fast and faultless walking. This year he was faster than ever, whilst his style and body-poise left nothing to be desired. He has now made five consecutive appearances in this race. He won in 1926, 1928 and this year, and finished 2nd to C. W. Hyde, the A.A.A. dual ex-champion in 1929 and 1930. Although the time recorded this year is 59 seconds slower than Hyde's of last year, yet it is the second fastest of the whole series and beats his own previous best by 63 seconds. Webb is a great favourite with the Battersea Park walking fans and each year they show their appreciation in no uncertain fashion. He was well backed up by R. C. Holdaway, and for a long while it appeared that the Poly. pair would beat the field. Holdaway had a touch of cramp at about 4 miles, however, and our pair, J. E. Field and F. W. Thorn, who were lying handy, quickly passed him. He recovered to hold on to 4th position. The finest thrill of the evening was provided by a young and diminutive "David" of the Surrey Walking Club, who found the pace and stride of the leaders too much for him during the first 2½ miles of this race and who was then lying only 8th in the field. But he was pugnacious and determined and the set of his mouth said plainly: "Has anybody seen any Goliaths knocking about round here?" Fiercely, although smoothly and stylishly, he pushed on in eager search of something to fight, and soon backmarked a tall young club-fellow who had led him by about 30 yards. Yet by doing so he had picked up no points for his club and he snorted viciously (I believe) as he went by and on after two London Vidarians, H. G. Churcher and P. W. Collier, who were some distance in front. At about 4 miles he caught them and, to his great delight, found them ready for a scrap. He fought them alternately until the bell went for the last lap, and then, making a further effort, gradually forged from two to three yards ahead. Near the tape, however, two quick turns of the head appeared to indicate an invitation to fight out the remaining inches. His fourteen points were thoroughly well earned. J. E. Field and F. W. Thorn both walked well and finished together. The former beat his previous best by 61 seconds and the latter reproduced the style and pace which won him the "Horwood Cup" last December, and which he had not shewn in his last few races. The three mile race followed, and for almost a mile A. D. Cawte, of the Valentine's S.C., led the field. Then, just as Blackmore and Archibald, of the Surrey Walking Club, were overtaking him, he was ruled out, and the pair went on together to finish well ahead of P. R. Bayliss, of the Ashcombe A.C. C. W. Redgrave and R. F. Elson finished together for us some 20 yards behind the Ashcombe man and, although by being so well placed they gathered 29 points for us, the skipper of the Surrey W. Club and his mate reduced our advantage from 10 to 4 points. A. L. Fletcher had just retained the 2 mile Championship of the London Business Houses at Stamford Bridge, but he represented the club in the race over the same distance and, by finishing first, repeated his double of a year ago. For a mile he was closely attended by H. F. King, but he then opened up a gap of about 30 yards and maintained this lead until the end. W. T. Chilton threatened danger to Harold for about 1½ miles, but then dropped back and eventually finished 3rd some 30 yards off. By gaining the maximum quota of points we now led our nearest opponents by 11 points. G. T. Galloway had finished 2nd to Fletcher at Stamford Bridge and he also came on to our meeting afterwards. He raced for the Surrey Walking Club in the final event over 1 mile and walked faultlessly in beating J. A. Bridger, of the London Vidarians, by about 30 yards. A. C. Bayliss, of the Ashcombe A.C., filled the 3rd position a similar distance behind Bridger. Our men finished 4th and 6th, scoring the same number of points as the Surrey Walking Club, and thus enabled us to run out winners of the competition by 11 points. SCORE DETAILS. Belgrave Harriers.—A. L. Fletcher 18pts., H. F. King, 17pts., F. W. Thorn 16½pts., J. E. Field 16½pts., J. G. Scamell 15pts., R. F. Elson 14½pts., C. W. Redgrave 14½pts., L. Storey 13pts. Total 125pts. Surrey Walking Club.—G. T. Galloway 18pts., F. Blackmore 17½pts., W. Archibald 17½pts., W. T. Chilton 16pts., H. W. Snow 14pts., N. A. L. Burt 12pts., R. M. Simmonds 10pts., S. E. Horton 9pts. Total 114pts. The walking this year was of a higher standard than during the past few years and only 3 competitors were disqualified in the course of the evening. Two years ago 3 of our team of 8 were ruled out and it was necessary for us to warn our members that future teams could only be chosen from men who could be relied upon to pass the judges. Despite the warning, 2 of our men failed to satistfy them last year and although we won the contest our victory was not so clean cut and satisfactory as we could have wished it to be. Many of our opponents also earned disqualification, and thus helped us to a rather lame win. This year, however, the whole of the 24 members of the first three teams walked fairly and finished their races and a single disqualification would have cost us the victory. Consequently we have reason to be proud of our success. J.B.B. m. s. 1. A. A. Webb, Polytechnic Harriers 38 31 †2. J. E. Field, Belgrave Harriers 40 17 †2. F. W. items.s: EVENING MEETING—JUNE 24th. Report and results of the club evening meeting on June 24th, where A. W. Penny won the 3 Miles Championship for the Griffin Cup in a club record 15min. 6sec., with handicap, novice walk, veterans and high jump results. The chief event of the evening was the 3 Miles Championship for "The Griffin Cup." Unfortunately, Arthur Allum, the holder, was unable to compete owing to ankle trouble, sustained at the end of the Winter season. Wally Bayliss led the field in the early stages of the race, but was displaced after a while by Arthur Penny, closely followed by Jack Flower. It was obvious that the championship was going to resolve itself into a struggle between the two last-named and this proved to be the case. Over the last lap Arthur drew away, and although Jack seemed to gain a little in the last fifty yards, Penny won by a few yards in the Club record time of 15min. 6sec. C. T. Carter ran well to finish third and would have been much nearer the leaders but for an attack of "stitch" over the last two laps. He should show considerable improvement over the country this coming season. Fourth came H. E. Footer and fifth N. Dewberry. These two gained first-class standard medals (inside 16sec.) and the following received second-class standards, (inside 16min. 30sec.): H. J. Fletcher, W. G. Webb, A. E. Smith, E. A. Duffett and K. B. O'Kell. In the handicaps R. W. Martin was once again prominent in winning the 880 yards race in 1min. 56 4-5sec. The 100 yards went to E. C. Rutter and the quarter-mile was won by C. Christie, the Wimbledon footballer, in very fast time. H. Latter gave evidence of maintained improvement by winning his second Club Walk handicap this season despite a "pull" of 75 yards. Jackman, second, also again showed improved form, and in A. Maynard, the winner of the One Mile Novice Walk, we have another young walker likely to strengthen our teams in due course. items.sum: Report and results of the "Doris" Shield inter-club meeting at the Richmond Athletic Ground on July 9th, where Thames Valley H. took the Shield from Belgrave, with handicap results.
items.s: "DORIS SHIELD" INTER-CLUB COMPETITION. Report and results of the "Doris" Shield inter-club meeting at the Richmond Athletic Ground on July 9th, where Thames Valley H. took the Shield from Belgrave, with handicap results. "It's gone"—in other words, we have lost possession of the "Doris" Shield presented by the late Bob Ricketts for competition between Thames Valley H., Ashcombe A.C. and ourselves. Thames Valley H. are the new holders of the Shield, and we heartily congratulate them on their fine win. The meeting, which was held on the splendid Richmond Athletic Ground on July 9th, was comprised of scratch events for the Shield and also Handicaps open to members of the three competing clubs. In the 100 Yards Scratch race Tavender, of T.V.H., won, with M. E. Odell second and Filkins, of T.V.H., a close third. For the 440 Yards race we relied upon H. Titherley and R. G. Michael and could only manage third place. Cooper, a fine runner, of T.V.H., won in good style, with Beswick, of Ashcombe A.C., second and Michael next. Our man ran rather green and will no doubt improve with more experience of scratch races. In the next Shield event, the 2 Miles Team race, we managed to secure major points, but only on the team principle, our scoring four being N. R. Dewberry 3, Arthur Allum 4, Bill Webb 6, and H. J. Fletcher 7. Thames Valley H. were second, two points in front of Ashcombe's total. L. J. Cohen, of Ashcombe A.C., won the individual race in 9min. 52sec., with A. J. Nuti, of T.V.H., second, while Norman Dewberry ran extremely well to secure third place. In the last race, the 1 Mile Relay, we were already resigned to our loss of the Shield, but at least hoped to score a win in this event. It was not to be, however, and although we led up to the final 220, Odell over this stage had to give way to Tavender, of T.V.H. On analysing these results the point that strikes one most is not so much our decline, but the improvement made by the Thames Valley H. They have been fortunate in securing several new members of distinct promise and must now be reckoned a fighting force in this annual competition. However, we look forward to next year's meeting and guarantee to give them a fine fight in trying to regain possession of our lost honours. With regard to the Handicaps, the Club was more successful in these, and we gained first and second places in the 100 Yards with B. W. Hayman and G. Basford. In the 1 Mile Handicap we had F. Walker 2, T. F. Morrell 3, and Alec Robertshaw 4. The winner, T. J. Lee, of Ashcombe A.C., ran a very plucky race and deserved his victory in what was quite good time. The 2 Miles Walk saw Ashcmbe A.C. gaining first two places with L. F. Bailey, of our own Club, third. So concluded a very interesting evening's sport, which I am sure was enjoyed by both spectators and competitors alike. RESULTS. INTER-CLUB EVENTS. 100 Yards.—1, H. G. Tavender (T.V.H.); 2, M. items.sum: Report of the third Inter-Club Relay Shield meeting at the "News of the World" Track, Mitcham, on July 1st, after which Belgrave led Mitcham A.C. by six points with one meeting left.
items.s: INTER-CLUB RELAY COMPETITION AT MITCHAM. Report of the third Inter-Club Relay Shield meeting at the "News of the World" Track, Mitcham, on July 1st, after which Belgrave led Mitcham A.C. by six points with one meeting left. The third contest for the Inter-Club Relay Shield took place at the "News of the World" Track, Mitcham, on July 1st. The second of the series had taken place at Epsom on June 10th and had left us with a nine points lead in the competition. Although we fielded a fairly useful side in the 4 x 100 Yards we had to be content with third place to Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. Owing to non-arrivals we were forced to run a makeshift team in the 4 x 880 Yards and Mitcham won easily by almost half a lap, with Epsom H. surprisingly beating Croydon for third place. The 4 x 300 Yards saw us having to run R. W. Martin, a half-miler who has done well in recent Club Handicaps, and he ran a very plucky race to enable Jock Wilcock to get away a few feet in front of Rickett, of Croydon. Mitcham A.C. were again easy winners of this event, with ourselves second and then Croydon H. and Epsom H. The 1 Mile Team race gave us our one win of the evening and here our men were A. W. Penny 1, C. T. Carter 4, E. A. Duffett 5. Arthur Allum made a most welcome re-appearance in this race, but was naturally not inclined to force matters in view of his groggy leg. On the evening's running Mitcham A.C. are to be congratulated on their fine show, they scoring 15 points to our 12, and Croydon's 8, with Epsom H. 5. As we had a nine points lead over Mitcham prior to this meeting we thus had a six points lead for the Shield with one more meeting to be held. items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Report of the final Inter-Club Relay meeting at Croydon on July 15th, where Belgrave won the 1 Mile Team race and the Inter-Club Relay Shield (52 pts to Mitcham A.C. 49), with a plea for more sprinters to support away fixtures; the results line prints "4 x 800 Yards" for the 4 x 880 Yards race.
items.s: INTER-CLUB RELAY COMPETITION MEETING. Report of the final Inter-Club Relay meeting at Croydon on July 15th, where Belgrave won the 1 Mile Team race and the Inter-Club Relay Shield (52 pts to Mitcham A.C. 49), with a plea for more sprinters to support away fixtures; the results line prints "4 x 800 Yards" for the 4 x 880 Yards race. The final Inter-Club Relay meeting was held at Croydon on July 15th. The weather was very unsettled and it rained hard during the afternoon, a fact which no doubt accounted for the non-appearance of our sprinters. Only one, F. W. Port, turned up and so we started off under a definite handicap. Although we had a six points lead for the Shield, we were a little apprehensive as to the final result of the evening's sport. In the 4 x 100 Yards, Epsom H. did not field a team and so our boys, namely, Port, Frank Webb, Martin and Michael just ran for the points scored for third place. Croydon managed to beat Mitcham and this of course suited our plans as we only lost one point to our chief rivals. For the 4 x 880 Yards we decided to give R. W. Martin and R. G. Michael a chance of showing whether their Club Handicap running could be produced in scratch races. Michael, doing the first leg, ran well and gave us a lead of 20 yards. Joe Flower went next and Ayton, of Mitcham, cut into this lead, so that when Martin went off he had about 10 yards lead over Norman Gunn. It was here that experience told and although Martin ran a very plucky race, Gunn reduced his lead to a bare yard or so. Frank Webb had Ferdinando, of Mitcham, to contend with on the last stage and, as we rather expected, the Mitcham man eventually beat Frank by about 5 yards. Quite a good race, but it proved that unless we field our best team our chances of beating Mitcham at this distance are very slight. The 4 x 300 Yards was a repetition of the shorter sprint, but for the fact that Mitcham beat Croydon, for whom Les Rickett ran a fine last stage. Giving away nearly 30 yards, he only failed in the last few strides to catch his man. The position, so far as points were concerned, was that up to this stage we had dropped four out of our six lead for the Shield. We were resolved not to have any "one point touches," so told our men it was a question of having "Belgrave" first, the rest nowhere, in the final race, which was the 1 Mile Team contest. They rose to the occasion in fine style and finished thus: A. W. Penny 1, C. T. Carter 2, A. Allum 3, and F. Tame 5. Arthur Penny's time of 4min. 42sec. on a track which was like a morass after the heavy rain which had fallen during the meeting, was very fine running, and he is, without a doubt, a live candidate for our Mile Championship honours. After the scores had been totalled up, the result of the competition for the Inter-Club Relay Shield was as follows: Belgrave H., 52pts., 1; Mitcham A.C., 49 pts., 2; Croydon H., 41pts., 3; Epsom H., 16pts., 4. There is no doubt that we have our distance men to thank, not for the first time, for winning the Shield once more, and we must find some sprinters who are willing to assist the Club in these races in which, although there are no prizes to be won, there is at least something to be gained, and that is the feeling that you at any rate have done your bit towards helping the Club to success. We have been given a very close run by Mitcham A.C., and Croydon were not far behind, and although we wish our rivals every success it would be rather a blow to our prestige if we lost this Shield. Lose it we certainly shall, the same as we did the "Doris" Shield, if our members do not support the away fixtures better than they do. I know there is a feeling in some quarters that the "old gang" are always invited to run, but, at all events, I know we can rely upon the older members not to let the Club down, and although I admit we have a lot of promising youngsters, you must remember that Mitcham can turn out very useful teams at all distances and that unless we make an endeavour to field our best side they will surely beat us. The results this season prove this, and our only hope is that next year our young members will have improved sufficiently to make them fit contenders for places in our teams. Until that time we must be content to rely upon the "old gang," men who run 10 miles over the country with the same cheerfulness as they do half a mile, and men who, at least, have the interests of the Club at heart. items.s: THE JUNIOR INTER-CLUB CONTEST. Report of Belgrave's easy win in the Junior Inter-Club Competition at Battersea Park (all three events), with the 300 yards and 880 yards Club handicaps held at the same meeting. This year's Junior Inter-Club Competition, held at Battersea Park, provided our boys with an easy win and gave ample evidence of the ability and promise of our young runners. Although we cannot truthfully say that our men were fully extended, enough was seen of their talent to justify us prophesying "big" futures for them. We must consider ourselves very fortunate to have such capable athletes in the making, and to know that in addition to those who actually represented the Club in this contest, there are many others who should also develop into first-class performers. The first event to be decided was the 3 x 100 yards relay. E. H. Pack gained a very narrow lead on the first "leg" over Burroughs, of Mitcham A.C., the Surrey County Junior champion, and this was increased considerably by R. Macpherson and D. Gratte, who breasted the tape an easy winner. In the 880 yards team race (4 to start and 3 to score) we were represented by F. H. C. White, S. Garland, W. G. Woolmer and A. A. Clubb. The race developed into an interesting struggle between White and Garland, White eventually drawing away in the straight to win in 2min. 10 2-5secs. Woolmer (6th) completed our team, which scored 9 points to the 19 of Mitcham A.C., and Croydon H.s' 20 points. The third event, the 3 x 200 yards relay, gave us our third win. The Mitcham runner led Gratte at the end of the first stage, but Clapham, running second, outpaced his rival, leaving Pack to stride round in effortless fashion. Two Club handicaps were held at this meeting, one at 300 yards, the other at 880 yards. In the former race, A. F. Powter was successful from the 22 yards mark, with G. Weston second. Tom Cotton won the "half" in workmanlike fashion, and the second man, R. G. Michael, impressed by his fine running from the 40 yards mark. RESULTS. 3 x 100 Yards.—1, Belgrave H. (E. H. Pack, R. items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Round-up of Belgrave members' placings at open and other meetings in June and July 1931.
items.s: ROUND THE MEETINGS. Round-up of Belgrave members' placings at open and other meetings in June and July 1931. The successes of our members during the past few weeks have been so many and varied that it has proved impossible to keep pace with them, and for that reason the following list does not claim to be complete. Our congratulations are extended to all those who have succeeded in being placed. June 13th.—The 1 Mile Team race in the Southern Amateur Athletic League was held at the Civil Service Meeting on this day and our team finished third. Bill Webb finished second in the Civil Service Mile Championship. June 15th.—A. L. Fletcher retained his title of London Business Houses Walk Champion, and T. H. Scrimshaw won the 880 yards title. June 20th.—The Southern Championships. In these Championships, held at Southend, J. W. Clemens won the Long Jump title with a fine jump of 22ft. 4½in. In the final of the half-mile Scrimshaw, although beating 1min. 57sec. for the distance, was only placed fourth. E. R. Turner (175ft. 7in.) and G. H. Powell (173ft. 1½in.) were second and third in the Javelin throw and J. Conroy was third in the Shot Putt. On the same afternoon Fred Rickards accomplished a very fine feat in winning "The Guildford Cup" race over 50 kilometres in 4hrs. 36min. 58 1-5sec., and so proved himself one of the finest long-distance walkers this country possesses. June 24th.—T. Cotton, 3rd, 880 yards, "Z" Division. June 27th.—The majority of our men competed at the Jubilee meeting of the Ravensbourne Club. Our team in the 4 x 880 yards relay consisting of H. Titherley, F. R. Webb, T. J. Flower and T. H. Scrimshaw, won fairly easily, and our representatives in the 4 x 440 yards (H. Titherley, E. H. Jarvis, F. A. Arrowsmith, T. H. Scrimshaw) were placed second. In the Three Miles Team Race our team was placed second, only four points behind the winners, Highgate H. A. Penny ran well to finish fourth in such a classy field and was well backed up by Footer and Warboys. Our team in the 2 Miles Walk finished third (H. F. King, J. E. Field, F. W. Thorn). On the same day at Luton, E. R. Turner won a Scratch Javelin Throw with a throw of 173ft. 8in. L. Morgan won both the 100 yards and 200 yards handicaps confined to Police held at this meeting. At Belvedere, G. Basford was second in both sprints, and C. Mains second in the Mile. July 3rd and 4th.—A.A.A. Championships. T. H. Scrimshaw distinguished himself by running second in his heat (his time being 1min. 56 2-5sec.) and fourth in the Final, with T. Hampson, S. Townend and Dr. Peltzer in front of him. Truly remarkable running, for a lad not yet twenty-one. The performances of Clemens (Long Jump) and Fletcher (Seven Miles Walk—54min. 15sec.) are mentioned elsewhere. J. F. King and H. F. King narrowly missed Standards in the Two Miles Walk; and J. E. Flower was fifth in the Steeplechase. E. R. Turner (6th) gained Standard in the Javelin, but A. Penny was not so successful in his event, the Four Miles. July 11th.—INTER-COUNTY DAY. Many of our men were called upon to represent their counties. E. R. Turner (Bedfordshire) and G. H. Powell (Surrey) were first and second in the Javelin Throw, and Scrimshaw finished third in the 880 yards after a very fine race with Hampson. On the same day our Two Mile Team was successful at Durants Park. July 15th.—T. Cotton, 1st, 880 yards, Croydon. July 18th.—"The Jockey Cup" was won by our two-milers for the fourth year in succession at Herne Hill. Arthur Penny finished second and our team (Penny, Jack Flower, Carter) scored 13 points to Highgate's 21. In the Open Handicaps J. G. Barrett won the 220 yards, F. Walker was second in the 880 yards and F. Powter third in the sprint. In the Printing Trade Events, J. Smith was successful in the Veterans' 80 yards from the half-yard mark, L. Clapham had two place prizes in the sprints, and A. A. Harley was second in the Walk. This must conclude the list of successes, although it is far from complete. Wilcock and Morrell, among others, have been troubling the judges and there are, no doubt, many other names equally deserving of inclusion. items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Walking notes on Tommy Green's return, Fred Rickards' form, arrangements for the London to Brighton Walk on September 12th, and new walking members.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes on Tommy Green's return, Fred Rickards' form, arrangements for the London to Brighton Walk on September 12th, and new walking members. We are very glad to see Tommy Green out again, and although he is not yet his old self, he has already been responsible for some very fine performances. Best of these, perhaps, was to beat T. Lloyd Johnson, the National 20 miles and 50 kilometres champion, in a 25 miles race at Manchester. We hope that Tommy will be fit for the Brighton Walk in September and show that eight hours for the distance can be beaten. * * * * * Fred Rickards, as mentioned elsewhere, is now very fit and should also do well in the London—Brighton Walk on September 12th. Anyone who is thinking of walking in this race and has not yet received an entry form should communicate with me as soon as possible. * * * * * I should also be glad to hear from any Club members or friends who are willing to act as attendants to our men on the road. A good attendant can mean all the difference between a good performance and an indifferent one on this trying course and it is up to us to see that our representatives do not suffer in this respect. Offers of assistance will be gratefully received by the Walking Hon. Sec., whose address appears at the foot of these notes. * * * * * We shall, no doubt, be having the usual 'bus for supporters following the race, and application for seats should be made at once. The 'bus, besides providing a good day out and a view of one of the most sporting events held in this country, is also very useful for bringing back to London the attendants and their cycles. We welcome this month J. A. Grimwade, a stylish young walker who has won his first "Open" race and bids fair to become a Club champion in due course; and R. L. Bowles, a powerfully-built novice with undoubted ability. We shall also have in our ranks shortly, J. F. O'Connell, who won the Public Schools Mile Walk Championship last April, thus emulating the performance of Jack Carne, who was record-holder of this event for many years. All enquiries to A. A. items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Running Hon. Sec.'s notes reviewing the track season, complaining of members failing to turn up for team races, and giving the final Club meeting, England v. Italy and the winter season opening.
items.s: FORTHCOMING FIXTURES. Running Hon. Sec.'s notes reviewing the track season, complaining of members failing to turn up for team races, and giving the final Club meeting, England v. Italy and the winter season opening. We are nearing the end of the Track season; one which has had its ups and downs so far as results go, but which, taken generally, has been a successful one for our members. Many have gained a prominence hitherto unattained and we hope they will remain at the top for quite a number of years. In these days of such strenuous competition it becomes increasingly difficult for a man to keep on the flood tide of success, and it more or less depends upon the individual himself, by studying his line of training and taking care not to overdo it, as to whether he will continue to show repeat performances. I have been a little disappointed with our members' attitude towards Inter-Club Relays and also Open Team races. On several occasions I have advised members of a meeting; in some instances have sent them the necessary Competitors' Ticket, and in the absence of any reply have naturally assumed they would be present at the meeting. They have failed to turn up, however, and the result has been we have had to field weak or short teams. Perhaps it is that they do not like writing a postcard—too much trouble, or else too busy—but whatever the cause, it certainly places me in an awkward position as to our teams. However, the season is now practically over and so we look forward to better results all round next year. We have the final Club meeting at Battersea Park Track on August 19th, when Handicaps at the following distances will be held: 100 Yards, 440 Yards, 1320 Yards, 2 Miles Walk. Entries (1/- each event) close on Friday, August 14th, and I trust our members will support our last meeting of the Summer in large numbers. On August 22nd there will be held at Stamford Bridge an International match, namely, England v. Italy, and this will be a meeting well worth watching. Our visitors from Italy have already been very prominent in our annual Championships and they will, no doubt, give England a hard fight for victory. The Winter Season will soon be here and we open at Wimbledon at our headquarters, St. John's Hall, Ridgway, on the last Saturday in September. The usual Road Running and Walking Handicaps will be held the following week and all members, old and new, are cordially invited to come along and join in the fun. We are already compiling our fixture list and hope to have it completed at an early date. In addition to meeting all our old friends and rivals we hope to break fresh ground and meet new faces, all of which tends to stiffen our boys so that the rigours of the later championship races will find them tuned up to concert pitch. Our prospects are as bright as ever they have been, and with Arthur Allum to give us a lead we ought to have a good season and so consolidate our position as one of the strongest clubs in the country. All entries and enquiries to E. A. Duffett, Running Hon. Sec., 1 Raymead Avenue, Thornton Heath. Arthur Allum Arthur Allum expected to lead the winter team E. A. Duffett E. A. Duffett Running Hon. items.label: July 1931
items.sum: Humorous account of a Club evening at Battersea Park written as a string of puns on members' surnames.
items.s: A "ROLLIN"(G) STOREY. Humorous account of a Club evening at Battersea Park written as a string of puns on members' surnames. On Wednesday, July 8th, we spent a very pleasant evening. Boarding a 'bus at TUTIN we rode via "CLAPHAM," to Battersea Park. The "CLARK" of weather had not been too bad, a little on the "COLE"d side, and the sun seemed to want to "HYDE" behind the "GRAY" sky on the "WESTON" front. Passing the bowling "GREEN," which looked at its "BEST," we stopped to admire the "FLOWERS" (especially the sweet "WILLIAMS") which made a "NICE" picture. Arriving at the running track we were about to witness (without "PAMMENT," excepting a two-"PENNY" programme) some good performances by the Junior section of that famous "CLUBB" known as the "BELS." We were just in time to see "Powter" win the first heat in the 300 yds. handicap and, he didn't "TURNER" "HARE," he "CAPP"ed it later by winning the final. (By the way, I hear his father makes a very good running shoe at the "WRIGHT" p"RICE," they cannot be "BEATON," you can "FOOTER" long in comfort, and you never get a "DUF-FIT"). A little accident occurred in the third heat, Fleming, getting a bit "COOK"ed, "FELL" and brought down "A Man" who seems to be a "MARTYR" to falling lately. "PACK," with his "CARNIE"-ra action, did well in the relays, and "WHITE" blended well with the "Claret and Gold" in the "FIELD" for the half-mile. "Tommy" did well to break the "COTTON" (sorry, I mean worsted) in the senior half-mile handicap. I noticed our old friend Charlie "FISH"ing about for new talent, it is a "MORRELL" certainty he can "WAKEM" up a bit, when they get into his "WEBB." Reading just lately about "beer in parks," we adjourned to the "BARS BE"fore leaving, but found we could get neither "BROWN" ale, "PORT," "READ'S," "WALKER," nor "BASS FOR D"rinking purposes, so we had to be content with good "BRAND"s of toffee by firms named "BARRETT" and Macin"TOSH." We were sorry we did not see our young half-miler taking an active part in the proceedings, and one thing I should like to say is that if he keeps his ana"TOMMY" "SCRIM(P)SHAW"ly, we shall be able to con"GRATTE"ulate him on being picked to run for the Old Country at Los Angeles next year. C. Williams C. items.label: August 1931
items.sum: Welcome to J. B. Belchamber as the club's new President, recalling his walking performances and service to the club.
items.s: OUR PRESIDENT. Welcome to J. B. Belchamber as the club's new President, recalling his walking performances and service to the club. It is with the greatest of pleasure that we welcome Mr. J. B. Belchamber as President of the Club for the ensuing year. "Jimmy" has always been a hard worker throughout the twenty odd years he has been associated with the Club. Much of the work he has done for the Belgrave welfare has been done unobtrusively, but none the less effectively; and he is one of the men to whom our present position as a leading Club is largely due. As Club Walking Captain he achieved many meritorious performances, some of the most notable being, perhaps, his third place in the A.A.A. 7 miles championship; fourth in the London—Brighton Walk in 1924, following upon his fifth position the previous year; and his second position, in 1926, in the Brighton and back walk (104 miles) to the record-breaking W. F. Baker. On the legislative side of the Club, and also outside, he has done yeoman service, and we are very proud indeed to have such a man—a man in a million it might be said—at the head of our organisation. To repeat, we are proud of our new President, as we have been of those who have preceded him in office, and we trust that we shall give him every reason to be proud of the Club over which he presides. J. B. Belchamber J. B. items.sum: Club notes: international selections for T. H. Scrimshaw, E. R. Turner and G. H. Powell, Tommy Green's London—Brighton walk, French Society of Walkers honours, new members, subscriptions, ties and cheap tickets to Wimbledon.
items.s: Club notes: international selections for T. H. Scrimshaw, E. R. Turner and G. H. Powell, Tommy Green's London—Brighton walk, French Society of Walkers honours, new members, subscriptions, ties and cheap tickets to Wimbledon. Congratulations to T. H. Scrimshaw upon his selection to represent England v. France, Italy and Germany. To become a "treble" international in the course of one season, and before the age of 21, is a wonderful achievement. Tommy has not been, and is never likely to be upset by his successes and we trust that he will represent his Club and Country for many years to come. E. R. Turner, our Javelin throwing expert, also reecived his "vest" versus Italy; whilst G. H. Powell was a reserve — a similar position to that filled by Clemens, our Long-jumper and the Southern champion, in the match versus France. Congratulations to these men upon the high honour bestowed upon them. It seems impossible to keep Tommy Green's name out of these congratulatory notices (not that we want to!), and his excellent walking in the London—Brighton race, despite wretched weather, calls for the highest praise. He was near to equalling his own record, but eventually finished a few minutes outside and had to be content with second-best figures for the distance. We must congratulate F. G. Thomson upon receiving the diploma and life membership of the French Society of Walkers, and T. W. Greeen, who has also been made a life member of this organisation. These two gentlemen are the first outside France to have been so honoured; and we are glad to know that it is two Belgrave men that have been selected for this distinction. We extend our best wishes to the following: E. C. A. Heather, S. L. Fairman, J. E. Edwards, G. Lennox, W. H. Martyr, A. Vincent, R. Laing, J. F. O'Connell, H. G. T. Ellis, L. Jackson, A. G. Bruce, J. T. Robinson, D. E. Brown, J. E. F. Barnett, A. E. Taylor, H. W. Shields, H. G. Churcher and C. E. Churcher, who have been elected to membership recently. We trust they will enjoy a long, happy association with the Club. Annual subscriptions are now due, so don't fail to send yours along without delay. Also don't forget to include the Gazette arrears, or that advance subscription. The Hon. Treasurer's address appears on page 1. Club ties may be had from A. A. Harley, 39 Roxburgh Avenue, Isleworth, at a cost of 2/6, or by post 2/9. Anyone requiring Club vests, coat badges, etc., should get in touch with the Hon. Treasurer. Members are reminded that cheap return tickets are available to Wimbledon from Waterloo, Vauxhall and Clapham Junction Stations, and may be had from Mr. W. J. Fish, or other Club officials. The Committee are anxious that full use should be made of these tickets and so repay them for the trouble entailed, and at the same time save the pockets of members. A good plan is to buy two tickets at the commencement of the season, and thereafter buy one from Mr. Fish each time Wimbledon is visited, for use the following week. In this way one ticket is always in reserve, and one is saved the sorrowful experience of having to pay full fare, knowing that with a little forethought, only half the amount would have been expended! e: Belgrave v. Cheiron Club and Old Emanuel A.C. match
items.s: MATCH v. OLD EMANUEL AND CHEIRON CLUB. Report and results of the triangular match against the Cheiron Club and Old Emanuel A.C. at Battersea Park on 22 July, won by Belgrave, with two club handicaps. On July 22nd, at Battersea Park, we held a triangular match versus the Cheiron Club and Old Emanuel A.C. A series of scratch events comprised the match and in addition we held a couple of Club handicaps. Running briefly through the match events, M. E. Odell won the 100 yards for us, with G. Basford third. F. Tame finished third to T. A. N. Mairs, who won the 880 yards for the Cheiron Club. We had first and second in the Long Jump, with J. W. Clemens and B. W. Fleming. The 440 yards was a good race with Ernie Jarvis narrowly beaten by R. E. Morgan of the Cheiron Club, in 52 9-10 sec. R. G. Michael filled third position and at this stage we were well ahead on points. In the 1 Mile A. Kench, a member of our own club, was running for the Old Emanuel A.C., and he won the race in brilliant style, finishing with a positively electrifying burst down the straight. Joe Flower and Bill Rice filled the minor placings and so collected a few more points. A Tie was the result of the High Jump, Fleming, and W. S. Collings, of the Old Emanuel A.C., both clearing 5 ft. The 220 yards saw J. E. Read score a good win, with the Cheiron Club and Old Emanuel representatives second and third. The last match event, namely the 1 Mile Relay, was literally a walk-over for the Club, the exciting part of the race being the struggle for second place between Cheiron and Emanuel. Tommy Scrimshaw turned out in this event and, running the half-mile against men who had already competed that evening, he gained for us a huge lead which our other men easily maintained. When the points were totalled up, the following result accrued: Belgrave H., 24½ pts.; Cheiron Club, 12½pts.; Old Emanuel A.C., 11 pts. The two Club Handicaps were the 1 Mile Run, which F. A. Sandell won in good style, with those two consistent runners, R. W. Martin and F. Walker, second and third, and a 2 Miles Walk, which was won by the limit-man, S. T. Ball. RESULTS. 100 Yards.—M. E. items.s: THE LAST EVENING MEETING. Report and results of the last club evening meeting of the season at Battersea Park on 19 August, with 100 yards, 1320 yards, 440 yards and 2 miles walk handicaps. The last Club meeting of the season was held at Battersea Park Track on August 19th, when four Handicaps were decided. In the 100 Yards, E. R. Jessop, one of our veteran members, ran well from a long-mark to score a decisive win. Jock McKay showed a welcome return to form in gaining a place. The 1320 Yards saw Tommy Scrimshaw on the scratch mark and although considered a non-starter he raked together some togs and astounded us all by nearly catching his field on the first lap. He then retired and we discovered he had only been round for a training spin! In the meantime the leadership was changing hands rapidly and Jack Flower, coming through very fast, looked as though he would pull it off. One of the long-markers in F. J. Green had a little in hand, however, and went away from Jack down the straight. F. Walker once again secured third place and he strikes one as being distinctly promising. The 440 Yards found P. J. E. Cook the only back-marker to qualify for the final. This was a well-contested race and T. C. Jones beat F. A. Horton, with F. G. Ford securing third place. In the 2 Miles Walk, F. E. Eborall proved a good winner—with Charlie Speechley second and T. W. Salmon third—so winning his first Club prize. RESULTS. 100 Yards.—Heat Winners: J. G. Barrett (5); J. R. McKay (5½); G. items.label: August 1931
items.sum: Report of the club championship meeting of 1 August 1931: half-mile, 100 yards, furlong, quarter-mile, mile (won by Kench in a Club record), junior furlong and walking championships, plus handicaps.
items.s: THE CHAMPIONSHIP MEETING. Report of the club championship meeting of 1 August 1931: half-mile, 100 yards, furlong, quarter-mile, mile (won by Kench in a Club record), junior furlong and walking championships, plus handicaps. AUGUST 1ST, 1931. The first championship to be decided was the 100 yards Boys' Championship, for which event only four entered, and only two started. W. A. Fox won fairly easily in time which was nearly as good as Pamment's time last year. This event was followed immediately by the half-mile championship. Neither Tosh, the holder, nor Scrimshaw, an ex-champion, started; the former has done hardly any running this year on account of ill-health, and the latter was representing his country. Six men lined up at the start; R. G. Michael had the inside berth and next to him in order were Frank Webb, H. Jones, E. A. Duffett, F. G. Ford, with T. J. Flower on the outside. Jones took the lead at the start, with Ford and Duffett close up. At the bell all the six runners were together, and at the quarter Jones and Ford shared the lead with Flower and Webb, side by side, just behind. Michael, who had been lying back, was now beginning to move up. With three hundred yards to go Jones, who had been in the lead practically throughout, made his effort and gained a useful lead. Meanwhile, Michael had been gradually drawing up, and at the furlong started his strong finish. He quickly caught Jones, and maintaining his speed and style went on to win a cleverly run race. Frank Webb and Ford both passed Jones, and the two of them had a desperate struggle for second place, which Frank just managed to win. For two years in succession Ford has been placed third in this race. The 100 yards championship was disappointing as a race, for neither Wilcock nor Jarvis started. Maurice Odell therefore won without serious opposition, but he did so in quite good time. He has won this championship seven times, and has held it continuously since 1925—a fine record for a sprinter. In the furlong championship, Jarvis, Wilcock and Odell were all non-starters, and the final was a glorious race between J. E. Read and G. Basford. Basford got in front of the King's College Hospital sprinter down the straight and stayed in the lead to win his first championship. Basford must be congratulated on his pluck in this race, for I have seldom seen a man more exhausted after a sprint. By this courage of his, and his hard training, he has developed from a middle-marker to a back-marker and champion. Jarvis, who did not start in either of the sprints, turned out in the quarter. He thought that R. G. Michael was a dangerous rival, and therefore had saved himself for this one race. He also saved himself in his heat, by just managing to finish third. It will be remembered that Jarvis did the same thing last year in the furlong championship. When the final came along, however, Jarvis found that he could easily beat the new half-mile title-holder over the quarter. That fine all-rounder, P. J. E. Cook, was third. As usual, the mile championship was a thrilling affair. Sixteen men lined up at the start, and it was thought before hand that it would be a race between Penny, Rice and Kench, but I believe the last-named was really the favourite. At the start, T. J. Flower jumped into the lead. For some years now Joe has done this in races, finding that it suits him to make his own running in the early stages. He was followed by Carter and Kench. These three were still together at the quarter, but after that Penny (the Club 3 miles champion) took over the pace-making. In the early part of the season it was generally recognised that Penny was the only one of our many good milers who was fit and capable of running a good mile, and in consequence he began to take miles seriously. Being a long-distance runner, he has to rely on his speed in the middle stages of the race, rather than the usual long sustained sprint at the end. His judgment was correct; it was essential that he made the pace once the competitors had settled down. Penny still held the lead at the half-mile, but Kench and Rice were near him, followed by Footer—who was later to frighten some of the favourites. Behind Footer was Bill Webb. At three-quarters of a mile Penny was still making the pace, but Footer was moving up rapidly and had passed Kench and Rice. Carter and Bill Webb were just behind these two. Then came Dewberry and a man who has been placed in handicaps every time except once this season. I refer to F. Walker, who is probably a potential Club champion. With 300 yards to go Footer raced past Penny and gained a big lead. As soon as he realised what Footer was doing, Kench started to chase him. But Rice was inclined to wait, thinking no doubt that neither could keep it up. Footer had run brilliantly, but it could hardly be expected of him that he could finish ahead of Kench, Rice or Penny. Nor did he, for Kench, maintaining his pace, passed him and took the lead somewhere near the long-jump pit. Rice now woke up to such purpose that he even caught Kench at the dressing-room. Some of us wondered whether Kench really could keep up that pace of his any longer, for it must be remembered he had been almost sprinting from the three-hundred mark. But he did keep it up right to the tape and Rice (the holder) had to be content with second place fifteen yards behind, Penny being third. I suppose Kench's long sustained finishing burst must be on a par with Jackson's Olympic Games race of 1912 and with Brown's amazing last quarted of a mile at the 1930 London Fire Brigade Sports. Needless to say, Kench's effort is a Club record. No less than seven men outside the first three beat the time standard, these being, in order of finish: Footer, Carter, Dewberry, Walker, W. G. Webb, Robertshaw and Mains. The furlong junior championship was a tragedy. At least it was so for the holder, S. Garland. Something went wrong at the bend in the first heat and Garland and Hyde fell, which, of course, knocked both of them out of the final. However, the new champion, J. D. Edwards, is a real find for the Club, and his final time was faster than Garland's of last year. For many years now, A. L. Fletcher has been in a class by himself in the Club as a track walker, and he had little strong opposition in the Walking Championship, retaining his title with ease. As last year, F. W. Thorn was second and in his walking he gave the impression that he was out to walk in good style rather than attempt to beat Fletcher, or put up a fast time. Thorn was not second all the way, for H. F. King walked behind Fletcher at a very fast pace for the two laps, after which he was disqualified. For most of the way Field was next to Thorn, but towards the end, Redgrave passed him and finished third, putting up his best performance in a Club event. The next two were Field and Harley, who beat the second-class standard time of 16 minutes. In addition to the championships there were the usual three handicaps. The first was the half-mile, which was won by Cotton off a short mark. It looks as though Cotton should have entered the half championship in an attempt to be placed. F. E. Cullen won the 75 yards handicap, and A. H. Green, who had previously finished third in the 100 yards championship, finished third in this event also. The remaining handicap was the hurdles race. This was won by Harper, who just beat the back-marker, T. C. Jones. Jones, earlier in the afternoon, had finished second in the half-mile handicap. Powell, who always seems to be placed in this event, finished third. The final of this event was the last race of the afternoon. In every event, except the hundred and the walk, titles had changed hands, and except in the quarter all the new title-holders were winning their first Club championship. Last year the chief impression left on the mind of the writer was that a large number of juniors had suddenly begun to take a prominent place in the Club. This year, the chief memory is that of the thrilling battle of champion and ex-champions in the last quarter of the mile championship. L.E.F. items.label: August 1931
items.sum: Report of the London to Brighton walk of 12 September 1931, won by Tommy Green in the rain without beating his record, with Belgrave third team after leading at Bolney.
items.s: ON THE BRIGHTON ROAD. Report of the London to Brighton walk of 12 September 1931, won by Tommy Green in the rain without beating his record, with Belgrave third team after leading at Bolney. September 12th, 1931. Being an account of a splendid attempt by Tommy Green to beat his own record over the historic course, narrowly frustrated by inclement weather; of how Belgrave had team honours in safe keeping (so it seemed!) at three-quarter distance, only to lose them in the last few miles; of the particularly good "first attempts" of two of our young walkers, Messrs. Hillier and Field; and sundry other matters of importance and interest to all Belgravians. Rain came with the dawn on September 12th, the day appointed for the Annual London—Brighton Walk, promoted by our friends the Surrey Walking Club; and rain continued intermittently through the day, rendering conditions extremely difficult for the walkers. Eleven of our men started from Westminster at the stroke of seven from Big Ben, and a twelfth, G. H. Laurie, half an hour later. At Croydon the field was led by Heaney, of Lancashire Walking Club, with a group consisting of Green, Lloyd-Johnson (Leicester), Ludlow and Taylor (Derby W.C.), D. Gum (Essex Beagles), and F. Holt (Yorkshire W.C.), a few yards in the rear. Gradually, Green and Johnson shook off their opponents and at Crawley (29 miles 1,104 yards) they were walking together. Soon after leaving Crawley, however, Tommy shot away and at "The Queen's Head," Bolney (38 miles 408 yards) was 7 mins. 25 secs. ahead of the Leicester man, who holds the R.W.A. Championships at 20 miles and 50 kilometres. This represents really wonderful walking on the part of Tommy, and it is a great pity that the rain, which by this time was insistent, handicapped our champion and prevented him from improving upon the record figures which he set up last year. Given fine weather another year, we may be certain that eight hours will be beaten for the distance by the Belgrave man. Last year's time of 8 hrs. 2 min. 55 secs., and that recorded this year, 8 hrs. 5 min. 43 secs., are superlative performances and considerable improvement upon the previous record by H. V. L. Ross, accomplished in 1909, of 8 hrs. 11 min. 14sec. This year's walk adds to our claim that Tommy Green is the "best ever" at distance walking and future generations of athletes and sportsmen may well look back with amazement at Tommy's astounding performances. But to get back to the race. Field and Hillier always seemed to be walking well within themselves, and Fred Rickards, who has been responsible in the past for some excellent walking in this race, after a slow start, gained numerous positions until at one time he was sixth. Between Crawley and Bolney he walked at an amazing pace and actually covered this section of the course in three minutes faster time than the second man, Lloyd-Johnson. At Bolney, with a little under 14 miles to go, an attempt was made to get an idea of the team scores, and we were delighted to find that we were leading. The approximate positions at this point were :— Belgrave H. ... ... ... 43 pts. Surrey W.C. ... ... ... 52 pts. Birmingham W.C. ... ... ... 53 pts. Here our scoring men were : Green (1), Rickards (6), Hillier (17), and A. H. Field (19). Joe King retired at this point, and Rickards, whose efforts over the Crawley—Bolney section now appeared to be taking their toll, eventually retired a few miles along the road. This necessitated going back to A. G. White for our fourth man and our high hopes of winning were turned to speculation as to the possibility of our team being placed! Such are the fortunes of the Brighton Walk! The Birmingham Walking Club walked splendidly in the last few miles of the race and they finished 9th, 10th, 11th and 13th, all four men finishing the course inside nine hours—a wonderful effort, deserving our heartiest congratuations. The promoting Club were placed second and we gained the third set of medals. Lloyd-Johnson's time over the historic course of 8 hrs. 16 min. 18 sec. was very creditable, especially as it was his first attempt. Green's performance has already been commented upon and carries with it the Club Long Distance Championship Medal and "Belgrave" Cup. This was, of course, as expected, but the performance of R. G. Hillier and A. H. Field in gaining the second and third medals, and in accomplishing such fine times, came as a pleasant surprise. We extend our heartiest congratulations to them upon their success, which was well-deserved on account of the large amount of hard training, extending over many weeks, that they had subjected themselves to during their preparation. It is very heartening to know that we have such promising young walkers in our ranks, worthy of upholding the prestige gained by the Club in the past. We trust that next year they will join the select band who have beaten 9 hours for the journey. Future hopes in the race must be considered very bright. During the progess of the race the loyal supporters of the Club encouraged our men by their shouts from the Club 'bus which had been commissioned, as usual. Our best thanks are due to the attendants who accompanied our men. The task, never an enviable one, was a thousand times worse on a day such as we experienced, and we are very grateful to those who assisted the Club in this way. While we have walkers such as those who represented us on this occasion, self-sacrificing friends to attend to their wants, and a loyal band of Club men to add their support, we need have no worries about the continued progress of our Club. items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING. Report of the Annual General Meeting of 24 September 1931 at St. Philip's Hall, at which J. B. Belchamber was elected President and the officers and committee were chosen. This meeting was held on the evening of September 24th, at St. Philip's Hall, Elizabeth Street, S.W.1, and was well attended. After the notice convening the meeting had been read, and the minutes of the previous A.G.M. passed, the Hon. Secretary made his report. He briefly sketched the past year's activities, athletically and socially, and concluded by saying that there was no other Club to even challenge comparison with Belgrave. Judged from the combined viewpoints—running, walking, field-events and socially—no one could cast doubt upon the Club's pre-eminence. His speech was enthusiastically received, as was that of the Hon. Treasurer, whose report disclosed a very favourable state of affairs. The Hon. Editors then presented a Gazette report, which was favourably received by the meeting. The Election of Officers then began. Mr. E. Gordon, after two years in the Presidential chair, relinquished his office, and nominated Mr. J. B. Belchamber, a co-worker in the Club's interests for the past twenty years, for the position. "Jimmy" was elected unanimously and told the audience that the Presidency of the Club was one of the highest honours that could come any man's way, and that he would do his utmost to prove himself worthy of it. All our Vice-Presidents were re-elected and the name of W. L. Bayliss added. Mr. H. Parker, the Hon. Treasurer, announced that he was no longer able to devote the time that the position demanded, with its growing responsibilities and ramifications, and nominated Mr. W. H. Hare, a past Hon. Treasurer, as his successor, who was elected unanimously. The following Officers were then elected : Gen. Hon. Secretary, W. L. Bayliss; Running Hon. Secretary, E. A. Duffett; Walking Hon. Secretary, A. A. Harley; Social Hon. Secretary, W. A. Rice; Cross-Country Captain, W. G. Webb; Vice-Captains, H. E. Footer and R. J. Savage; Road-Walking Captain, F. H. Elson; Vice-Captain E. Saunders; Track Captain (Running), W. G. Webb; Vice-Captain, W. A. Rice; Track Captain (Walking), A. L. Fletcher; Field Events Captain, G. H. Powell; Vice-Captain, J. Clemens; Hon. Handicappers (Walking), J. B. Belchamber; (Running), L. E. Fletcher; Trustees, O. Horwood, E. Gordon; Hon. Auditor, J. R. McKay. Many of these have already served the Club well in their various capacities, and the newcomers will, no doubt, prove themselves of great worth. The same remarks also apply to the new Committee, who were elected as follows: H. Parker, F. G. Thomson, L. E. Fletcher, F. R. Webb, H. L. Rollins, J. R. McKay, B. J. T. Knifton, C. W. Redgrave, H. Evans, K. B. O'Kell. Votes of thanks were passed to the retiring officials and all who had worked for the Club. "Other Business" was then invited and several matters were discussed and recommended to the Committee for their further attention. A vote of thanks to the Chairman concluded the meeting. E. Gordon E. items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes: new walking members, the winter open-race fixtures, the walking secretary's new address, and Tommy Green's wins at Nottingham—Birmingham, Hastings—Brighton and Manchester—Blackpool. We are joined this month by C. E. Churcher, H. G. Churcher, S. L. Fairman, J. F. O'Connell, D. E. Brown and E. C. Heather. The ability of the Churcher brothers is well and E. C. Heather. The ability of the Churcher brothers is well known to all those interested in Walking and there can be no doubt that they will be of great value to our teams when they are duly qualified. Heather is a stylish young walker whose future will be watched with interest, for he has possibilities of developing into really first-class man as he matures in years. We extend a cordial welcome to these newcomers. * * * * * The Winter season promises to be as strenuous as ever. Following upon our own Club novice and five-miles handicap, the "Open" season commences with a race promoted by the Highgate Harriers (who have taken over the R.W.A. date) at New Southgate on October 31st, and the Enfield A.C. "Open" follows on November 14th. Our own Open race will take place on November 28th, when it is hoped a record entry will be obtained, and a record number of Belgrave men included in that entry. All walkers are requested to note the Hon. Secretary's change of address. Letters should be addressed to :— A. A. Harley, 39 Roxburgh Avenue, Isleworth, Middlesex. * * * * * All walkers are reminded that entry forms for the Open race should be handed or sent to A. A. Harley about 10 days before the race takes place, in order that teams may be made up and entered. * * * * * Green's Brighton performance is apt to dwarf some other very fine achievements; but space must be found to congratulate him upon his ridiculously easy wins in the Nottingham—Birmingham Walk (55 miles) which took place throughout in a downpour of rain; and his win in the Hastings—Brighton Race (38 miles). Our best wishes go with him to the Manchester—Blackpool Walk (50¼ miles), to be held on October 3rd. If Tommy wins this for the third year in succession the 100 guinea trophy presented by the Blackpool Corporation becomes his own property. Tommy has since done this and we congratulate him most heartily. C. E. Churcher C. E. Churcher new member (walker); one of the Churcher brothers H. G. Churcher H. G. e: South of the Thames Cross Country Championships
items.s: FORTHCOMING EVENTS. The running secretary's preview of the cross-country season from the Wimbledon headquarters, listing October fixtures, training nights and rail tickets. Welcome! members new and old, to our headquarters at Wimbledon. Those of you who troubled to read the back of your A.G.M. notices will be fully conversant with the real facts and it only remains for me to emphasize the enjoyments which one can derive from training over the country. Several packs go out, each under the leadership of a well seasoned runner and the veriest novice is well looked after in this respect. Even our track runners only, will do well to come along, for there is nothing better than this to improve one's stamina and general fitness. This is a view subscribed to by Tom Hampson, the A.A.A. 880 Yards Champion, while Tommy Scrimshaw is another who is often seen out at Wimbledon. Our fixture list is a full one and is on much the same lines as previous years. Many alterations have been suggested, but our Committee consider we are well served by our present opponents and fixtures. New opposition will be met in the matches v. the Metropolitan Police A.C., and members should make a note to come along to Imber Court and sample the hospitality of the "men in blue," and also enjoy the comforts of their fine Pavilion and dressing rooms. As usual, we have our 3 Miles Road Running Handicap race on October 3rd, and I hope to see a large entry, in view of the Round Ilford Relay race, which will be held a fortnight later. Also on that date, namely the 17th, we shall entertain the Ealing Harriers to a run over our home course at Wimbledon. On October 24th, we have the Metropolitan Police coming to Wimbledon, not with any serious intentions, I hope, and a match over our 5 miles course will take place. The 31st sees the first of the Inter-Club races v. Ashcombe A.C. and Thames Valley Harriers being held from T.V.H. headquarters at Hounslow. All members should support this fixture, for not only does the all-to-score rule operate in the races, but in view of the South of the Thames race to be held a fortnight later, all prospective team men should be getting racing fit. Cheap rail tickets for use between Clapham Junction and Wimbledon, also from Vauxhall, can be obtained from M. W. J. Fish or at the Club room on training nights. Our training quarters during the week—Tuesday and Thursday are the nights—are at the "Rising Sun," Ebury Bridge Road, which is quite near Victoria Station and also easily accessible from the other side of the river. With our increasing mmbership we should have large fields out every Saturday, and anyone who requires information as to reaching Wimbledon or any other particulars, if they will drop me a line I shall be pleased to do my best to assist them. All entries and enquiries to E. A. Duffett, Running Hon. Sec., 1 Raymead Avenue, Thornton Heath. items.label: October 1931
items.sum: Letter from the new President thanking members for electing him and praising the club's team spirit.
items.s: My Dear Bels, Letter from the new President thanking members for electing him and praising the club's team spirit. My Dear Bels, In thanking you most cordially for electing me to a position so honourable as the Presidency of the Belgrave Harriers, I would like to tender additional thanks to you for giving me such a galaxy of enthusiastic, conscientious and industrious officers to perform all the necessary duties. Tried and capable fellow-workers fill every position, and consequently I am confident that with their co-operation the prestige of the Club will not only be upheld during the coming year, but that successes will be achieved, surpassing any yet recorded by the Club. We have progressed so steadily and persistently for some years past, that the impetus worked up must assuredly soon be sufficient to urge us away in front of all our rivals. We have athletes of proved ability and of wonderful promise, at all distances, in both our running and walking sections; whilst our field events section has progressed out of all knowledge during the past twelve months, and now threatens to rival its elder brothers. But, chief of all, the team spirit pervades the minds of our members increasingly, as the years roll by. During almost 20 happy years of membership I have always had many club-mates who consistently placed the club before "self," and to whom individual honours were of small value when compared with team-wins and team-championships. The "Belgravian" and all the club officers are intent on fostering this spirit, and I am sure that the percentage of such whole-hearted Club members is higher now than ever. And it is this, more than anything, that assures me of the continuance of our rising fortune. J. B. BELCHAMBER, President, Belgrave Harriers. J. B. Belchamber J. B. BELCHAMBER President; almost 20 years a member J. B. BELCHAMBER

items.label: October 1931
items.sum: Report and full result of the club's opening 5 miles handicap walk of the winter season on a new course, won by C. E. Churcher on his club debut.
items.s: THE OPENING WALK. Report and full result of the club's opening 5 miles handicap walk of the winter season on a new course, won by C. E. Churcher on his club debut. Our first event of the Winter season—the usual 5 miles Handicap with the competitors going off in advance of the scratch man, according to their handicap allowance—attracted 28 starters. This is a record entry for this particular event and it is to be hoped that it is the forerunner of a record season. Despite our large field, several familiar faces were missing, notably Tommy Green (who was winning the Manchester—Blackpool Walk the same afternoon), Fred Rickards, H. F. King, J. F. King, J. G. Scamell, J. C. Bidgood, P. Khlopin, R. C. Hillier, F. E. Bentley and several others. Circumstances prevented them from competing in the handicap, but their assistance will be forthcoming during the season, and there is no doubt that in numbers and performance the season we have just commenced should eclipse even those of the past. It was found impossible to use our old course on the roads across Wimbledon Common, which are in a disgraceful condition, and so we planned a new course, consisting of a lap of a portion of the Common at the start and finish, the middle section being over our now familiar Coombe Hill—Cambridge Road—Pepys Hill circuit. Jack Thomas, closely followed by A. Martin, started first and soon the rest of the competitors were chasing our veteran members. The eventual winner was Charlie Churcher, thus scoring in his first Club race. Bert Field, apparently very fit from his excellent "Brighton" performance, finished second; and Harry Churcher accomplished the actual fastest time and was placed third. Of the newcomers, D. E. Brown impressed in his first race as likely to do very well in the future; whilst Heather and McCarthy were both responsible for creditable performances. The full result is appended and, considering that the race took place on the second Saturday of the season, before our walkers could hope to be anywhere near fit, it may be considered very satisfactory. We congratulate the Churcher brothers upon being so prominently placed in their first race with us, and look forward to the time when they will be helping our teams to gain further honours. items.sum: Report and result of the club's Three Miles Road Race of 3 October 1931, in which H. E. Footer set a new course record of 14 min. 23 sec. and W. Hazael-Harrison won the handicap; the report says 39 started, the result says 43 started.
e: Belgrave Harriers Three Miles Road Race
items.s: THE THREE MILES ROAD RACE. Report and result of the club's Three Miles Road Race of 3 October 1931, in which H. E. Footer set a new course record of 14 min. 23 sec. and W. Hazael-Harrison won the handicap; the report says 39 started, the result says 43 started. I am annoyed with Footer and Penny. When I put in print such a statement as "It is now Club history how Penny . . . . set up such a record that neither he, nor anyone else, can ever hope to equal," I don't anticipate its contradiction on the first possible occasion. And that is exactly what these two did on Saturday, October 3rd. In writing this account I hardly know what to say. Perhaps two tables will be more eloquent— TABLE I. Showing the lowering of the course record. 1924 A. E. Elliott 15 min. 9 sec. 1928 H. S. H. Cook 15 min. 0 sec. (H. E. Footer and W. A. Rice also beat 15.09). 1929 S. H. Warboys 14 min. 55 sec. (J. E. Flower did 14.59). 1930 A. W. Penny 14 min. 28 sec. (A. Allum and S. H. Warboys did 14.45). 1931 H. E. Footer 14 min. 23 sec. (A. W. Penny did 14.24). TABLE II. Showing the number of runners to beat 15.00. 1929 2 (S. H. Warboys, J. E. Flower). 1930 3 (A. W. Penny, S. H. Warboys, A. Allum). 1931 5 (H. E. Footer, A. W. Penny, J. E. Flower, C. T. Carter, S. H. Warboys). The most outstanding conclusion from the above summaries is the rapid improvement of our runners in the last two years. Of course, road running is by no means the same as cross-country running, but, nevertheless, those who put up good times in a road race usually perform creditably over the plough. Now, in 1930 and 1931 we were placed in the Southern. In view of the tables above, am I too optimistic in thinking that we shall be first in 1932? Allum, Penny, Footer and Warboys are all capable of getting in the first dozen. To return to the road race. The weather was perfect and quite a good proportion of the 39 who started had been in training several weeks for this event. These two facts, plus the general improvement of the running that is so evident, account for the excellent performances. As already stated, five runners beat fifteen minutes, and no less than nine others beat sixteen minutes, scratch time, and only seven men took more than 17 minutes, scratch time. As usual in this handicap the veteran G. Tyrer went off first, but this year he was off form and was caught fairly quickly. For a long time S.G.B. Wilson was in the lead, and it was only in the last half-mile that Hazel-Harrison and Miller went past him. The former has a typical road-running action, a very economical one, and this enabled him to run throughout the race at an even pace sufficient to give him first place in the handicap. It was Footer's fault that Miller finished only third, for Footer has no respect for reputations or records. From the beginning he started sprinting his way through; when he could sprint no longer he started running through, and when he had run himself out he commenced to fight his way through. I remember his passing me half-way round. As he came by I first caught sight of a chin which soon was followed by a face, determined and relentless, the face that Footer wears when racing, dancing and attending A.G.M.'s. When Footer combines fitness with this well-known desperate determination of his, records are bound to go, and so Footer now holds the course record until next year, when Allum or Penny will probably set up a new one. I am prepared for anything now ! It is a pity that so many did not start in this race. The reason given by many was that they did not want to start racing so soon in the season. This may be legitimate when made by those who are expected to be at their best for the Southern and National. It will be noticed, however, that with the exception of Allum, who had not completely recovered from his injury, all our team men turned out. Without wishing to give offence, I should like to warn Belgravians against cultivating that superior aloofness from racing that is being encouraged so much by some authorities nowadays. Last year in this event a Club champion was sporting enough to finish, although he was last, and this year our captain was in the last three. L.E.F. RESULT. 43 started. Pos. Name Act.
