items.sum: Review of the end of the 1932 track season: losing the Inter-Club Relay Shield to Mitcham, the juniors' wins at Croydon, winning the S.A.A.L., beating the London Athletic Club, the final club meeting and the match with the Police and Navy at Imber Court.
items.s: THE TRACK SEASON'S CLOSE. Review of the end of the 1932 track season: losing the Inter-Club Relay Shield to Mitcham, the juniors' wins at Croydon, winning the S.A.A.L., beating the London Athletic Club, the final club meeting and the match with the Police and Navy at Imber Court. The past track season seems a long way behind us, but in view of the interesting fixtures we had at the end of the summer it would not be right to forget to make a few remarks and comments on these. On July 20th, the last of the Inter-Club Relay meetings was held at the “News of the World” Track, Mitcham. Up to this meeting we had a lead of 4 points for the Shield and were fairly optimistic of retaining it. Such was not to be, however, and with Mitcham A.C. securing premier honours in the 4 x 100, yards, 4 x 880 yards and 1 mile Team race, they eventually beat us by 1 point for the Shield. We must heartily congratulate the Mitcham boys on their success. This is the first time we have lost the Shield since its inception, so you can see that Mitcham have earned their just reward after many seasons' striving. They showed exceptional keenness; even when behind on points they still turned out and ran their hardest to pull us back. Whether our own members considered their early lead sufficient and so decided to rest on their laurels, I don't know, but teams were certainly not up to the Belgrave standard in the later matches. Our Juniors, however, did a little towards regaining our lost prestige by fairly swamping the Junior opposition of Croydon and Mitcham. This meeting was held at Croydon on July 28th, and we won all three events, namely, 3 x 100 yards, 3 x 200 yards and 880 yards Team race. They say our Juniors of to-day are the Seniors of to-morrow, so we hope they carry on their good work in the future. On July 23rd the last event of the S.A.A.L., namely, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, was run off at the Fire Brigade meeting held at Stamford Bridge. To win the League we had to beat S.L.H. and this we did. Highgate H. finished first in the Relay with ourselves second, Herne Hill H. third, South London H. fourth and Ilford A.C. fifth. Our team, Michael, Jarvis, Basford and Read, ran very well and together with the other men who have represented us so ably in these League events, deserve our very best thanks. To win the Southern Amateur Athletic League, and then to lose the “Doris” and “Inter-Club Relay” is inconsistency at its best. On August 13th we had the great pleasure, I was almost going to say honour, of appearing at Stamford Bridge in opposition to the London Athletic Club in a series of match events. The L.A.C as you know, have come down to Battersea Park for the last three years to oppose us in match events, and as yet we have not had the pleasure of beating them. However, everything comes to those who wait, and we duly had our revenge at this meeting on August 13th. Rather an ominous date from the L.A.C.'s point of view, doubly so now that the Bridge is to be transformed into a “Dogs' Home,” but they were the first to congratulate us on the victory. It was a most exciting match and with two events to be decided we were level on points. We forged ahead in these, however, and recording two 5 to 1 wins won the match, 28 pts. to 20 pts. The best performance of our men was Arthur Penny's 2 Miles win in 9 min. 53 sec., and he fairly ran away from the rest of the field who included J. G. Helps, the well-known Midland and Birchfield H. crack. We hope the L.A.C. will find a new home and trust to have the pleasure of renewing their acquaintance there, and also wish them every success when they oppose us in the annual match at Battersea Park Track next year. Our final Club meeting of the season was held at Battersea Park on August 17th. A notable feature of the racing was the smallness of the fields, and it looked as if our members had had a surfeit of racing events and so were disinclined to support our final meeting. Jack Holder won the Sprint in fast time off 6½ yards and displayed fine dash for so late in the season. F. D. Haly was placed second and young Jack Crilly third, so the latter thus concluded a very successful season. The 1320 yards Handicap resulted in a win for Harry Shields, and off a liberal mark he led Tom Pritchard and A. T. Jordan home.. Jordan, who was a member of last season's Surrey Youths C.C. Championship winning team, ran well and kept off a determined challenge by Bill Rice. Tom Scrimshaw displayed some fine running in the 440 yards Handicap and the final was a great race to watch. Tosh, off 1 yard, kept Scrimshaw outside him for the first 100 yards, ran I should think in record time, and then Tommy went up and got on to the heels of Michael, who had taken the lead. Mike, however, had more finishing power than Tommy, and won the race with Charlie Jones filling third place. The 2 Miles Walk was won by Charlie Churcher, with E. C. Heather and Charlie Speechley dead-heating for second place, in a red-hot finish. Our final fixture of the track season was a very charming match at Imber Court, the Metropolitan Police Headquarters. Our opponents were the Police and the Royal Navy and Marines, Portsmouth, and a series of flat and field events were decided on the team and relay principle. Some very good sport was seen and the outstanding performance was perhaps Tommy Scrimshaw's run in the 3 x 440 yards relay. He took over about 30 yards behind the Naval man, with “Jock” Simpson, the well-known hurdler and runner some 10 yards behind himself. Tom not only caught the leader and won by about 20 yards but he also left Simpson well in the rear. The result of a most interesting match was a win for the Police by 2 points with ourselves and Navy dead-heating with 21 points each. Of the 11 events we won five, the Police four, and the Navy two, but the better packing with regard to placings by the Police deservedly gained them the day. Then followed Tea and Dancing and everyone who made the trip agreed it was our best fixture of the season, and should certainly be held again next year. Our thanks are due to the members who came along and turned out for us. Some competed in as many as four events, owing to our shortage of men, and it is pleasing to know that there are still members left who retain some of the old-time Belgrave spirit and are ready to turn out and assist the Club even if there are no medals or prizes as their reward. So closed yet another Track Season and the Club as a whole can consider it a most successful one. True the smaller Shields were lost, but the winning of the S.A.A.L. 1st Division fully compensated us for this, and moreover our members were well to the fore in the various Open Relay and Team races. Perhaps a little less concentration on the latter and a bit more on the various Inter-Club events would be more pleasant to a few of us, but in these days of striving after personal gain I suppose it is only natural for members to expect to receive a little in return for the months of hard training. items.label: August 1932
items.sum: Report of the London to Brighton walk of 10 September 1932, in which Belgrave won the team race and the Edward Knott Memorial Shield with three walkers in the first five, with the result and team placings; the result prints Whitlock's second-place time as “8 1 6” (faster than the winner's) and Green's as 8 14 59 against 8 hrs. 14 min. 50 secs. in the text.
items.s: THE BRIGHTON WALK. Report of the London to Brighton walk of 10 September 1932, in which Belgrave won the team race and the Edward Knott Memorial Shield with three walkers in the first five, with the result and team placings; the result prints Whitlock's second-place time as “8 1 6” (faster than the winner's) and Green's as 8 14 59 against 8 hrs. 14 min. 50 secs. in the text. Describing how seven Belgravians fared in the historic London—Brighton race; of the manner in which a bus-load of supporters accompanied the event; of how the team race was won and the “Edward Knott” Memorial Shield regained by the Club; of the unparalleled achievement of having three Belgravians placed in the first five; and several other matters of interest. September 10th—up with the dawn and away to Great Smith Street Baths, Westminster, where 82 walkers prepared to start in the classic race to Brighton promoted so efficiently by the Surrey Walking Club. We had eight entrants; and our sympathy went out to Bert Field, who, after a three months' conscientious preparation, had the misfortune to sustain a slight foot injury on the eve of the race and had to content himself as a spectator from the bus-top. It was a great disappointment to such an enthusiastic walker, and we can only hope that future races will bring him his due reward. This reduced our number of starters to seven, and it was evident from the start that our walkers intended playing an important part in the race. At Croydon, Green and Rickards of ours, Ludlow (Derby W. & A.C.) and D. Gum (Essex Eagles) were leading the field. Our third man, Bentley, had made a good start and was walking easily in fifth position. Hillier was tenth, and our others, Khlopin, Holman and Wattam—once again making his annual journey from Lincolnshire for the race—were further back, taking things steadily. The forward position of our first four men was very encouraging at this point, but we have long learned not to build up false hopes in a race of this description in the early stages. And so our bus moved on to Merstham, the occupants wearing quietly optimistic smiles. After a while along came the walkers. Our two, with Ludlow, were still in the lead, Bentley remained fifth and Hillier was in 11th position. At Redhill, positions were practically the same. Good! And so on to Crawley, feeling very satisfied! And then came the rumour, travelling as fast as bad news is supposed to, do, that our Olympic Champion, Tommy Green, was “having a bad time.” And on this occasion Dame Rumour was no liar! Ludlow had very wisely taken advantage of our champion's indisposition to open up a gap and at “The George,” Crawley, led by over three minutes from Fred Rickards, who was now second. Tommy was nearly two minutes behind Fred, but seemed to be getting into his stride again. Bentley, walking his first race over this course, and at this distance, was still quite unperturbed and walking strongly in sixth position. Whitlock, of the Metropolitan W.C., who had been walking a very steady race, was now becoming prominent and had taken fourth position. At Crawley we also had a further disappointment, for shortly before this point Reg. Hillier had sustained a severe attack of cramp which necessitated his retirement from the race, and allowed Paul Khlopin to become our 4th man. He was some distance back, and it seemed our chances of a team win were slipping—but we still had confidence in the ability of our men to regain the Shield. Between Handcross and Bolney we had further evidence of the strong Club spirit which binds our members together; and of the spirit of self-sacrifice of his own chances which Fred Rickards has shown on many occasions in the past. Between these two points Fred acted as pacemaker to Green in his endeavour to take him up to the leader and although he was denied this pleasure, he had the satisfaction of helping Tommy along and reducing the gap between first and second men. From Bolney to the finish, however, Ludlow was faster than our man, and eventually Green was passed in the last few miles by H. Whitlock. This, of course, gave Tommy third position, with Fred Rickards fourth, and Fred Bentley fifth. Three in five! Good work, and as the first two men were individual entrants our walkers gave us a perfect start in the team scoring with 1, 2 and 3. A journey back along the road showed Paul Khlopin to be our fourth man still, and in a position which only had to be retained to give us winning honours. He was apprised of this fact and announced his intention of doing all that was expected of him! And so he did, and we ran out winners of the team race with 21 points to the 25 of the promoters, Surrey Walking Club. Last year's winners, Birmingham W.C., did not compete this year, but it is very unlikely that they would have beaten us after the wonderful start given to our scoring team by Green, Rickards and Bentley. Three men within 8 hrs. 34 mins.! This can never have been accomplished before by three members of any other Club! Of GREEN'S “failure” (if to walk the course in 8 hrs. 14 min. 50 secs. can be so described) we have but little to say, except that it can hardly be expected of any human being that he should be at the peak of condition and fitness (and this would certainly have been necessary to even extend Ludlow on his walking in this race) after changing Californian climate for that of this country within a few days of the race. And trans-continental rail travel, followed by days on an Atlantic liner cannot be considered the best of training for an arduous race. There is no need for excuses for Tommy, for his future performances will prove that he is still the most consistent distance walker this country has ever had, and that we may still expect broken records and amazing versatility from him for many years to come. Incidentally, 8 hrs. 15 mins. can only have been beaten on about half a dozen occasions in this race. Green has done so on three occasions (in successive years) and in 1929 was only a few seconds outside. Of Ludlow's performance we have the highest admiration, and extend to him our heartiest congratulations. He has fully deserved his win and new record over the course. On many occasions he has had to play second fiddle to Green, often in times which a few years ago would have been acclaimed as sensational new records. To quote from the November, 1930, issue of the “Belgravian”: “In the Manchester—Blackpool race Ludlow was again second, finishing in 7 hrs. 44 mins. 46 2-5 secs., or only 5 mins. 16 secs. behind Green, the winner. Accordingly he walked 50 miles in about 10 minutes less than the figures standing as a World's record and yet was beaten by the decisive margin of 5 furlongs. Surely this is an experience that has no parallel in the history of athletics. “So we are pleased to record our warm and unstinted appreciation of the splendid achievements of this persistent and plucky runner-up. He is young and the highest honours should surely reward his efforts in the future.” These prophetic words appeared in our columns two years ago, and now that they have been realized, we have much pleasure in extending our congratulations and best wishes to the Derby man. RICKARDS accomplished his best yet over the course and it is far and away the best accomplished by a Police or Service walker. Fred adopted different tactics this year in holding on to the leaders to the half distance and the experiment pleased him and us! In fact, next year he may well start and finish with the leaders! It is difficult to praise the first attempt of BENTLEY too much. To finish fifth, in the fine time of 8 hrs. 33 mins. 54 secs., is a performance which hundreds of seasoned walkers would remember with pride for the remainder of their lives. There is need for Fred to do this, however, for he has years and years in front of him, and may yet be the first walker to beat eight hours! It is interesting to note, and also a tribute to our strength this year, that Bentley's performance gains for him a third medal in the Club Long Distance Championship. In 1919, 1921, 1923, 1924, 1926, 1928 (to mention a few dates) his time would have actually won the race! This year fifth, and third in the Club Championship! So has our Club standard improved and so may it continue to improve! PAUL KHLOPIN completed our team and now has the distinction of having been a member of victorious running and walking Club teams. He earned the Club's thanks by pluckily and tenaciously “sticking to it,” and in this connection we owe thanks to Paul's attendant, who played an important part in the winning of the race. He confided to me that Paul had enough tea to enable him to swim the distance, and when he couldn't have tea (whisper it!) he had vodka and water or something very similar. A few places behind came HOLMAN, who made a creditable first appearance in this race, and WATTAM, a couple of minutes outside 10 hours. A. O. TOOKEY, walking in his first-claim Polytechnic H. colours, also made his debut, and F. W. CHANDLER, who has now joined us, gained useful experience. We owe a deep debt of gratitude to the cyclist attendants who accompanied our men, for it must be almost as great a test of endurance to ride over the course at slow speed as it is to walk it at 5—6 miles per hour. We offer them our very sincere thanks and appreciate all they did to help our men along; and for their very real contribution towards the Club success. Our supporters were delighted with our team's win and went home in a very joyful mood. The “Edward Knott” Memorial Shield went home with us on the bus, as did some of the competitors and attendants with cycles on top; so demonstrating the great value of a conveyance such as ours. A pack of cards appeared from someone's capacious pockets and we were amused (and paid for our amusement!) at C. Cook, Esq. calling “Twos” on Ace, King, Queen, Jack! Really Charlie, at 68 you should have learnt to be cautious and avoid risks! The appended results reflect credit on all who participated, and all who helped to make the race a success from our point of view. Green, Rickards and Bentley take 1st, 2nd and 3rd medals in the Club Long Distance Championship as above, Green winning the “Belgrave” Cup for the fourth year in succession. F. items.sum: Report of the Annual General Meeting at the Rising Sun on 27 September 1932, with the reports, a rule change on subscriptions and the officers elected.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING. Report of the Annual General Meeting at the Rising Sun on 27 September 1932, with the reports, a rule change on subscriptions and the officers elected. The Annual General Meeting was held on September 27th at “The Rising Sun” and a good crowd assembled to hear the Hon. Treasurer's and Hon. Secretary's Reports and to elect officials for the ensuing year. The meeting opened by the Hon. Secretary reading the notice convening the meeting and the minutes of the last Annual Meeting, which were approved. The Hon. Secretary then made his report on the year's activities. He expressed the Club's regret at the deaths of J. N. Thomas and H. Wright; and then quickly surveyed the past year's performances. He commented in particular on our representatives' success at Los Angeles and of the fine running of T. H. Scrimshaw in England and Paris; and of several other performances, notably the winning of the Southern Amateur Athletic League, which had enhanced the Club's reputation. The Hon. Secretary's report was approved, and was followed by a statement of financial affairs by the Hon. Treasurer. He disclosed a favourable state of affairs, but appealed to members to lighten the work and expense necessitated by those who delayed paying their subscriptions. His report was adopted, and one of the Joint Hon. Editors called upon for a “Gazette” report. He pointed out that the loss on this branch of the Club's activity was almost identical with that incurred last year; and he asked for the co-operation of all members both in the matter of prompt payment, and in the submission of literary contributions to the columns of the “Belgravian.” His report was accepted, and the meeting then considered the proposal from the Committe that in future members joining after March 28th should pay full subscriptions and not half-rate as hitherto. It was pointed out that anyone joining the Club at the commencement of the Track season had a very fine programme of events arranged for them, and as this part of the season is the heaviest on the Club's funds it was only right that he should pay in full for the privilege of membership. After discussion the proposal was approved. The election of Officers then took place, with the following results:— President: J. B. Belchamber. Vice-Presidents: As last year with the addition of F. M. Stone. Hon. Secretary: W. L. Bayliss. Hon. Treasurer: W. H. Hare. Walking Hon. Secretary: A. A. Harley. Team Hon. Secretary (Running): H. Parker. Social Hon. Secretary: W. A. Rice. Captains: W. G. items.label: August 1932
items.sum: Walking notes looking ahead to the 1932-33 winter fixtures, reporting Tommy Green's Norwich to Ipswich record and fourth Manchester to Blackpool win, and A. H. G. Pope's world walking records.
e: Belgrave Harriers seven miles Open Walk
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes looking ahead to the 1932-33 winter fixtures, reporting Tommy Green's Norwich to Ipswich record and fourth Manchester to Blackpool win, and A. H. G. Pope's world walking records. Once again the Winter season is upon us and it is with optimistic eyes that we look forward to a very successful season. We have numbers, enthusiasm, ability, the will to win; and the opportunities to prove these assertions are coming along in the form of Open Races, Match events and, last but not least, Championships. There is no reason why this should not be a record season for us. It depends upon ourselves. If each individual is determined to do his utmost, to persevere, to train conscientiously, our teams will undoubtedly have a record season. It is for us to make season 1932-33 a memorable one in Belgravian (and Road Walking) history! * * * * * We start off with the applause given our Brighton Walk team win still ringing in our ears to give us inspiration. The details of this race, with its unprecedented 1, 2, 3 start to the team score, appear elsewhere, and it is hoped there are many more equally creditable wins to come our way. The first Open event of the season is that promoted by the Highgate Harriers on October 29th. In view of the travelling difficulties experienced in past years in getting to De Bohun Farm, Southgate, the promoters have obtaned permission to hold their race in Regent's Park, from St. Dunstan's Headquarters. We shall be well represented and should be well to the fore. A fortnight later (November 12th) Enfield A.C. hold their usual race over a seven miles course; and on this occasion the “Berman Cup,” awarded to the first scratch team, will be up for competition. Enfield are holders of this trophy at the moment, and it would be a splendid start to regain this Cup over the holders' own course. What about it? On November 19th the Metropolitan Police A.A. visit us at Wimbledon for an “all-to-score” team race; and the following Saturday our own promotion—a seven miles Open Walk—will take place from Wimbledon. Our race is one of the oldest established Open events at this distance, and we have always been fortunate in attracting a large entry. It is hoped that this year our event will be as successful as ever, and that every active Belgrave walker will send in his entry to the Hon. Secretary as early as possible. * * * * * It was good news, but certainly not unexpected news, to know that Tommy Green, a fortnight after his gruelling race to Brighton, broke the Norwich to Ipswich (42 miles) record by over 23 minutes, and so proved that he is as strong and capable as ever. The old record was created by another Belgrave walker, Stanley A. Manning, in 1923, and altogether he won this event three times. It was good to see Stanley on the Brighton Road this year as an onlooker, and to see him turn out from St. John's Hall for the first training spin of the season. Tommy followed this up a week later by winning the Manchester to Blackpool (50¼ miles) Walk for the fourth time in succession. He has already won one 100-guinea trophy outright, presented by the Blackpool Corporation, and it looks as if he is after another one to make the pair! * * * * * We heartily congratulate A. H. G. Pope, of Woodford Green A.C. upon his recent performances in creating six new World's walking records at the White City Track. We, who struggle round the track with difficulty can appreciate better than anyone the merit of the new figures. Well done, Pope! Len Fletcher, T. Green and H. G. Churcher were invited to participate in the Record attempt. Only the last-named was able to accept the invitation, and he did well enough to make us think that one day he may be making a serious attempt to improve still further upon the new records! * * * * * All enquiries and entries should be addressed to A. items.label: August 1932
items.sum: Running notes on the coming cross-country season, advice to junior runners, the Winter Fixture List and the Inter-Club race of 22 October.
items.s: RUNNING NOTES. Running notes on the coming cross-country season, advice to junior runners, the Winter Fixture List and the Inter-Club race of 22 October. Without doubt the runners can look forward with confidence to another successful season, there being several good youngsters determined to obtain further honours for the Club. They will have their first opportunity in the South of Thames District Race on November 12th. We are again competing in the Round Ilford Relay Race and hope to follow up our success of last year with another win. A word of advice to our junior runners would not be amiss here. Keep with your pack leader but do not try to race him and always finish your training spin “easing up” and feeling that you have plenty of reserve energy left in you. In short, never race whilst training. The Winter Fixture List and Handbook is now in the Printers' hands and will be issued shortly and runners will find themselves well catered for. Several “B” Team fixtures have been arranged and it is hoped that these will be well supported. Don't forget that all runners score in the Inter-Club races, so let us have a record turn-out on October 22nd. There is also a sealed handicap in conjunction. The Hon. Secretary will be pleased to accept entries. His address is:— W. L. Bayliss, 71 Ravensbury Road, S.W.18. W. L. Bayliss W. L. Bayliss Hon. Good entries were received for both events, and in both races there was ample evidence of continued improvement and of successes to come. The run went to S. T. Ring, who was in the Club walking teams last year; whilst J. G. Coleman, who started his Club career as a runner, showed great improvement in winning the walk. A newcomer of considerable promise, E. Saunders, was second in the run, with Alec Traquair taking third place. Saunders, Shields, Taylor, and our Erith friends, Mains and Shaw, all showed up well and will be strong challengers for premier places in our teams and worthy representatives of the Club. Arthur Penny recorded fastest time and we expect him to be very prominent over the country this year. Bert Field was another to show improvement in taking second place in the Walk Handicap, and H. G. Churcher (third) indicated something of the value he will be to our teams. T. W. Green accomplished fastest time from the scratch mark. items.sum: Social notes on the opening social evening at Wimbledon on 8 October 1932, the next on 5 November and the dance programme at Wandsworth Baths Hall from 16 November.
items.s: SOCIAL. Social notes on the opening social evening at Wimbledon on 8 October 1932, the next on 5 November and the dance programme at Wandsworth Baths Hall from 16 November. The Social Season started at Wimbledon on Saturday, October 8th, and proved a success. Over 70 stayed to tea and 40 to 50 others came along later. Incidentally, I should be glad to see more at tea. It makes a longer evening with your Club-mates, and helps to meet the expenses of the arrangements, for the nominal sixpence charged at the door to late-comers does not nearly cover the expense of hiring the hall and a suitable band. The next Social evening is on November 5th, so come along, and come an hour or so earlier and join in tea with the boys and their friends. Our Dance programme commences at Wandsworth Baths Hall on Wednesday, November 16th. In past years the Club has held some very successful dances at this Hall and there is no reason why the former successes should not be repeated. Tables are arranged round the Hall in “Palais de Danse” style and so creates a sociable atmosphere. It is necessary to have your tickets (1/6 each) before the day, as it is not permissible for money to be taken at the door, and members should not attempt to sell tickets to strangers outside the Hall. Enquiries, etc., to W. A. Rice, 36 Ascalon Street, S.W.8. W. A. Rice W. A. Rice takes dance enquiries; address in the issue W. A. RICE Wimbledon Wandsworth Baths Hall

items.label: November 1932
items.sum: Club notes: J. F. King's marriage, Arthur Allum's recovery, Committee changes, the Holt team v. Cambridge University, the youths' team win, new members, the Boxing Day meeting, the building fund and F. A. Arrowsmith's appointment.
items.s: Club notes: J. F. King's marriage, Arthur Allum's recovery, Committee changes, the Holt team v. Cambridge University, the youths' team win, new members, the Boxing Day meeting, the building fund and F. A. Arrowsmith's appointment. Heartiest congratulations to J. F. King upon his recent marriage. Joe has been winning Sussex walking championships for many years past and has represented the Club with distinction on many occasions. We wish Mr. and Mrs. King the best of luck in their new venture. * * * * * We are glad to see Arthur Allum about again, apparently none the worse for his recent operation for mastoid. It came as a severe blow to us to learn that our Cross-country International had been rushed away to hospital to undergo a critical operation. Happily his strong constitution and bodily fitness enabled him to pull through quickly; and now he is keenness itself, and anxious to be up and doing. He has great hopes of getting fit in time for the "Southern"; and it goes without saying that we all trust he will be successful in his efforts; and that his enforced stay in hospital will not prove an insuperable handicap. * * * * * Owing to the resignation from the Committee of K. B. O'Kell, who is now living at Dagenham and finds it impossible to keep in close touch with Club affairs, a vacancy occurred on the Committee. It was also decided to fill the vacancy caused by the election of H. Parker to the position of Asst. Hon. Secretary, thus becoming an ex-officio member of Committee. To fill these two positions, as empowered by the Club rules, H. E. Footer and H. W. Shields were appointed members of Committee. In resigning his position, Ken O'Kell, ex Club captain and champion, makes it quite clear that there is no diminution in his interest and enthusiasm for the Club, but he feels that with so many keen men anxious to serve the Club, and able to do so, and with himself uncertain of being a regular attendant at Committee meetings, it is only fair that he should withdraw in favour of someone else not handicapped in the way he is. No doubt we shall have an occasional scheme from him as in the past just to show that his thoughts are still with us, and we can be certain that he will show up when the Championships come along! * * * * * J. E. Flower, H. E. Footer and A. W. Penny were recently honoured by being invited to run as members of Mr. E. J. Holt's team versus Cambridge University. The race took place over 7½ miles of very heavy country and was won by the visiting team—largely due to brilliant running by two of ours, Footer and Penny, who finished equal first. Flower also scored for the winning team, and so our triumvirate showed the Cambridge men that our colours were worthily worn; and our men's performances in keeping with the reputation our cross-country men have been building up for some years past. * * * * * Congratulations to Messrs. D. Martin, G. R. Chantler, J. E. Barnett and E. Pointer, who formed our team which won the Surrey County Youths' Race at Wimbledon on December 3rd. * * * * * We have pleasure in welcoming to membership F. J. Bankhead, A. Beavan, G. E. Chaffin, C. F. Clark, R. B. Gilson, J. Hewitt, E. W. Hayward, W. H. Piggott, A. R. Wright, and extend to them our usual good wishes and hopes for future successes. * * * * * You'll be along to the Boxing Day Meeting, at Battersea Park Track? We are always glad to see members whose active days, perhaps, are over; or who are unable to find the time for training, and this meeting of ours gives a splendid opportunity for re-union. All active men are urged to send along their entries at once to the Hon. Secretaries concerned. * * * * * The Hon. Treasurer has Club vests, ties, badges, etc., for sale as per notice in the Club handbook. * * * * * The Christmas season would appear to be a very fine time to make your contribution to the "Belgrave Building Fund." The number of halfpennies is gradually growing, but out Hon. Treasurer won't be happy till he receives your little bit! * * * * * We congratulate F. A. Arrowsmith upon his recent appointment as Hon. Secretary of the University of London Athletic Union. Arrowsmith has represented us creditably on several occasions in past seasons, and it hoped that his secretarial work will not prevent him from turning out for us during the next track season, although the demands on his services by the University are bound to be heavy. He was entered in the Sussex County Team at the last Inter-Counties Meeting, and still has plenty of time in which to gain further honours. J. F. King J. F. items.s: WITH THE RUNNERS. Report of Belgrave's win in the Ilford Road Relay, with record runs by Footer and Penny, and the stage and team result (the third stage runner is printed as F. Shields in the text and H. W. Shields in the table). "Micky Walker" commences this month's comments on racing exploits with a description of THE ROUND-ILFORD RELAY. Once again the Belgrave Harriers have proven their capabilities in producing yet another winning team in this year's Ilford Road Relay. Despite adverse weather conditions, the Belgrave boys tore up the Ilford course from start to finish in one long burst of brilliant running. A stiffish wind was making itself felt as Carter took off on the first relay, but nothing deterred, he went forward to present his team companions with the comfortable margin of a 200 yards lead, and establishing for himself the very pleasing time of 19 min. 25 sec. The challenge was then taken up by F. Webb who, let it be noticed, accomplished the not unfair time of 20 mins., under the handicap of making his own pace. A surprise was created in the third relay in the shape of F. Shields, a junior of no small merit who pulled out a remarkable run in 19 min. 51 sec. The name of this promising lad will not easily be forgotten in the inevitable after-the-race "inquest." C. Mains ran well with 19 min. 40 sec. to his credit, as also did J. E. Flower, Shaw and A. Taylor, their times being 20 min. 26 sec., 20 min. 38 sec., 20 min. 23 sec. respectively. W. Rice produced some of his old form which, however, was not too aged to enable him to secure the useful time of 19 min. 40 sec. Intense interest was caused in the race by H. E. Footer and A. Penny, two of the club's most prominent men, whose keen but friendly rivalry has always spurred each to greater things. Bounding with his customary zest, Footer made ground with every stride, and it was not surprising to learn that his last year's record was scattered to the four winds, with the vastly improved time of 18 min. 58 sec. to replace it. Last relay, and Penny keyed up to beat his rival at all costs. Running like one possessed, he reached the last quarter mile to the accompaniment of enthusiastic cries from numerous supporters, doing much to urge him on to even greater efforts. What a run! He finished faster than he started, showing the exceptional and almost incredible time of 18 min. 46 sec., thereby smashing the standing record by 4 sec. Altogether a most satisfying win, marked by many very meritorious individual performances, and a collective effort which gained further prestige for the Club, and an addition to the Club sideboard in the shape of the newly-awarded Cup, of which we become first holders. items.s: BELGRAVE HARRIERS v. EALING HARRIERS. Hon. Editor's report and full result of Ealing Harriers' win over Belgrave in a five-mile match at Wimbledon, 314 points to 352 (S. T. Ring's time is printed 25 52 between 29-minute times). The Hon. Editor fills the breach and writes on:— BELGRAVE HARRIERS v. EALING HARRIERS. While our first choice were away at Ilford winning the Relay promoted by the local Club, our remaining strength entertained the Ealing Harriers to a race over five miles at Wimbledon. Len Rollins had been detailed to write an account of this sporting match and had agreed to do so—nay, had volunteered—but next day, as we wandered through the highways and byways of Surrey (and whenever Footer led, the roadways!) he resigned his commission. It may be that the caustic enquiries asking how it was possible for man finishing 35th to describe the progress of a race had something to do with his action. Perhaps the Pride of the Rollins, or the Curse of the Footers, entered into it. Could it have been that he had a premonition of the following week when his friends sent him home from the Dance in odd shoes, one black and one tan; or was it just his natural slackness asserting itself? We must cease speculation, however, and bemoan the fact that we should have been deprived of what, we are sure, would have proved a model literary contribution. Having given the inner history of this affair, in strict confidence, of course, we will now pass on and become official once again. We congratulate our visitors most heartily, not only upon winning a close scoring match, but also upon having the first three men home. It was a most enjoyable fixture and we look forward to the return date on Ealing's course. W. Mitchell showed something of his old form in finishing fourth, and a return to his running of a few years back, when he was Club Champion, should greatly strengthen our team. Ring and Saunders again attracted attention by their prominent placings, whilst Frank Tame and H. J. Fletcher also showed that they will have to be considered later in the season. RESULT. items.s: INTER-CLUB RACE. Arthur Penny's report and result of the first Inter-Club run between Ashcombe A.C., Thames Valley H. and Belgrave, won individually by L. J. Cohen of Ashcombe with Belgrave easy team winners and H. D. Brown winning the handicap. Vice-Captain Arthur Penny gives his commentary on the first of the Inter-Club runs. INTER-CLUB RACE. ASHCOMBE A.C., THAMES VALLEY H., BELGRAVE H. A good crowd faced the starter on the occasion of the first of the Inter-Club runs held from our headquarters. Immediately H. S. Cook took the lead, closely followed by Carter, Jack Flower and W. S. Mitchell, all of the Bels. Going out towards the village, Cohen of Ashcombe crept up and took the lead when crossing the Golf Links. The runners were now beginning to thin out, but T.V.H. had a good crowd of their men with ours at this point. Beverley Brook was passed and the Kingsmere reached, and here one of our men, Cecil Mains, went to the front, but appeared to be doubtful of the course. From here to the finish he was pressed by Cohen, who eventually won by a few yards. Well run, Cohen and Mains! Bicknell was the first "Valley" man to finish (9th); but as the Bels. placed their fifteen to score in the first 18 positions, we ran out very easy winners of the race. Our "Juniors" ran well, and with conscientious training will greatly add to our strength. H. D. Brown well deserved his handicap win, showing minutes improvement over previous running. Harry Shields, in finishing fifth in the scratch race, deserved some sort of reward for this, probably his best yet, and was placed second in the handicap, with Bill Mitchell, our second man to finish, third, with an allowance of 1 min. 45 sec. items.s: THE SOUTH OF THE THAMES "JUNIOR." Harry Shields' report and result of the South of the Thames Junior cross-country race at Epsom on 12 November, where Belgrave's "A" team finished third behind Reading A.C. and R.N. & R.M. (Portsmouth). Harry Shields carries on with the good work and gives us his impression of THE SOUTH OF THE THAMES "JUNIOR." On Saturday, November 12th, three teams and a number of supporters made their way to Epsom for the South of the Thames District race. Some of those who represented us last year were no longer eligible, but on this occasion our "A" team finished third, one place better than last year. All our "A" team men got well away with the leaders, Frank Tame, in particular, doing well until a strained leg caused him to fall back. Eventually Jack Fletcher, showing fine judgment of pace, led our team in, finishing 13th, closely followed by Shaw 14th, Cecil Penny 18th, and Walker 20th. This shows fine packing, although perhaps a little further back than we could desire. Ring, formerly walking, showed up well, and among the "B" and "C" teams could be seen many who are certain to carry our colours with credit in future races. Both the winners, Reading A.C., and the second team, Royal Navy and Marines (Portsmouth) ran exceedingly well, both teams finishing their four men inside the first 11 position—splendid Our boys did well to take third place with such strong opposition. items.s: RUN v. METROPOLITAN POLICE A.A. The Walking Hon. Secretary's short account and result of Belgrave's easy win, 67 points to 188, in a run against the Metropolitan Police A.A., with J. E. Flower and H. W. Shields dead-heating for first. The Walking Hon. Secretary contributes a short account of the RUN v. METROPOLITAN POLICE A.A. We had a good muster of Police visitors, and our team was composed in the main of runners who have yet to make their places in our senior team secure. Two notable exceptions to this generalization are, of course, Club ex-champions in J. E. Flower and W. S. Mitchell. Our runners were soon to the fore, once the race started. Harry Shields was in the lead for some distance with Jack Flower a few yards behind; but from the Windmill home they strode in together with "Bill" Mitchell a few yards in the rear. Then came the first of our visitors in H. Dyke, a Kent County runner. Our remaining runners packed in well to secure for us a very easy win scoring 10 aside. RESULT. Pos. Name Club m. s. 1. J. E. items.sum: Joe Flower's report and result of the combined 7-a-side and 5-a-side match with Ealing H., Kensington A.C. and Mitcham A.C. from Ealing's headquarters, won by Ealing H. with Belgrave last in both; A. F. Mitchell was fourth and first Belgrave man home.
e: Belgrave v. Ealing H., Kensington A.C. and Mitcham A.C.
items.s: MATCH v. EALING H., KENSINGTON A.C. AND MITCHAM A.C. Joe Flower's report and result of the combined 7-a-side and 5-a-side match with Ealing H., Kensington A.C. and Mitcham A.C. from Ealing's headquarters, won by Ealing H. with Belgrave last in both; A. F. Mitchell was fourth and first Belgrave man home. Joe Flower has his say regarding the MATCH v. EALING H., KENSINGTON A.C. AND MITCHAM A.C. It is hoped that this fixture will be supported in a better manner in the future. The Ealing A.C., from whose headquarters this race was run, are a fine crowd of sportsmen and give our boys a very warm welcome both on the track and on the country. They have a great respect for the Belgrave Harriers so in future I appeal to our runners, especially new members, to make enquiries of their officers as to ways and means of travelling to the venue. This applies to all our away fixtures. It encourages the club spirit among ourselves, and gives our runners the opportunity of trying different country, which it is only way of building up a strong team of cross-country runners. To get back to the job of reporting the race. Forty-eight runners turned out, eight only being Belgrave, although in extenuation it must be pointed out that we had another fixture elsewhere on this day. It was decided to hold two races in one, that is to say, three clubs competed in a 7 aside scoring match, and four clubs in a 5 aside competition. In both events we were last, which can hardly be termed creditable. The most pleasing feature from our point of view was the forward running of A. F. Mitchell, who finished fourth in the race and was first man home for us. When one realizes that he was only just beaten by Edwards, of Ealing, who was fourth the previous week in the North of the Thames Junior race, we can say our man did very well for one who has had little racing experience. Ealing H. won both matches easily; and I would like to remind the Bels' that this is the third time in succession that they have beaten us. In fairness to them we must turn out in greater numbers and strength next time and then—well, wait till then! In conclusion, on behalf on those present, I would like to thank the Ealing H. for their hospitality and a good run. RESULT. Pos. Name Club m. s. 1. Pulleston M.A.C. 31 30 2. Johnson E.H. 31 40 3. items.s: CRANFORD INTER-CLUB RACE. Report of the Cranford inter-club run between T.V.H., Ashcombe and Belgrave H. on 25 November, won by Belgrave by three points with Carter first home. And so on to the CRANFORD INTER-CLUB RACE. The T.V.H., Ashcombe and Belgrave H. inter-club run took place on Saturday, November 25th, resulting in a win for the club by a narrow margin of three points. It is worthy of note that of the 15 representatives of the club, 10 to score, many were in prominence at the finish. The course was in typical cross-country condition and eminently suitable to our men, for Carter made the tape in very convincing fashion, with 100 yards or so to spare. Mitchell, showing his old form, dropped into third place, with those three promising juniors, C. Penny, F. Walker and H. Shields, who seem never to be far behind, making a useful backing—their place being 6th, 7th and 10th respectively. RESULT. Pos. Name Club m. s. 1. T. Carter B.H. 35 6 3. W. S. Mitchell B.H. 36 0 6. items.label: November 1932
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes: the Youths' team win in the Surrey County 3 miles race, prospects for the club 7 miles championship for the Blackstaffe Shield, and the Boxing Day Meeting.
items.s: THE HON. SECRETARY CALLING. The Hon. Secretary's notes: the Youths' team win in the Surrey County 3 miles race, prospects for the club 7 miles championship for the Blackstaffe Shield, and the Boxing Day Meeting. THE HON. SECRETARY CALLING. Hearty congratulations to our team which won the Surrey County 3 miles Youths' race at Wimbledon on Saturday, December 3rd. These youngsters have been very earnest in their training and well deserved their honours. As expected, D. Martin got well away with the leaders and running in very good style finished third in the team race. He was well supported by G. Chantler, who ran well to finish 4th, followed by J. Barnett, 8th, and E. Pointer, 13th. The result should certainly be a tonic to our Surrey Juniors who will compete in the Junior Championship (over 18 and under 21) at Putney Heath on January 21st. Now what of our 7 miles Championship for the "Blackstaffe Shield" on December 17. Arthur Allum, much to our regret and his disgust, will probably be a spectator. Arthur has just recovered from a serious operation to his ear and will not commence training for a few weeks. Footer and Penny, who are both running well, will no doubt be making the pace hot. They finished together at the head of the field in a match versus Cambridge University on November 26th. I suspect, however, that J. E. Flower, who is now commencing to shew his old form, and C. T. Carter will be troubling them. Then what of W. W. Mitchell? He is now training in earnest and if on form can worry the best men we have. With such a crowd of good boys as we have, anything may happen. Mains and Shaw tell me they are both keen on making a good show. This sounds encouraging with the "South of Thames" race in view. The form of H. Shields and A. J. Mitchell is very promising and I have no doubt that both of them will be giving us a pleasant surprises shortly. I look forward to a very interesting race. The approach of Christmas reminds us of our Boxing Day Meeting. The usual handicaps will be run and sprinters are specially urged to try and support this half Athletic, half Social Function. Please make an effort to turn up and meet your Club friends the morning after the night before. Entries can be posted or handed to W. L. Bayliss, the Hon. Secretary. D. Martin D. items.label: November 1932
items.sum: Walking notes on the opening of the winter season: team placings behind Enfield A.C., Tommy Green's form, H. Latter's handicap win and the improving juniors.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes on the opening of the winter season: team placings behind Enfield A.C., Tommy Green's form, H. Latter's handicap win and the improving juniors. WITH THE WALKERS. The Winter Season has opened quite successfully for us and we have certainly not gone back on last year's performances. Two of the three opening races have found us taking second place to Enfield A.C. in the scratch team races, but we have no doubt this state of affairs will alter as the season progresses in the same way as it did last year. We have had one winning and two second handicap teams in three races despite rapidly decreasing marks, and this is very satisfactory. Tommy Green has led the field home once (at Enfield); and finished a creditable second in our own Open event. Len Fletcher has not succeeded in being in the first three yet this season in Open Event, but the New Year should find him back to his old form and all the better for a steady start. In the individual handicap races H. Latter earned himself distinction (and no doubt a considerably reduced handicap!) by winning our own event, whilst J. G. Coleman did well in taking third prize at Enfield. Several of our "Juniors" are showing considerably improved form. In particular our "Veteran Junior," Charlie Speechley, calls for attention, as does also A. H. Field. Many others have also improved upon their previous best and the result of our "Junior" Club Championship for the "Horwood" Cup should make interest reading. Tommy Green Tommy Green led the field home at Enfield; second in our own Open event Len Fletcher Len Fletcher H. Latter H. Latter won our own open walk handicap J. G. Coleman J. G. items.s: THE HIGHGATE HARRIERS' "OPEN." Report and result of the Highgate Harriers' open walk in Regents' Park, where Belgrave's A team tied with Enfield A.C. on 57 points for the scratch team race, A. L. Fletcher fifth, and the B team second in the team handicap (J. McCarthy's printed time does not fit his placing). THE HIGHGATE HARRIERS' "OPEN." Very wisely, the Highgate H. decided to promote their race in Regents' Park this year and were rewarded by an excellent entry. Len Fletcher was our first man home, fifth, with Tommy Green eighth. Our team and Enfield A.C. tied for scratch team honours with 57 points each, although we had the satisfaction of finish-ing seven men (some of them being "B" team members) before the fourth Enfield man finished. The handicap was won by W. A. Sykes (Eastleight Town S.C.) and his team won the handicap team race which afforded Tommy Green much pleasure, for he has been at great pains to encourage the sport in his home town. Our "B" team, consisting of Brown, Coleman Latter and C. E. Churcher, were second. Altogether, a successful start to the season. It is unusual for our teams to gain handicap awards in the first race of the season; we usually require a few weeks to settle down, but this year proved an exception. RESULT. Pos. Name Team Act. items.s: ENFIELD A.C. OPEN WALK. Report and result of the Enfield A.C. open walk for the Berman Cup, won by T. W. Green with Enfield A.C. taking the team race from Belgrave and Belgrave's A team second in the handicap team race (Joe Coleman is said to take the handicap prize, while the result notes he was placed third). ENFIELD A.C. OPEN WALK. Our first team entered in this event presented a strange appearance, several of our prominent walkers being unable to turn out. In fact, it was obvious that the circumstances depleting our strength gave us no possible chance of winning the "Berman" Cup from Enfield A.C., and indeed, that we should do well to take second place from the other contending clubs. Tommy Green walked splendidly to lead to field home; Enfield winning the team race with us, second; North London H. third; and Leicester W.C. fourth. Joe Coleman started off splendidly and although he slackened off a little in the second half of the race, he did well to take the handicap prize. Our team, consisting of Coleman, Jackman, Speechley and C. E. Churcher, took second handicap prizes as the annexed result shows. RESULT. J. G. Coleman was placed third in the Individual Handicap. items.s: OUR OPEN WALK. Report and result of Belgrave's own open walk, won by J. T. Johnson of Enfield from T. W. Green, with H. Latter winning the handicap and the Belgrave B team the handicap team race (Belgrave A's printed team positions add to 38 though 36 pts. is printed). OUR OPEN WALK. 194 entries, comprising 22 teams, entered our Open race which took place over the same course as used in the last year or two. We had four teams entered, Surrey Walking Club sent along three teams, and the Polytechnic two. The race resolved itself into a duel between Johnson, of Enfield, and Green, of ours, with Johnson eventually gaining a creditable win. He also had the satisfaction of leading his team to victory, Enfield scoring 28 points to our 36. H. Latter, one of our young walkers included in the "B" team, surprised us all by finishing 13th in the scratch race (out of 170 starters), so winning the handicap with an allowance of 5 mins. 50 secs. This success, combined with good walking by A. H. Field enabled our "B" team to win the first handicap team prizes, the team being completed by Harley and Brown. Second prize in the handicap went to W. J. Hogan (Southgate and Wood Green A.A.) with an allowance of 5 min. 20 sec., handicap time 52 min. 56 sec.; and a Surrey W.C. visitor, L. Woodcock (allowed 7 min.) was third. Len Fletcher took the prize for the first Belgrave Harrier to finish not gaining any other award; and the full times and placings of all our men appear below. Our very best thanks are due to the officials who came along to help us; and to all the competitors who once again gave us excellent support. RESULT. Winner of Individual Handicap—H. Latter. Pos. items.s: Note that Fred Bentley, who made a fine first effort in the Brighton Walk, was slightly injured on Police duty when a motor cycle threw him onto a taxi. Fred Bentley, who made such a fine first effort in the Brighton Walk recently, met with a slight accident in the course of his Police duties a week or so back. A motor cycle mounted the pavement and then threw him on to a taxi. Fortunately his injuries were only slight, involving a strained leg, and he expects to start training again in the New Year. Fred Bentley Fred Bentley first effort in the Brighton Walk; strained leg in an accident on Police duty; no club printed (Police duty is his job, not his club; not presented as ours here) London to Brighton Walk

items.label: November 1932
items.sum: Forthcoming walking fixtures from Boxing Day to the Junior Championship in Birmingham, where the club hopes to hold the Garnett Cup.
items.s: FUTURE WALKING FIXTURES. Forthcoming walking fixtures from Boxing Day to the Junior Championship in Birmingham, where the club hopes to hold the Garnett Cup. FUTURE WALKING FIXTURES. Dec. 26th—Boxing Day. Our usual three miles walk on the track will be included in our Battersea Park Meeting programme commencing at 11 a.m. Entries (1/-) should be handed in, or sent, at once. On the same day we shall be represented in the Godstone and back Walk (18¾ miles); and also in the Eastleigh—Southampton and back race (12 miles) promoted by the Eastleigh Town S.C. Our racing programme is then clear until January 21st, when the Cambridge H. hold their Open Walk at Eltham. We are usually fortunate enough to bring back a large proportion of the awards from this event, and it is hoped that history will again repeat itself. The following Saturday our Club 10 Miles Championship will be held, but more of this in our next issue. The New Year should find our "Juniors" beginning to think seriously of the Junior Championship which is to be held in Birmingham on March 4th. Writing at this early stage we appear to have an excellent chance of recording our fourth win, but stern opposition may be expected from Surrey Walking Club (in particular), Dunlop W.C. and Highgate H. It will be necessary for every man to be at the peak of fitness if we are to hold the "Garnett" Cup once again. Half-measures will certainly not be sufficient. Every individual must train, stroll and race, with the determined knowledge that he will not let his club-mates or his Club down; but rather that they should attain further honours by reason of his concentrated efforts. items.label: November 1932
items.sum: Humorous unsigned sketch of the club's Sunday strolling party from Earlsfield and its regulars, chiefly Bert Footer and Harry Shields, ending with an invitation to members to join.
items.s: ON OUR STROLLERS AND STROLLING. Humorous unsigned sketch of the club's Sunday strolling party from Earlsfield and its regulars, chiefly Bert Footer and Harry Shields, ending with an invitation to members to join. ON OUR STROLLERS AND STROLLING. It has been suggested that our readers might like to know of the exploits of a band of intrepid Belgravians who brave the elements on Sundays to catch a glimpse of Autumnal beauty, to feel the wind tugging at the hair roots, and to know that joy of living a little more intensely than the daily round permits in a work-a-day world. But first let us state our very deep sense of gratitude to Bert Footer upon the heroic self-sacrifice which makes these Strolls possible. Our usual meeting-place is Earlsfield; not, as the uncharitable might suppose, because Bert lives nearby, but because he realizes that should the rendezvous be fixed at some more distant point, he might possibly delay the party. Rather than risk this he prefers the meeting-place to be within two minutes' walk of his doorstep. What nobility of thought! What consideration for others! What an example for those who never stop to think of one's conduct in relation to one's neighbours! In all humility, I should like to ask "where would we be without Footer?" "On the footpaths, through the fields, away from the roads, enjoying ourselves," the cynic might answer, but we must not be too hard on our B.F. He has his limitations, his shortcomings, and there are moments of pathos such as when he asks to be lifted up above the hedges so that he, too, may see the rolling countryside and the wonderful panorama of Surrey landscapes. It is then that we realize that he is always condemned to be on a lower plane than ourselves. Stilts are his only salvation. He reads a map in the same easy facile fashion he would a sonnet by Sir Rabindranath Tagore in the original; and believes that maps were published as badges of authority rather than as guides to wayfarers. Really a remarkable fellow whom, despite his idiosyncrasies, we are all proud to know. And then there's H. W. Shields, who may be described as an antidote to Footer. Harry has a stentorian voice of which the thunder clouds are jealous; tremendous boots—seven-league ones straight from mythology—, and a gargantuan appetite. (The original Non-Stop. And what Variety! Onions and oranges. Bread, butter and blackberries!). He also possesses a broad grin, youth, a desire to argue (to put it mildly), immense reserves of energy, is an avowed misogynist (we have our doubts!) and has a mission in life—that of keeping H. E. Footer, whose name has, I believe, occurred before in these coloumns, in subjection and to curb his tendency towards Mussolini emulation. Should you want to know more of Shields, talk to him gently, take 10 paces away, and wait for the answer! Someone has said, not in any malicious manner, I assure you, that Harry may develop into a second Footer. He certainly has running potentialities, and is the equal of anyone in zeal for the Club weal. Another regular member of our parties is Len Rollins, who introduced Marcel waves, plus-fours and the odd fashion of wearing odd shoes into the Club. In addition to Sunday walks, he is addicted to nocturnal wanderings and thinks nothing of walking from Wimbledon to Cricklewood (say via Walham Green) in the small hours of the morning. Rather eccentric you may think, but then it takes all sorts to make a world. Then there's Micky Walker, who is smiling when you meet him in the morning and smiling when you leave him in the evening, and spends 60 minutes of every intervening hour in exercising his penetrating, infectious laugh. If I hadn't met Harry Shields I might have commented on Micky's appetite! But now I won't trouble. Now meet smiling F. G. Ford ("Felicitous Freddy"), eyes twinkling, ever-cheerful, a song on his lips, as happy as the days are getting short, aren't they? I'm afraid Fred's winning smile would find him unplaced, but as I'm playing with fire it would appear advisable to change the subject! There's Tom Cotton (complete with pipe) giving us the benefit of a much wider repertoire of song than we ever knew he possessed; and Alf Miller and Alf Taylor, who croon about Minnie, who's tall and skinny, and other ladies of their acquaintance. And there's Frank Haydon, who dearly loves to get his teeth into Footer (I write figuratively, of course. There are various reasons why it would be impossible physically), and "Doug" Sloper, who comes along when Circumstances (very charming ones, I admit) permit. Anyone reading all the foregoing must wonder if the party has any saving grace, if there are any Belgravians who raise the tone of the party, give it distinction and respectability, create prestige and generally tend to keep the standard up when, but for their presence, it would inevitably sink lower and lower. The answer is—Yes! And who are these gentlemen of eminence, you may ask, whose nobility of character and high standards of honour and decency alone prevent the waves from engulfing, etc., etc.? They are the Hon. Editors of the "Belgravian," that celebrated gazette whose informative comments and brilliant journalism are eagerly awaited by an enthusiastic public every month, or two months, or even quarter (Advt.). They are our saviours, our defenders, our benefactors, and so on, and so on, and so on, culminating in a really devastating peroration. And yet I'm not quite satisfied in my own mind about one of these two gentlemen, Frank Webb, formerly "Spider," because of his name! now "Super-Snake," because of his habits. No, on second thoughts I'm definitely not satisfied. It may be his employment ("Here's the rent, and would you like a cup of tea, Mr. Webb!"); or his nature; and I can't forget that we heard very little of that holiday at Paignton. And very few have seen the photographs that were taken! No, Frank, I'm afraid that upon mature consideration you must take your place with the rest! So far I have dealt only with personalities and have left myself very little space to devote to our actual strolls and experiences. Let it be said that we cling slavishly to the Footer-tradition of doing one lap, or two small circles, as a prelude to the day's walk. As proof of what I have written about Harry Shields' appetite, let me mention the seat which gave way under his increasing weight and deposited him and two other gentlemen on Mother Earth. Then there was the disgraceful incident on Colley Hill when Harry most effectively put the damper on Bert Footer, and the occasion when "Doug" Sloper caused us to wade through the icy River Mole; and the attempt at self-strangulation by Footer (why does this name intrude so often?). using his haversack for the purpose, and many other memorable episodes. Now to be serious. Any member who would like to join in these parties is cordially invited to do so. Just ask any of the regular party for the next Sunday's arrangements and spend a day with "Nature in the raw," not to mention Mascot Footer, eccentric Leonard, treble-forte-voiced Harry; Alfs one, two and three; T.C.; F.R.W.; D.A.S., and the others; and so add to and benefit from the sociability and Club spirit which it is our earnest desire to maintain and extend. items.sum: Social notes: the November 5th Social with guests from Croydon H., Epsom H., Mitcham A.C. and the R.A.F., the first dance at Wandsworth Baths, and coming socials and dances including an extra dance at Queensberry Hall for the Building Fund.
items.s: ON THE SOCIAL SIDE. Social notes: the November 5th Social with guests from Croydon H., Epsom H., Mitcham A.C. and the R.A.F., the first dance at Wandsworth Baths, and coming socials and dances including an extra dance at Queensberry Hall for the Building Fund. ON THE SOCIAL SIDE. A very successful Social was held on November 5th, when we had as guests old friends in Croydon H., Epsom H., Mitcham A.C., and new ones in the R.A.F. from Northolt. Many members of the last-named three clubs stayed to tea and the dance following; and, of course, there was the usual good crowd of our own fellows and their friends. The dance was only interrupted once, although the ominous date and an unconfirmed rumour that Footer was to be publicly burnt had led me to expect more. The only "turn" was a series of turns by two gentlemen announced as "Castor and Oil, Continental Tumblers." They looked suspiciously like two Club members, "Nick" Carter and "Paddy" Donnelly—one clad in the height of fashion — plimsolls, football shorts, "dicky," "tails" and "topper"; the other in shorts and a tennis shirt with more rents than Frank Webb could collect in six months. The act consisted of some burlesque acrobatics, a slow motion boxing contest and similar fooling; performed all the while with serious expressions and with never a suspicion of a smile! The audience, on the contrary, laughed themselves into helplessness! I am still ignorant as to who was Castored and who was Oiled; and also from which continent the performers came, although I suspect it is not very far from "The World's End!" Our first Dance of the season was held at Wandsworth Baths on November 16th and proved a success. The attendance was not, perhaps, as great as some of those we have held in the past at Wandsworth Town Hall; but the arrangement of tables and chairs around the dancing area was appreciated, and all the dancers seemed to enjoy themselves to the full. Those who did not attend on this occasion will have another opportunity on February 15th. Whilst on the subject of dances, an extra Club Dance has been arranged for Saturday, March 11th, 1933, profits from which will probably be allocated to the Belgrave Building Fund. The Dance is to take place at "The Queensberry Hall," Harrington Road, South Kensington. This hall is easily accessible from all parts of London. Buses from Putney, Clapham Junction and Hammersmith pass the door; while the District and Metropolitan Railways, and "Piccadilly Tube" serve the nearby South Kensington Station. Further details will appear later, meanwhile bear the following dates in mind :— Jan. 28—Social at Wimbledon at which, I am told, "The Nonsuch Girls" will re-appear. Feb. 15—Dance at Wandsworth Baths. Mar. 11—Dance at Queensberry Hall, S. Kensington. Any enquiries to W. A. Rice, 36 Ascalon Street, S.W.8. L. Rollins as Assistant Hon. Secretary, new members and a treasurer's appeal. It gives us much pleasure to wish A. E. Smith and T. Hampson many years of happiness; and to congratulate them most heartily upon the occasion of their recent marriages. * * * * * Congratulations to the members of our cross-country team which regained the Surrey title for the Club; and in particular to A. Penny and H. E. Footer, who finished first and second respectively. Such form will assuredly carry our team into prominent positions in the Championships to come. * * * * * A hearty handshake and "Well run" also to Harry Shields, who finished first in the Middlesex Junior cross-country championship at Northholt. If Harry elects to run in the Southern Counties "Junior" Championship he must stand a very good chance of winning this title; and we shall have a capable team to afford him backing. * * * * * Owing to business claims H. Parker has found it necessary to resign his position as Assistant Hon. Secretary. His resignation has been accepted by the Committee, who will continue to have the benefit of Mr. Parker's advice and experience gained during his 20 years' association with the Club. H. L. Rollins has consented to fill the vacant post, and it is hoped that all our active men will co-operate with him and lighten his task as far as possible. He has served the Club creditably in the past as Social Hon. Secretary, and as Joint Hon. Editor; and we wish him every success in his new position. His ability is proved, his enthusiasm tremendous, and we have no doubt that the Club will continue to progress under his guidance. His duties principally concern the runners; so, Runners, give him your support, your confidence and your co-operation, and see the Club forge ahead under the power of your united efforts! * * * * * The following were accepted into membership at our last Committee meeting: W. F. Davies, E. P. Pearce, H. W. Clemow, D. J. Heath, G. H. Dalziel, L. Jones, F. E. C. Buck. We extend to them all our usual very cordial welcome, and trust their potential performances will be a credit both to themselves and their Club. * * * * * The Hon. Treasurer is anxious to receive :— (a) Overdue subscriptions. (b) Orders for Vests, Ties, Badges, etc. (c) Donations to "The Belgrave Building Fund." Please allay his anxieties at the earliest possible moment. A. E. Smith A. E. Smith recently married T. Hampson T. Hampson recently married A. Penny A.
