items.sum: Preview of the coming fixtures for Whit Monday to August 1935, including Belgrave v. Birchfield Harriers 3 Miles at the British Games, the Doris Shield, the Inter-Club Relays, the A.A.A. Championships and Club Championship Day, with entry details.
items.s: FORTHCOMING EVENTS. Preview of the coming fixtures for Whit Monday to August 1935, including Belgrave v. Birchfield Harriers 3 Miles at the British Games, the Doris Shield, the Inter-Club Relays, the A.A.A. Championships and Club Championship Day, with entry details. As usual, there is quite a feast of entertainment for Whit Monday, chief among the many Athletic meetings being the British Games at the White City, Shepherds Bush. This meeting will commence at 1-30 p.m. with a Grand March Past of athletes, and will be followed by a gigantic programme of events, including an International Inter-Club contest, and Inter-Universities contest, Open Scratch races at all distances, two events open to those under 20 years of age (i.e., 100 yards and 1,320 yards), and also Relay races. Then, just to give the crowd an exhibition of real running, the Birchfield Harriers and the Belgrave Harriers will compete in a 3 Miles scratch race, with eight men aside to run, and six to count. Whether the "Stag-bearers" can turn the tables on us remains to be seen, but bearing in mind their impressive record for many years past, it is certain that our boys will have to be at the top of their form in order to gain victory. On the same day our old friend, Tom Hampson, is promoting a meeting at Clarence Park, St. Albans, and we have promised to send a team along for the 2 Miles Team race. There are also Open Handicaps at all distances and I hope our members will support these to these best of their ability. On June 22nd there are the Southern Championships at the Royal Naval Barracks Sports Ground, Portsmouth. Whether this venue will prove too far away to appeal to the Metropolitan athletes remains to be seen. Another fact to be borne in mind is that now-a-days you can obtain a Southern Standard medal in your County Championships. I expect, however, that the Varsity men will be there in full force. and if one can manage it, it should be a meeting worth witnessing. On Wednesday, June 26th, at Battersea Park Track, we have the "Doris" Shield Competition between Ashcombe A.C., Thames Valley H., and ourselves. Thames Valley H. are the present holders, and it is up to our boys to bring the Shield back to our safe keeping once again. The events are: 100 yds., 440 yds., 1 Mile Relay and 2 Miles Team Race. These are all level events and points are awarded for the first three places in each race. In addition there are the following joint Club Handicaps: 100 yds., 1 Mile run, 2 Miles walk and Shot Putt. Entries for these should be sent off at once, or handed in at Battersea Park Track on any training night Last year the sprint was very poorly supported by our members and I hope they will remedy this by making this year's race a bumper one. On Saturday, June 29th, we have the S.A.A.L. 1 Mile Team race at the Herne Hill Track in connection with the Civil Service Sports at which are also the following Open Handicaps: 100 yds., 440 yds., 1 Mile, which may be of interest to our members. On Tuesday, July 2nd, at Pampisford Road, South Croydon, will be held the second of the Inter Club Relay contests and if we want to retain our hold on the Shield it is essential that we place a fairly strong team in the field for these away fixtures. On July 6th, at the White City, will be held the A.A.A. Junior Championships, and any members who are eligible to compete should take care to get their entry in early so as to avoid being refused. The following Friday and Saturday, July 12th and 13th, the A.A.A. Championships proper will take place at the White City Stadium. Will all those members who contemplate entering kindly get in touch with the Gen. Hon. Sec., who will submit their names to our Committee, with the object of selecting those who are considered worthy of entry, bearing in mind the special conditions which are now laid down as a condition of entry to these events. On Wednesday, July 17th, at the "News of the World" Track, Mitcham, will be held the third of the Inter-Club Relays, and seeing that this venue is fairly accessible for our supporters I trust we shall see them there in good numbers to give our lads a few shouts of encouragement. On July 24th at Battersea Park Track there will be the following Club Handicaps: 100 yds. (under 16), 100 yds. (Vets. 40 or over), 100 yds. Club, 440 yds., 1 Mile run, and a Discus Throw Handicap. In addition there will be two events Open to all Unattached Novices, i.e., 100 yds. and 1 Mile Walk. These are scratch races and members can help the club by sending their names to our Gen. Hon. Sec. not later than 7 days before date of meeting. Entry is FREE for both these events. Wednesday, July 31st, at Epsom, is the final Inter-Club Relay meeting, and I hope that the members asked to make the journey will do so, and thus avoid our fielding our half-milers in the sprints, as we have so often had to do in the past. Don't forget Saturday, August 3rd, is Club Championship Day at Battersea Park Track. The meeting will start at 3 p.m., and there are championship events at all distances, including the 100 yds. for those under 15 years of age, and the 220 yds. for those under 18. Standard medals will be awarded in all events over the sprint distances and are as follows: 440 yds., 56 secs.; 880 yds., 2 min. 8 secs.; 1 Mile, 4 min. 50 secs.; 2 Miles Walk, 15 min. 30 secs. and 16 mins. Please enter early. You can send your name on a postcard to either of the following, and they will be extremely obliged to all those who do so, and so avoid last-minute congestion. For the Field Events men there will be two Club Handicaps, i.e., Long Jump and Shot Putt. We have not yet instituted Championships for these events although the "Harry Wright" Shield is awarded annually to the best performer in this section. In the past our entries for Club Championships have been sadly lacking in numbers; but I hope that this year, with the deletion of the usual Handicap races, that the members will support the championship events, and thus show that they do not object to competing in company with the Club's so-called "cracks." All Entries and any enquiries can be sent to our— Asst. Hon. Sec., E. A. Duffett, 10, Barrow Road, Waddon, Surrey. or Gen. Hon. Sec., 71 Ravensbury Road, S.W.18. items.s: ANOTHER NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP ! Editorial notes: Belgrave retain the National 50 kilometres walk title and Horlick Cup at Bradford, T. Cotton's Building Fund scheme, a Flannel Dance, the re-opening of Wimbledon headquarters, the coming A.G.M. and unpaid subscriptions. Congratulations to the team which made the long journey to Bradford and successfully defended our title of National Champions in the 50 kilometres Walk, held on Whit Monday. We thus retain the "Horlick Cup" for another year. Tommy Green broke his own record for the Bradford Walk, but finished second to H. H. Whitlock, who caught Tommy in the last two miles. Fred Bentley (6) and Fred Rickards (7) completed our team, and our trio deserve our very heartiest congratulation. The two last-named had anything but an easy journey over the second half of the course; cramp and the severity of the course (the last nine miles of which is reputed to be stiff hill-climbing!) affecting our men, as it did most of the competitors. However, determination got them there, and the final team scoring gave us a one point advantage over Birmingham W.C. Our fourth man, Bob Martin, gained a first-class standard medal. Well done, all! * * * * * Most members have recently received a letter from Mr. T. Cotton, explaining a scheme which can give considerable help to our Building Fund. If the idea is to be carried out, with consequent advantage to us all, it is necessary that the Acting Hon. Secretary be notified immediately of the help you are prepared to give. Much detail work has to be done, and it is essential that the measure of support forthcoming be known well in advance. Please, therefore, make it your duty to write to T. Cotton, 25, Duntshill Road, S.W.18, at once. Many thanks. A Flannel Dance will be held at the Express Dance Hall, Clapham Junction, on Saturday, September 14th, following upon our final track meeting of the season at Battersea Park. Tickets will be available shortly, from our Social Hon. Secretary, and it is hoped that our Social programme will receive a good send-off and thus provide our Social sub-committee with the encouragement to make our 1935-36 season the best yet. * * * * * Our headquarters at St. John's Hall, Ridgeway, Wimbledon, will re-open on Saturday, September 21st. With the mercury high in the thermometer, and our Summer holidays before us, it seems rather strange to be writing of the Winter season—but inevitably Wimbledon days approach. Much as we regret the passing of Summer, many of us look forward to the "country" and the "road," and to all that the Winter season holds in training, racing and cheerful cameraderie. Successful as last season was on the racing side, we can still add a little here and there, whilst not forgetting the very real business of holding what we have. The training part, whatever your rating, whether you profess to be speedy or not, can hold healthy enjoyment for everyone. Our attendance at Wimbledon should not be far short of 200 a week. (We'll find room somewhere! Here, Ben, put Footer on top of the cupboard! Thanks!). The more the merrier. As for the spirit, read K. B. O'Kell (of Ford's S.C. and Belgrave H.) in our last issue. Well, see you there! * * * * * During September, you will receive the customary advice of the Annual General Meeting, which will be held towards the end of the month on a date not yet fixed. Every member should make an effort to be present to hear the account of their stewardship given by the Officials, and to see that those responsible for the management of your Club during the coming season, are those best fitted to do so. It is your duty to your Club, and to the Executive of 1935-1936; for they need your fullest support and confidence if we are to continue to progress. * * * * * And now to end these notes with a constantly recurring subject—unpaid subscriptions. The Hon. Treasurer's heart is heavy and his pocket light (the one in which he keeps the Club money!), and all because a few have yet to fulfil their obligations. To enable the books to be closed for the auditors' inspection, please act at once should you be one of the few who like to enjoy the Club's privileges on a year's credit. This also applies to those who owe for "Belgravians." In fact, all who are indebted to the Club are asked to settle up right away; and if you like to send along next year's subscription as well—do so! The Hon. Treasurer has plenty of receipt books on hand, and nothing pleases him more than to write in your name and the amount, and then sign on the dotted line. Address on page 1. items.sum: Report of Belgrave's annual inter-club scratch walks on June 3rd (five, three, two and one mile races, with results and points; Surrey W.C. won on 122 points, Belgrave second on 105), followed by three Belgrave club handicaps (100 yards, One Mile, Long Jump).
items.s: THE ANNUAL INTER-CLUB WALKS. Report of Belgrave's annual inter-club scratch walks on June 3rd (five, three, two and one mile races, with results and points; Surrey W.C. won on 122 points, Belgrave second on 105), followed by three Belgrave club handicaps (100 yards, One Mile, Long Jump). Our usual programme of inter-club scratch walks was held on June 3rd, and we were accorded splendid support by the Metropolitan clubs, no fewer than ten teams participating. A high standard of walking was seen, generally, and the success of this annual no-entry fee, no-award contest once again confirmed our opinion that this is one of the most eagerly-awaited track events of the season among walkers. Proceedings commenced with the five miles race and Redman (Met.) took the lead followed by Len Fletcher. Later Hake (S.W.C.) came through, and in the latter stages of the race a great duel was fought out between Redman and Hake, the first named prevailing by a few yards. Fletcher finished in third position in 38min. 41sec., which indicates that he is regaining some of his form of a year or so back; and our other representative, Charlie Churcher, finished in fifth place. Totalling the points for this event, we found that Surrey Walking Club and ourselves had both scored 34 points, the next highest being the Valentine's S.C. with 29 points. RESULT. 1, F. Redman (Met. W.C.), 37 min. 42 sec.; 2, H. A. Hake (S.W.C.); 37 min. 44 sec.; 3, A. L. Fletcher (Bel.), 38 min. 41 sec.; 4, F. C. Ryder (Val.), 39 min. 18 sec.; 5, C. E. Churcher (Bel.) 39 min. 48 sec.; 6, L. Woodcock (S.W.C.), 40 min. 1 sec. Fourteen finished. Ashcombe A.C., nil; Belgrave H., 34 pts.; Essex Beagles, 13 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 11 pts.; Metropolitan W.C., 27 pts.; Poly. H., 24 pts.; Surrey A.C., 9 pts.; Surrey W.C., 34 pts.; Valentines S.C., 29 pts.; Woodford Green A.C., 8 pts. Next came the Three Miles race, and here we saw A. A. Cooper, in action. Harry Churcher was not far behind at the end however; and our other man, Bill Treacher, paying special attention to style, took sixth position. The combined walking of our men gave us a two points advantage over Surrey Walking Club, an advantage we also held in the competition at this point, for we had scored equal points on the first race. Not for the first time, the contest looked like being a neck and neck affair between our Surrey friends and ourselves, although Woodford Green scored heavily in this race. RESULT. 1, A. A. Cooper (W.G.), 22 min. 2 sec.; 2, H. G. Churcher (Bel.), 22 min. 12 sec.; 3, N. L. Burt (S.W.C.), 22 min. 42 [?] sec.; 4, A. H. Foster (W.G.), 22 min. 52 sec.; 5, H. H. Whitlock (Met)., 22 min. 59 sec.; 6, W. A. Treacher (Bel.), 23 min. 2 sec. Fourteen finished. Ashcombe A.C., nil; Belgrave H., 34 pts.; Essex Beagles, 9 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 11 pts.; Metropolitan W.C., 16 pts.; Polytechnic H., 13 pts.; Surrey A.C., 15 pts.; Surrey W.C., 32 pts.; Valentine's S.C., 22 pts.; Woodford Green A.C., 37 pts. In the next event, the 2 Miles, we were represented by Speechley and Harley, whilst Surrey W.C. had Fisher and Burgess, the Kent champion. From the start Stone (Poly.) led, followed by the Surrey pair, and our two. It seemed that our two points lead was to be taken from us in this event, and we should be all-square on the competition total, leaving the One Mile race to be the deciding event. This was not to be, however, for Charlie Speechley suffered disqualification and we were points down: Surrey W.C. scored 37 points to our 17, and our chance was gone! RESULT. 1, V. W. Stone (Poly.), 14 min. 46 sec.; 2, W. L. Burgess (S.W.C.), 15 min. 23 sec.; 3, M. J. Fisher (S.W.C.), 15 min. 25 sec.; 4, A. A. Harley (Bel.), 15 min. 38 sec.; 5, H. Watts (Met.), 15 min. 43 sec.; 6, A. H. Rayner (S.A.C.)., 16 min. 3 sec. Ashcombe A.C., 10 pts.; Belgrave H., 17 pts.; Essex Beagles, 20 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., nil.; Metropolitan W.C., 25 pts.; Poly H., 34 pts.; Surrey A.C., 23 pts.; Surrey W.C., 37 pts.; Valentines S.C., 23 pts.; Woodford Green A.C., nil. Fourth and last came the One Mile race. Here we had Don Brown, fresh from his win in the Surrey County Championship, and Percy Wright, opposed by Hancock and Amer, of S.W.C. Our chance had gone, but our rivalry still continued, and there was still second place in the competition to be consolidated. Brown gained a comfortable win from Hancock, and in a great struggle for superiority over the last hundred yards, Wright, of ours, and Amer, of theirs, both had to "come-out," leaving the leading six as follows:— RESULT. 1, D. E. Brown (Bel.), 6 min. 57 sec.; 2, L. Hancock (S.W.C.), 7 min. 15 sec.; S. H. Reynolds (W.G.), 7 min 23 sec.; 4, A. De'ath, 7 min. 46 sec.; 5, R. J. Crump (L.V.), 7 min. 46 sec.; 6, C. Webster (E.B.), 7 min. 46 sec. Thirteen finished. Ashcombe A.C., nil; Belgrave H., 20 pts.; Essex Beagles, 25 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 16 pts.; Metropolitan W.C., 28 pts.; Poly H., 25 pts.; Surrey A.C., 9 pts.; Surrey W.C., 19 pts.; Valentine's S.C., 8 pts.; Woodford Green A.C., 32 pts. FINAL PLACINGS. As a last word—our thanks to the walkers who provided the competition, and those who helped to carry it through satisfactorily and contributed to the undoubted success of the meeting. In addition to the Walking events, we held three Club handicaps as follows:— The 100 yards saw our International half-miler, T. H. Scrimshaw competing, and off the 7 yds. mark he scored a good win, with R. G. Michael yet another half-miler, second off 8½ yds. F. J. Skelley, our promising Junior sprinter, secured third place, but the result on the whole does not reflect very highly on the majority of our so-called sprint men. In the One Mile handicap, one of our cross-country Juniors came to the fore, K. N. Wood winning in very fast time off a liberal mark. G. R. Chantler also showed improvement on previous form in finishing second, with A. A. Bird filling third place. Bird's form on the track is full of promise and he is already recognised as one of our regular team men for the Inter-Club contests. The Long Jump handicap was won by F. J. Skelley and his actual jump of 18 feet should encourage him to persevere, as good long-jumpers are few and far between. As Skelley is only 16 years of age, the future looks full of promise so long as he gives plenty of time to those little details which make all the difference in this branch of sport. Max Henchoz gained second place, with A. A. Deacon third. 1. Surrey W.C. 122 pts. 6. Woodford Grn. A.C. 77 pts. 2. Belgrave H. 105 pts. 7. Essex Beagles 67 pts. 3. Polytechnic H. 96 pts. 8. items.s: THIS AND THAT ! Club notes: a coach and cyclist attendants for the London—Brighton Walk on September 7th (Knott Memorial Shield), Belgrave's ninth place in the Kinnaird Trophy, Jim Ginty's narrow defeat by Scarsbrook in the Southern steeplechase, officials barring J. Parker from the Kinnaird 3 miles (contrasted with D. Finlay's club switching), news from B. C. Button in New South Wales, the narrow British Games team-race defeat by Birchfield, open team race wins, A.A.A. Championships performances and a proposed club points trophy, protest at Ginty's non-selection for England v. France, and the Club Outing to Frensham Ponds. Take notice that we shall have a double-deck coach accompanying the London—Brighton Walk, on Saturday, September 7th. The race has been brought forward a week from the previously advertised date at the request of the Brighton authorities. The race will start as usual at 7 a.m., and our coach will leave Westminster at 7-30 a.m. and proceed by easy stages to Brighton, the return journey being timed for 6 p.m. We shall be strongly represented and expect to win the "Knott" Memorial Shield for the fourth successive year. Tommy Green will be renewing his acquaintance with this race, and Fred Bentley is another we expect to get near eight hours for the journey. Seats on the coach may be booked right away (5/- each) and application should be made to the Walking Hon. Secretary. Last year the number of supporters was very disappointing. Let this year make up for it! * * * * * Offers to act as cyclist attendants to our men during the race would be gratefully accepted by Mr. A. A. Harley. Efficient and conscientious attendants can mean so much to the men they help, and we hope the usual volunteers will come forward and assist our walkers on this occasion. * * * * * We had the usual invitation to compete in the "Kinnaird Trophy" Competition at the White City, and, as usual, our men acquitted themselves well, although scoring but few points. Tom Scrimshaw ran brilliantly to finish second in the 880 yards race; and Syd Ring finished fifth in the 3 miles event. These two men placed us ninth of the twelve competing clubs. Achilles won with 52 points, and the clubs we succeeded in leading at the finish of the competition were Birchfield H. (1), Highgate H. (4) and Mitcham A.C. (1). As we have pointed out repeatedly in these columns, this form of competition places a very high premium on outstanding individuals, and shows but little reward to the Club with a large number of "good average" strength members No doubt, however, the day will come when we shall make a serious challenge to hold the trophy. Certainly, next year, with our added Field Event strength and improved form on the track, we should exceed seven points, which is our best score to date. * * * * * At the same meeting Jim Ginty essayed his first attempt at the Two Miles Steeplechase (Southern Championship), and ran so well that he forced the A.A.A. and Southern Counties champion to run much faster than he did in last years A.A.A. championship. Scarsbrook and Ginty fought it out in the last hundred yards and our man had to admit defeat by a narrow margin. Well run, Jim! * * * * * There was one unpleasant and entirely unnecessary happening in the Kinnaird Trophy Competition. We refer to the action of some of the officials in not allowing J. Parker to run for us in the 3 miles event. Parker had been entered by our Asst. Hon. Secretary (who is probably the most conscientious man in England in regard to entries) according to the terms of the entry form, which were that all members were first-claim members of the club they were representing. As Parker had been a member of our Club for more than three months he was obviously eligible to compete for us in an individual event. However, at the instigation of some of the other competitors, in some strange fashion team race rules were said to apply to an individual event. And, in still stranger fashion, the Judges said it was so! One is amazed at such "reasoning," and is tempted to ask if, when Team Race rules were first introduced, anyone had suggested that they could be so construed, would he not have been covered with ridicule? The absence of justice and clear thinking which robbed our man of his race is so enraging that it would be as well to pass on to something else. * * * * * And so we come to what ordinary laymen like you and me, who are not supposed to be able to interpret rules, might think to be a parallel, but which in "higher" circles passes unnoticed. At the "Kinnaird" Meeting D. Finlay, the English 120 yards hurdles champion, represented, quite rightly, Surrey Athletic Club. A WEEK later, at the British Games, in a programme of inter-club events, he competed for Milocarians A.C. in the short hurdles event. Later in the programme, he competed as a member of the Milocarian relay team—a team event, if ever there was one. These are the facts. Think them over! * * * * * Our contention is that the man in question would have been eligible to represent his new club in the hurdles (individual event) after three months' membership, but not in the relay (team event) until he had served twelve months' membership with his new club. * * * * * We are aware that we leave ourselves open to the cry "Two blacks don't make a white," but we contend that WE have yet to make a black mark! This business has its humorous side, for since the above events, Finlay has been entered as a member of a Surrey Athletic Club relay team! * * * * * Many of our members of ten years or so standing will remember B. C. Button, who in 1926 and 1927 showed great promise as a runner. He went to Australia with his parents, has had his share of racing successes, and now writes to say he is Hon. Secretary of the St. George District A.A.C. of New South Wales. He asks for news of former friends, and sends us the Annual Report of his club, which makes interesting reading. Their track standard seems to be quite a high one; but in the field events section there are some very fine performances. B. Dickinson has done 24 ft. 0 5-8 ins., Broad Jump, and 49 ft. 11 7-8 ins. Hop Step and Jump. Their best Shot Putt is 43 ft. 4in., Javelin Throw, 168ft. 5 ins.; Discus, 129 ft. 10½ ins Certainly, very good performances. It is good to know that one of our old comrades still enjoys good health, and is helping to carry on the sport in another part of the Empire. * * * * * It is indeed pleasing to see the introduction of so many boys to the Club recently. Among them are many who have distinguished themselves in school athletics; and we hope that in the course of a few years they will attain similar success in senior events. * * * * * At the British Games the "star" event was the Three Miles team race between Birchfield H. and ourselves; eight aside running, with six scoring. The race will be long remembered by those who had the pleasure to witness it. At one mile Birchfield led; at two miles we were leading handsomely, but in the last lap our Midland friends managed to pack in together and inflict a four points defeat upon us. Actually, the greatest excitement prevailed at the finish of the race, and he would have been a bold man who attempted to give the team winners without adding up the scoring positions. A four points deficit was our lot, but so close was the race that the gain of ten yards or so by one of our men on the last lap would probably have reversed the result. We congratulate Birchfield upon scoring one over us; and both teams were delighted with the match—and, may it be said, are eager for the next. Jim Ginty, of ours, led the field home in 14 min. 43 sec., and Ring and Rice did well to finish third and fourth. Final scores were Birchfield H. (2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9), 37 pts.; Belgrave H. (1, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12), 41 pts. Our scoring men were Ginty, Ring, Rice, Taylor, Allum, Parker; with Carter and D. Patience as the non-scoring men. * * * * * At the time of writing our two and three mile teams have competed in seven open team races and won five of them. Wins have been our reward at Luton, Chelmsford, St. Albans, Wealdstone and Ponders End. The least said about Ravensbourne the better! We were particularly pleased with our win at Ponders End, for our "B" team finished third—and Birchfield were second. Carter ran a fine race here, losing by inches to R. R. Sutherland, of Birchfield. Our success in these races is very gratifying, especially as we have had to do without the assistance of A. Penny, H. E. Footer and R. W. Jordan. * * * * * Recent individual winners of Open events include C. E. Churcher, F. R. Webb, A. R. Shaw, A. A. Bird, H. W. Shields, H. E. Footer, J. E. Flower (hush!), to whom our heartiest congratulations go. We were also winners of a scratch relay at Woking. * * * * * We had several representatives in the A.A.A. Championships, and D. E. Brown (2nd, 2 miles Walk), J. Ginty (2nd, 2 miles Steeplechase), T. H. Scrimshaw (4th, 880 yards), H. G. Churcher (5th, 2 miles Walk) and A. R. Shaw (Standard, Steeplechase) were our principal performers, and merit our sincere congratulations. Don Brown had to give place to Cooper in the Walk, but his time of 13 min. 53.8 sec. is amazingly fast. Tommy Scrimshaw ran splendidly (he was unofficially timed at 1 min. 55.4 secs.) and yet this only gained fourth place. Most years this time would carry a championship with it, but Tommy has always been unlucky in his running. We were all glad to see a good club-man in A. R. Shaw qualify for his Club Honours Badge; and Harry Churcher repeated a previous year's performance in gaining a Standard Medal. Of Jim Ginty we shall have something to say presently, but meanwhile,—well done, all! * * * * * It would be interesting to have a special trophy in connection with the A.A.A. Championships, to be held for a year by the club whose representatives scored most points, reckoning on a basis of six points for a winner, down to one point for the sixth man in a final, and a point for every man (not included in the foregoing) who beat standard for his event. Such a trophy would provide added interest to spectator and competitor alike, pay some tribute to clubs, who are, when all is said and done, the backbone and the life-blood of Athletics, and provide that little extra element of interest and keenness for the public. If such a scheme were instituted, it is interesting to note that on this year's results we should have been placed fourth—a very satisfying position to occupy. Scores would have been (E. & O.E., of course): Achilles 31, Polytechnic H. 26, L.A.C. 22, Belgrave 16, Melocarians 15, Woodford Green A.C. 12, Salford A.C. 12, Army A.A. 11. The sport at the A.A.A. Championship was tremendously keen, and everyone must have enjoyed Friday's and Saturday's programmes. But why, oh why, are we not allowed to know who has won Standard medals? We have complained about this before. There must be thousands of athletes in the crowd who appreciate what A.A.A. standard means. In a Club such as ours, the Honours Badge depends upon it, and yet competitor and spectator can get no information during the meeting. We suggest that out of courtesy to the competitors, and to that section of the spectators who are athletes enjoying a "busman's holiday," these details should be given immediately following the event. * * * * * All present on the Saturday were impressed by the performance of Ginty in the 2 miles Steeplechase, and his spirited running against George Bailey, of Salford, who eventually triumphed in very good time. Here, we thought, England has two of the finest steeplechasers she has ever been able to call upon. Reference to the records showed us that in the eighteen years that the times have been taken in this event, Jim's time (10 min. 29.8 sec.) had only been beaten twice, one occasion being when Iso Hollo, the Finnish world's record holder, had taken the title in 1933. Here, we thought, England has two men who will do well against France on July 27th, and against the rest of the world at Berlin in the 1936 Olympiad. But in some unaccountable way, despite the fact that the first two Englishmen were religiously chosen in all the other events for the match v. France, the second string in the Steeplechase was announced as "A. N. Other." We submit that the Selection Committee have allowed feelings other than strict impartiality, and attention to their own Championships, to influence them. It is pitiable that England should not have the services of one of the gamest triers and proved performers that have ever drawn on spikes. We are not unmindful of last year's selection of the team to visit Australia, when the claims of A. V. Reeve, of the Poly., were ignored. We trust that those in a position to do so will make enquiries into the matter, to ensure that such flagrant injustice shall not again be meted out to athletes who fully earn their selection; and consistently by their sportsmanship and whole-hearted endeavour, prove their worthiness to represent their country. We have sympathy for the man, game runner though he be, selected to take the place rightfully belonging to our man; for he is well aware that he is not the second-best steeplechaser in England, and, indeed, to the best of our knowledge, he has never yet competed in a Steeplechase event. Jim Ginty, sportsman that he is, refuses to discuss the matter; and we can only hope that the future will bring his International colours over both country and track, to compensate in some degree for present disappointments. STOP PRESS.—Subsequent events have shown that the Selection Committee robbed England of a probable three points, and at worst a certain one point, by their non-selection of Ginty. These points might have made all difference in such a closely-fought match. * * * * * Nearly sixty members and friends took part in the Club Outing on Sunday, July 21st. Our double-deck coach left Victoria at 10-15 a.m. and took us to Frensham Ponds, where the party swam, played cricket and rounders, and generally enjoyed themselves. It was good to see Arthur Penny lapping round the bases at full speed. A move was made to Elstead for tea, where the company tried, unsuccessfully, to demolish completely the home-made rolls, butter, jam, lashings of cream, and cake provided. After tea, we adjourned to Footer's idea of an open space (we suspect it was inside, for the pull-up was within a short distance of a hostelry!) and indulged in further games. Then, homewards. Everyone voted the day's outing a most successful one, and many enquired if another could not be arranged in a few weeks' time. The weather favoured us, and we were delighted to see some of our more recent members taking part in everything, and thoroughly enjoying themselves. items.sum: Juniors' report: Belgrave won all three events of a junior inter-club contest with Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. at Mitcham on June 3rd, plus S. C. Botwright's Middlesex junior 220 yards title, H. M. Quackenbos's third in the A.A.A. junior steeplechase and a second place in an Enfield team race.
items.s: WITH THE JUNIORS. Juniors' report: Belgrave won all three events of a junior inter-club contest with Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. at Mitcham on June 3rd, plus S. C. Botwright's Middlesex junior 220 yards title, H. M. Quackenbos's third in the A.A.A. junior steeplechase and a second place in an Enfield team race. On Monday, June 3rd, a Junior Inter-Club contest was held at Mitcham between the local club, Croydon H. and ourselves. We were successful in winning very convincingly the three events decided, and we congratulate ourselves upon having such splendid young runners in our ranks. We are sure that we shall be well represented in Senior events a few years hence, judging by the talent on show at this Inter-Club event, and in other races. It is not our policy to give our juniors too much racing, for we know the evils which such over-indulgence can inflict upon promising careers, but it is certainly very pleasing to see the Belgrave Harriers of to-morrow performing so creditably when called upon to represent the Club in junior fixtures. RESULTS. 3 x 100 Yards Relay.—1, Belgrave H. (Botwright, Jones, Saunders); 2, Mitcham A.C.; 3, Croydon H. 3 x 200 Yards Relay.—1, Belgrave H. (as above); 2, Mitcham A.C.; 3, Croydon H. 880 Yards Team Race.—1, Belgrave H. (Clements 2, Quackenbos 3; Cottrel, 5), 10 pts.; 2, Mitcham A.C. 11 pts. S. C. Botwright greatly distinguished himself by winning the Middlesex Junior 220 yards Championship; and he will undoubtedly show himself to be a first-class sprinter in a year or so; possibly developing into a champion quarter-miler. H. M. Quackenbos also merits our congratulations upon his third place in the A.A.A. Junior ¾-mile Steeplechase Championship. He will surely become one of our future stalwarts. Four of our young milers, Clements, Chantler, Stimpson and Wood competed in an under 20 mile team race at the Enfield A.C. Open Meeting, and although our scoring men finished 4, 5, 6, we were placed second. However, this form guarantees good future performances. Steady training, co-operative effort, willingness to learn and apply the principles expounded by the senior runners, and moderated racing during the early years, should develop within the Club a set of performers capable of bringing further lustre to the Club's name in the future. items.sum: Southern Amateur League Division 1 report: Belgrave fifth-placed team in the 4 x 220 yards relay at the White City on May 25th and winners of the 1 Mile Team race at Herne Hill on June 29th, leaving them one point behind Herne Hill and leaders Blackheath with two events left.
items.s: SOUTHERN AMATEUR LEAGUE EVENTS. Southern Amateur League Division 1 report: Belgrave fifth-placed team in the 4 x 220 yards relay at the White City on May 25th and winners of the 1 Mile Team race at Herne Hill on June 29th, leaving them one point behind Herne Hill and leaders Blackheath with two events left. Division 1. On May 25th, at the White City, was held the 4 x 220 yds. and we fielded a useful team in Kealey, Stroud, Mewes and Michael. Kealey elected to start for us, and drawing number 1 station, he was twice bumped very badly and so we lost any advantage which we might have had. Mewes and Michael both tried their best to reduce the gap between the leaders, and Stroud went off over the last leg just in front of the Poly and S.L.H. He could not hold Yates, of S.L.H., but just managed to beat Carmen, of the Poly, by inches for fifth position. Blackheath beat Herne Hill for first place, with Mitcham A.C. third. The 1 Mile Team race was held at Herne Hill on June 29th, and we repeated our last year's success in this race and all our men ran extremely well. Tom Scrimshaw, in finishing fourth in the actual race, which was won by the now A.A.A. champion, S. C. Wooderson, fully justified those who think he may do even better over longer distaces than he has done over the half. Our other three men, Bill Rice, Arthur Allum and Albert Shaw, finished 7, 8, 9, and so we scored 28 pts. to Blackheath H. 38, Mitcham A.C. 51, Poly H. 52, Herne Hill H. 59, and South London H. 72. Thus, with two events still to be decided, Blackheath are leading, with Herne Hill one point behind. We are one point behind them. So that with two points to make up, and the 1 Mile Medley Relay and the 4 x 880 yds. to take place, we can be fairly optimistic regarding our chances of retaining our title of champions. The big danger—and on their present form it is a very big one—are the present leaders, Blackheath Harriers. With S. C. Wooderson to lead them and men like Poole, Whittingham, Wiard, Parkes and Page, they present a very formidable opposition, and if our boys can pull it off, then they will have well deserved our congratulations. items.sum: Report of the Doris Shield inter-club contest at Battersea Park on June 26th, won back by Belgrave from holders Thames Valley Harriers by 28 points to 26 (Ashcombe A.C. 12), with the accompanying handicaps (100 yards, one mile, shot putt, 2 miles walk).
items.s: “DORIS” SHIELD INTER-CLUB CONTEST. Report of the Doris Shield inter-club contest at Battersea Park on June 26th, won back by Belgrave from holders Thames Valley Harriers by 28 points to 26 (Ashcombe A.C. 12), with the accompanying handicaps (100 yards, one mile, shot putt, 2 miles walk). This was held at Battersea Park Track on June 26th, and after an enjoyable evening's sport we managed to win back the Shield once again. The holders, Thames Valley Harriers, put up a stern fight, however, and we were only successful by the narrow margin of 2 points. In the 100 Yards match, Tavender, of T.V.H., just pipped Brodie in 10 2/5 secs., and with Stroud filling third place we managed to share points in this event. Points were scored on the basis of 6 to 1 in 100 to 440, and in the Team and Relay race they were 6—4—2. Tommy Scrimshaw turned out for us in the 440 Yards match event, and ran home an easy winner in 52 2/5 secs. T.V.H. men were second and third, with Michael fourth, and so once again points were even between the two clubs. By the way, Ashcombe A.C. were also competing but they had the last two men in both these races. In the 2 Miles Team race, Ashcombe did us a good turn by beating T.V.H. for second place in the team race. L. J. Cohen was the individual winner, with R. W. Jordan, who was making one of his rare appearances for us (he is now at Chichester, but happened to be on holiday, for which we were duly thankful), and he ran a fine race to finish second, with Tom Carter third. With Jack Flower fourth, we thus had an easy win, with, as mentioned above, Ashcombe finishing second and Thames Valley H. third. We now had a 4 points lead and, barring accidents, the Shield looked as good as won. For the final event, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, A. D. G. White, of T.V.H., gave his team a winning lead over the half-mile stage, and so we finished second with Ashcombe behind us. T.V.H. thus knocked two points off our lead, and the final scores were: Belgrave H. 28 pts., Thames Valley H. 26 pts., Ashcombe A.C. 12 pts. There were the usual handicaps open to each club, and in the 100 Yards we had all six finalists, and M. Holt scored his first win in club events; with S. C. Botwright, another of our promising Junior sprinters, second; and R. G. Michael third. The One Mile Handicap was won in rather easy fashion by G. V. Godfrey, of T.V.H., off the 155 mark, with C. E. Cheyney, now of Ashcombe, second and W. J. Ashford, of our own club, third. Our club also held a Shot Putt handicap with our new member from Germany, F. Grassau, on the scratch mark, but he failed to get placed, the winner being E. M. Waldron, with that consistent field event performer, S. Jones, second, and Eagle third. The 2 Miles Walk handicap resulted in a popular win for Jack Field, with J. Banfield, of Ashcombe, second and W. Snell, of our club, third. items.s: INTER-CLUB RELAY MEETING AT CROYDON. Report of the inter-club relay meeting on Croydon's ground on July 2nd (4 x 100, 4 x 880, 4 x 300 yards and 1 mile team race), after which Mitcham and Belgrave led the Shield contest with 25 points each. This was held on July 2nd on Croydon's ground, which is quite close to the Croydon Aerodrome, and the track has a nasty gradient which has to be "climbed" five times in the course of a mile race. However, the 4 x 100 opened the proceedings and, as usual, we filled our usual third position with Croydon beating Mitcham for first place. In the 4 x 880 yds. we fielded a useful team, and with Frank Webb giving us the lead over the second stage, and Alec Ball keeping it, Tommy Scrimshaw just "sauntered" round for the last leg. In fact he almost went too slow and gave the rest of us a few hearts attacks when Ayton, of Mitcham, got to his shoulder at the last bend. Tommy, however, with a quick glance round, immediately sprinted away from him, and we realised Tom had been gently pulling our legs. The 4 x 300 yds. was a repetition of last year's race, in that it caused tremendous excitement, and although Croydon had a winning lead over the last leg, Tom Scrimshaw chased the Mitcham boy all the way and although he caught him, on the narrow track he could not quite get by, and they finished with Tom and his opponent "locked" together as they flashed past the post. The verdict of the Judges was: Croydon, Mitcham, Belgrave and Epsom, and so once again we just failed by the proverbial inch. In the 1 Mile Team race our men, ably led by our Captain, Bill Rice, kept together in fine style at the head of the field, and although on the last lap Frost, of Croydon, went into the lead with 300 yards and go, Harry Shields raced away and finished in easy winner in time which was very good considering the state of the track. Our men scored 1, 2, 4, 6, and in spite of our Captain trying to "wangle" things, Mitcham beat Croydon by 2 points for second place. When we totalled the scores, we found that the home club, Mitcham and ourselves each scored 12 points on the evening, and so Mitcham and Belgrave still lead with 25 points each, with Croydon 21, and Epsom 9. items.label: June-July 1935
items.sum: Report of the third inter-club Shield contest at the News of the World ground, Mitcham, on July 17th, leaving Mitcham one point ahead of Belgrave before the final meeting at Epsom.
items.s: INTER-CLUB “SHIELD” CONTEST AT MITCHAM. Report of the third inter-club Shield contest at the News of the World ground, Mitcham, on July 17th, leaving Mitcham one point ahead of Belgrave before the final meeting at Epsom. At the "News of the World" ground, on July 17th, was held the third of these contests, and we knew that Mitcham would make every endeavour to secure a lead over ourselves, especially as they were on their own "midden." Unfortunately, and I say that advisedly, we were without the sprinters we had been relying upon, and so our team for the 4 x 100 was Mewes, Bennet, Michael and Camkin. The latter had turned up on the off-chance and had very wisely brought his "togs" along and so we pressed him into service. He did very well on his first appearance in these events, and our team actually surprised their own supporters by beating Mitcham for second place with Croydon winning the event. We had hoped to run Scrimshaw in the 4 x 880, but although he turned up, it was to inform us that he was under treatment by the dentist and would not be able to compete. We therefore ran Harry Shields, together with A. A. Bird, Frank Webb and Fred White. These all ran extremely well and we finished easy winners with Mitcham second and Croydon narrowly beating Epsom for third place. In the 4 x 300 we were forced to field the same team as for the shorter sprint, and our boys failed to rise to the occasion as they had done in the previous event. Mitcham beat Croydon after a fine race, with ourselves beating Epsom for third place after the positions had constantly been changing. The position was now that Mitcham were level with us on the evening; and also, of course, on the gross score, and so it was up to our milers, as it has so often been before. The One Mile Team race proved a most exciting race, and the Mitcham boys rose to the occasion in fine style, and although Bill Rice almost ran his heart out in an attempt to force a win, it was not to be, and with Mitcham scoring 1, 5, 6, 7 to our 2, 3, 8, 12, we were one point down on the total points scored to date. The final meeting will be held at Epsom on July 31st, and remembering our past difficulties in fielding representative sides at this venue, the question of our retaining the Shield is very much open to doubt. Our only hope appears to be that if we can at last get some of our best sprinters to make the journey, we might secure a few much-needed points in the two sprint events and so lessen the strain of our middle-distance men, who are always faced with the fact that they have "got" to win the other two races for us in order to have a chance. Total points to date are: Mitcham A.C., 38 pts.; Belgrave H., 37 pts.; Croydon H., 31 pts.; and Epsom H., 14 pts. items.sum: Preview of the remaining 1935 track fixtures (Club Championship Day, matches at Imber Court and Battersea Park, S.A.A.L. relays and club handicaps), with entries to the Asst. Hon. Sec.
items.s: WINDING UP THE TRACK SEASON. Preview of the remaining 1935 track fixtures (Club Championship Day, matches at Imber Court and Battersea Park, S.A.A.L. relays and club handicaps), with entries to the Asst. Hon. Sec. August 3rd, Club Championship Day at Battersea Park Track, and by now all entries should have been handed in. On present form it looks as if some of the titles may change hands, notably the 440, in which the holder, A. Kench, is a doubtful starter; and if Tom Scrimshaw turns out for the 880, he should regain his title once again. The One Mile should, as usual, provide a most exciting race, and at the moment it would be a brave man who would prophecy the winner. On August 10th we have a match with the Metropolitan Police and, I believe, the Surrey A.C. and Polytechnic H. at Imber Court. This is a most attractive ground and some good running should be seen among the competing clubs. I hope that our members will support their Track Captain in his endeavour to field our best possible strength. The 1 Mile Medley Relay in the S.A.A.L. will be held at the White City on August 17th, in conjunction with the Fire Brigade sports, and in regard to the "open" events at this meeting I should like our members to do their best to support these, as a feature of this meeting is the "pot" which is given to the first unplaced member of the club which has the most members competing in the Mile and Walk. On August 19th we are reviving our old evening meeting in August in which the 1,320 yards race used to feature. This time, however, we are holding a 100 yards, 880 yards and 2 miles Running Handicaps, 2 Miles Walk, and there are also two S.A.A.L. Field Events. Seeing that during the Summer we have gained many new members, I hope these will take this opportunity of competing in club races. These races do give you very useful experience and, moreover, give you a better chance of becoming acquainted with your fellow-members. The 2 Miles Run should attract the runners who have an eyes on our 3 Miles Championship, and also those who think that the halves and miles are a little too fast for them. Over the longer distance they will have more time to settle down, and so here again, I hope to see many new faces appearing. Entries should be sent to either Mr. Bayliss or myself at least a week before the date of the meeting. The fee is 1/- for each event. Our final track meeting will be held on Saturday, September 14th, at Battersea Park, at 3 p.m. We have a return match v. the Metropolitan Police and Polytechnic Harriers; and, in addition, we are staging the final event in the S.A.A.L. Div. 1. This is the 4 x 880 yds. and we are hopeful of repeating our last year's success in this race. Also at this meeting will be held the Club 3 Miles Track Championship for the "Griffin" Cup (Holder, A. Allum). Standard medals are awarded to all those who beat 16 mins. and 16 mins. 30 secs. Our cross-country International and Empire Games 6 Miles Champion, A. W. Penny, contemplates making a return to the "fray" once again in this event, having now recovered from his fractured foot, which has kept him out of the game for so long a period. The following Handicaps will be held: 220 Yds., 880 Yds. and 2 Miles Walk, and as this will be the last chance for club members to secure a "pot," I hope they will enter in large numbers and do their best to "trip" the Handicapper up. Entries sent in a week in advance will be appreciated, so please do not leave it until the last minute to enter. All Entries and Enquiries to either :— E. A. DUFFETT, Asst. Hon. items.sum: Review of the club's field-events men in summer 1935, with their championship performances, the club's lead in Southern Amateur Athletic League Division 1 and provisional "Harry Wright" Shield positions.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS. Review of the club's field-events men in summer 1935, with their championship performances, the club's lead in Southern Amateur Athletic League Division 1 and provisional "Harry Wright" Shield positions. With the Summer season nearing its close, we can express pleasure that our men have shown up so well in Field Events. The last few months have been notable for the number of really first-class field-events men that have poined up, including J. Dodd, F. Grassau. F. Waters and H. Heider. Dodd recently put up two remarkable performances in the Northern A.A.A. Championships, when he finished second in both High Jump and Pole Vault Championships, with leaps of 6 ft. and 11 ft. 9 ins. respectively. In the latter event he surpassed the previous record, but had to be content with second place. In addition to the above performances he has jumped 5ft. 10½in. for us in a S.A.A.L. event, and we may be sure that in a year or so he will be an A.A.A. Champion and International. We trust that Dodd's studies will be followed by a London appointment, and that we may have his services for many years to come. F. Grassau has beaten 40 ft. with the Shot and should be the winner in our coming matches v. Metropolitan Police and Polytechnic H. H. Heider promises to succeed Pfenninger in versatility, for he has cleared 5 ft. 9 ins. High Jump and beaten 21 ft. Long Jump and is also useful with Shot, Discus or Javelin. Vassall and Stannard have collected maximum S.A.A.L points for us in the Pole Vault with jumps of 10 ft 6ins. and 10 ft. respectively. We seem to have a very good school of pole-jumpers! F. Waters and H. Jones represented us in the Kinnaird Trophy hurdles, but were drawn in heats with Finlay and Pilbrow respectively, and so were unable to qualify for the final. At this meeting Sutton (35 ft. 8 ins.) and S. Jones (34 ft. 11½ ins.) represented us in the Shot Putt. In the Surrey County Championship George Powell had his usual win with the Javelin (165 ft. 3½ ins.), with another of ours, E. H. Finneron, second (155 ft. 10½ in.). George followed this up a fortnight later by getting second place in the Southern Championships. Standard medal winners in the County Championships included: Shot, Sutton and Jones; Discus, Jones and Henchoz. Melchoir has now recovered from a damaged ankle and has thrown the Javelin a few inches short of 150 ft. recently. With such talent as we have outlined above, plus the services of field events men such as Robertson, Waldron and Holder, and the continued influx of new devotees of field events, we should not find it difficult to hold the lead we have established in the Southern Amateur Athletic League (Division 1). We are at the head, followed by South London H. and Polytechnic H. The other clubs comprising this division of the league are Mitcham A.C., Blackheath H., Herne Hill H., Croydon H., St. George's Services S.C., Southgate H., Southgate and Wood Green A.A. Subject to confirmation, the following are the positions in the "Harry Wright" Shield, which carries with it the Club Gold Medal. Performances required to equal the 91.97 % of Dodd are: Shot, 42 ft. 1¼ ins.; Discus, 134 ft. 1½ ins.; Javelin, 188 ft. 11½ ins.; Pole Vault, 11 ft. 6 ins.; Long Jump, 22ft. 9 ins. items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking-section notes: the Brighton Walk coach, County walking champions Don Brown and Joe King, and a club handicap won by A. H. East at Ashcombe A.C.'s meeting. Details of the Brighton Walk, for intending competitors, may be had from the Walking Hon. Secretary; and attention is once again drawn to the fact that we shall have a coach on the road on September 7th, and that early application for seats (5/-) should be made. Also offers of assistance from prospective cyclist attendants would be gladly received. * * * * * We have two County Walking Champions in our ranks. Don Brown won the Surrey race, and Joe King the Sussex, both putting up fastest times. * * * * * The Winter season fast approaches and we should be glad to see a few new faces, in addition to all the old ones, at Wimbledon this year. So if you know of anyone likely to be interested in our sport, bring them along. * * * * * The result of the Club handicap held by courtesy of Ashcombe A.C., in connection with their meeting on July 26th, resulted as follows :— 1, A. H. East (650); 2, W. A. Treacher (100); 3, J. E. Rutland (325). Time, 13 min. 58 sec. It is 1922 since Bert East won his last Club first, so this win is not out of turn. * * * * * Two Club handicaps remain down for decision and entries should be sent to the Walking Hon. Secretary a week beforehand. It is not fair to the Hon. Handicappers, or the other competitors, to turn up on the evening and expect to walk if formal notice, either verbal or in writing, has not been given. items.label: June-July 1935
items.sum: Building Fund appeal for a club headquarters at Wimbledon, describing the supporters' membership-card scheme, fund-raising events and the Sub-Committee.
items.s: BUILDING FUND NEWS. Building Fund appeal for a club headquarters at Wimbledon, describing the supporters' membership-card scheme, fund-raising events and the Sub-Committee. Shall we at this time next year be searching for a suitable headquarters of our own at Wimbledon? Shall we be a good deal nearer doing so than at present? Alternatively, shall we simply be going on at quarter-speed, hoping that in seven or eight years' time we might try to purchase a place within two miles or so of the Common? The answer to these questions is in the hands of each individual member, particularly those who have so far contributed pessimism only. We Committee members always consider that the will and achievement belong to the individual member in as great a degree as to us, and that if we do not receive every bit of support of which you are capable, we might as well turn the "Building Fund Committee" into a dart club, or each purchase a pair of rabbits. Recently every member was notified of a supporters' club scheme which the Committee is trying to launch and which in a short space of time would put us in a strong position. Can we do it? Well, what do you, the individual member, think? We have nearly six hundred members on our books and we require to sell about one thousand membership cards to be very successful. Nobody need be out of pocket by the arrangements. Five members between them already have asked for five hundred membership cards. Can we succeed? If we cannot, I am very sorry indeed for the club spirit we so often get proud about. All we need, lads, is a small effort from everyone who feels proud of the Club's great achievements this year; from all those who cheered when the boys were winning the "Brighton Relay"; and we can do more than most of you dream. There are a few more interesting items of news concerning the fund. No records are being broken with "Building Bricks" so far, and if you are loth to part with these charming ornaments, I promise to replace them immediately in order to leave no blank space on the mantlepiece or behind the wringer, as the case may be. Pin boards are doing fine, thanks; and if you want to be really popular with your friends and family, just let me know right away. During the Winter months, Mr. E. Gordon is running a Dance specially for the Fund; and we intend holding another "Smoker." Dates and details of these events will be published as soon as fixed. For your information, the Building Fund Sub-Committee consists of E. Gordon, H. Parker, A. W. Penny, F. H. Elson, T. H. Scrimshaw, C. E. Poulter, and the writer; and, of course, the usual Club officers ex-officio. Do try and get your friends and family, as well as yourselves, interested and keen on our Building. They, as well as you, will be able to spend many pleasant hours with us when our object is attained. In conclusion, many thanks to all those who are ever ready to help in every direction. It is good to know we have such stout chaps as fellow-members and pals. Any Building Fund enquiries should be addressed to :— T. COTTON, 25, Duntshill Road, S.W.18. Mr. E. Gordon Mr. E. items.label: November 1935
items.sum: The new President, O. Horwood, recalls the club's lean years, thanks members for his election at the Annual General Meeting and addresses the Juniors.
items.s: FROM OUR PRESIDENT. The new President, O. Horwood, recalls the club's lean years, thanks members for his election at the Annual General Meeting and addresses the Juniors. Looking back into the past, I well remember the lean years of the Club. At one time I marked the track, combined the offices of Hon. Secretary, Hon. Treasurer and Hon. Handicapper; and carried on with the help of a few members who, for love of the Club, were determined that we should not be disbanded. For fear of leaving out any name that should be mentioned, I will not give any names. It was wonderful how we stuck together, facing all sorts of troubles and anxieties to keep the Club going. I well remember how, when we had collected a few new members and were beginning to show winners in open handicaps (which to us at that time was like winning A.A.A .Championships to-day!); one member came to me and handed in his resignation. When asked the reason he said he wished to support a better club, one that had trophies and relay teams. I remember appealing to him very strongly to stay with us. I remarked that we should not always be a poor club and right down; but that we had hopes of having trophies and relay teams in the future. The reply was that Belgrave would never be a big club; or have trophies as long as they were in existence. This annoyed me, and made me more determined than ever that with the help of others, the Club should one day be held in high esteem. At the recent Annual General Meeting, I went over these times in my mind again, and when I recalled the recent wonderful performances that our members have made in all parts of the world, I felt well-rewarded for all our past work. When our retiring President, Mr. J. R. McKay, spoke on my behalf proposing me as your new President, and his remarks were seconded by Mr. A. A. Harley, I was amazed at the warm welcome the members gave me and wish to express my heartfelt thanks. Throughout the meeting I noted the keenness and good spirit that exists among the members and could well understand how, with such team-spirit and co-operation, Belgrave has achieved its wonderful position to-day. I should like to address a few words to the Juniors. The Seniors who have placed the Club where it is cannot last for ever, so let us remember what they have done and how they have done it; and to train with the same spirit. Aim not only to hold the various titles they have won, but to do even better! Mr. R. J. Savage, in charge of our Junior section, will, I am sure, welcome all our Juniors and watch over their interests; and for their part, it is up to them to accept and carry out the advice that is given. Let our Juniors make their motto : "Still Better." Yours faithfully, O. HORWOOD (President). O. Horwood O. HORWOOD President; signs the letter O. HORWOOD J. R. McKay J. R. McKay retiring President; proposed Horwood as President A. A. Harley A. A. Harley seconded Horwood's election R. J. Savage R. J. Savage in charge of the Junior section Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting

items.label: November 1935
items.sum: Club notes: the A.A.A. apology over Jim Ginty's omission from the England team, F. G. Thomson's election as R.W.A. President, a letter from Birmingham Walking Club, Tommy Scrimshaw's international running, members' illnesses and marriages, novice race winners and a letter from B. C. Button in New South Wales.
items.s: THIS AND THAT. Club notes: the A.A.A. apology over Jim Ginty's omission from the England team, F. G. Thomson's election as R.W.A. President, a letter from Birmingham Walking Club, Tommy Scrimshaw's international running, members' illnesses and marriages, novice race winners and a letter from B. C. Button in New South Wales. In our last issue we had occasion to refer to the scandalous way in which Jim Ginty has been ignored when the England team to meet France was selected; and expressed the hope that some enquiries should be instituted, and an attempt made to secure some satisfaction. Our Committee had, of course, acted in the matter, and were informed that Ginty had not been selected as it was thought that he had an Irish qualification; this in spite of the fact that confirmation or otherwise of his qualifications could have been given inside a few seconds, if called for, and that the true facts had appeared in the Press a clear week before the International Meeting. This explanation was considered unsatisfactory by our Committee. A further letter was written, and our delegate to the A.A.A. undertook to take the whole correspondence to Birmingham on October 12th, and lay the matter before the General Committee of the A.A.A. This was done, the Middlesex County A.A.A. delegates supported us, and further support came from all parts of the Committee room. The result was that the Selection Committee admitted their error, and extended an apology. So the matter ends, and it is good to know that even if such a wrong cannot be righted, we have, at least, been able to secure some redress and respect for our opinions. * * * * * Heartiest congratulations to Mr. F. G. Thomson upon his election as President of the Road Walking Association. Such an honour is the reward for much hard work for Walking and, indeed, Athletics generally; and we wish him a most successful year of office. He is the first Belgrave Harrier to be so honoured; and it would be very fitting for us to regain the "Junior" and "Senior" Championship trophies during his year of office, and set them by the side of the 50 kilos. Championship Cup which we already hold. * * * * * Here follows a letter received recently from the Birmingham Walking Club :— "Arising from the report presented to a record attendance at the A.G.M. of this club on Tuesday last, it was pointed out that your club had beaten the Birmingham team by a single point in the 50 kilos. National Championship. "I was asked to convey the meeting's congratulations on this win, together with your club's popular success, when, among others, you beat our friends the Birchfield Harriers, to win the English Cross-country Championship, thus completing a unique double. "Will you kindly pass the appreciation on to the members of your club, together with our wish that the relations between the two Clubs will continue to be of a most friendly nature. "(Signed) B. BASHFORD, Hon. Gen. Secretary." * * * * * We were glad that Tommy Scrimshaw did so well when running for England v. France, at the White City; and against Germany, at Munich. On both occasions his running in the half-mile stage of the Medley Relay Races was virtually responsible for England's wins in these events. We all hope that Tommy will achieve Olympic honours next year, when the good wishes of all of us will be with him. Incidentally, we understand that he is learning German this winter, so! . . . . * * * * * It came as a great shock to us to learn on the evening of the A.G.M., of the sudden illness of Bill Rice, our popular Social Hon. Secretary and Track Captain. For four days, with the help of oxygen, he battled as we all know he can; and now we are happy to write that he is making slow, but definite, progress. Very soon now he will be with us again, and we wish him a rapid and complete recovery of normal health and fitness. Of our other one-time invalids, Ted Saunders is out walking with us again, and Harry Shields has made a marvellously quick recovery from his recent operation, and will probably be running again over the country before you read these notes. Edgar Stammers, our popular Vice-President, is another to make rapid progress, and we expect to have his smiling face among us again before long. Our heartiest congratulations and very best wishes go to Joe Coleman, Bert Field and Jim Ginty upon their respective marriages. We wish them all years of health and happiness. * * * * * Our recent novice races have been won as follows : J. Amsden (100 yds.); J. Paterson (1 mile walk); A. H. Beaumont (3 miles run); S. R. Wood (3 miles walk). Entries for these events have not been good, and we can only assume that our members make a point of introducing new friends immediately they realise their interest, and do not wait for novice events. Anyhow, we are always glad to welcome new members, and it must be said that recent introductions have been numerous, and proved themselves good clubmen. * * * * * Our readers will remember that in our last issue some news was given of B. C. Button, and many will recall him as a promising young runner in our ranks in 1926—1927. He is now Hon. Secretary of the St. George District A.A.C., New South Wales, and in a recent letter, after recalling old times, etc., he proceeds to give some details and insight into Australian athletics, as follows :— " . . . . I often tell the fellows out here about these and other incidents, and you would be surprised at the interest they take in any overseas happenings. As you say, the Club has made great strides over the past two or three years, and you certainly have a huge membership. I get the "Sunday Pictorial" each week, and although they are very sparing with their Athletic news, I often notice Belgrave's name appearing in the major events and, needless to say, I pass it on to the fellows out here and even take some credit for it! Fancy being able to win the London to Brighton relay. This was beyond our greatest expectations at one time as it looked like being perpetually in the hands of the northern runners! "Now for some local news, so that you can get some idea of the Athletic activities out here. "We have, of course, track and cross-country fixtures, and although in the cross-country season we have quite an attractive programme, the total number of members engaged from all clubs is only about 200. My Club has a membership of about 80, with an average cross-country attendance of 20, and we have more or less been the strongest distance club over the past few years. At the moment we hold all the major N.S.W. titles. We have three big races, viz., the five-mile Novice Championship, open to runners who have not been placed within the first ten of any major cross-country championship, the 10,000 metres C.C.C. and the 10 miles C.C.C., with the 15 miles Modified Marathon in September each year. In the second and third of the above Championships, there are three teams' races. You nominate all your men, and the first six to finish count for the "A" team; the next four in the "B" team, and the next four for the "C" team. On August 17th this year we have the Australian C.C.C. in Sydney, and I have been appointed as one of the three Selectors to choose the N.S.W. team, and also as the Manager. Each State takes it in turns in having the Australian C.C.C., which is held once every two years. When you realise that South Australians have to travel nearly 1,000 miles, Tasmanians about the same distance, and that all visiting competitors have to get a week off, you can see that it is not so easy to stage these events. "By the way, I was recently appointed as 'Sporting Commentator' for one of our Broadcasting Stations, and each Saturday night at 6-30 p.m. I give a review of all sports results, including, of course, Athletics. "Apart from the Championships, we have Open Handicaps in which all clubs compete and the entries usually total about 90 runners. In these events the runners start off their handicap time allowances, and it is seldom that we have sealed handicaps. In Victoria the running is on a much better basis, and in their cross-country opening run they have anything from six to seven hundred Athletes competing. In N.S.W. we have so many sports, viz., Rugby League Football, Rugby Union Football, Soccer (English Football), Baseball, Hockey, etc., etc., and in the Summer time the surf is a hard factor to overcome, particularly in N.S.W., as around Sydney we have numerous surf beaches which really are most attractive. On the track we have numerous competitions. Firstly, for seven or eight weeks, the Inter Club Competition, in which all Clubs meet on one central ground—each club enters two or three grades. There are four grades, viz., (a), (b), (c) and (d), and they provide good competition. Next comes the "Dunn Shield" Competition, which is limited to selected Athletes from each Club, then the State Championships, followed by State Relay Championships, etc. "Believe me, in N.S.W. we produce some really first-class athletes, considering the conditions we have to overcome, as we do not have track facilities, etc., such as you do. "My Club is fortunate in having the use of a good Oval for its Track Meeting every Tuesday night, and at our Annual Carnival we usually attract five to six thousand people. The locals are good supporters if you give them good, fast sport, and we usually intermingle athletics with cycle races and one or two displays. Jack Metcalfe is probably known to you, as he won the Empire Games High Jump Championship. Speaking of the Empire Games, it looks as though there is every chance of them being held in Sydney, provided they can raise £10,000, so if any Belgrave men are chosen, don't forget to give them my address. "Jack Metcalfe is good for a consistent 6ft. 3ins. or 6ft. 4ins. in the high jump. Now, in my Club I have a young chap called Basil Dickinson, who clears just over 24ft. 11ins. in the broad-jump, and is so keen that I really think he has an excellent chance of seeing the next Olympic Games as an Australian representative. He can also clear over 50ft. in the hop, step and jump. We also have Bill Mackenzie, the Australian discus and shot putt champion in the St. George Club, and he is a really first-class Athlete. By the way, he has just been appointed with Jack Metcalfe and another man to form a N.S.W. Coaching Committee, and if you have any spare pamphlets on any aspect of coaching, etc., they will be very much appreciated. They have already purchased some good slow motion films which they show to Clubs at fixed intervals. "The walking standard out here is terrible, and with the present control they have there seems no chance of any immediate improvement. There is nobody to coach young fellows interested in the game, and the judges do not seem to understand the elementary rules of walking. "Must close now. Best wishes to all over there, and again thanks for your welcome letter. "With kind regards, "Yours sincerely, "B. C. BUTTON." Jim Ginty Jim Ginty omitted from England team v. items.label: November 1935
items.sum: Report on Belgrave winning the Field Events section of the Southern Amateur Athletic League, with final league positions, the Harry Wright Shield placings (won by J. Dodd) and hopes for the high and long jumps.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS. Report on Belgrave winning the Field Events section of the Southern Amateur Athletic League, with final league positions, the Harry Wright Shield placings (won by J. Dodd) and hopes for the high and long jumps. This season has proved the most successful yet in the history of the Club, and in winning the Field Events section of the Southern Amateur Athletic League, we have demonstrated that we have no superiors at all-round field events in the London area. We should probably be justified in going a step further and saying "in the whole country." The men who have brought this distinction to the Club, and have competed in one or more S.A.A.L. event on our behalf, are as follows: S. Jones, F. Grassau, G. H. Powell, F. Waters, C. A. Melchoir, K. Robertson, J. Dodd, J. Ginty, E. Byther, H. Vassall, E. W. Stannard, J. Holder, J. Tierney and W. Sutton. Final positions in the S.A.A.L. are :— Performances in the "Harry Wright" Shield Competition have been on a higher level than in previous years, and the standard has risen to such an extent that the fifth man in this year's competition surpasses the winning percentage of two years ago. The winner of the Shield and Club medal is J. Dodd, as shown below, and to him we extend our heartiest congratulations. Generally, we have every reason to be pleased with the season's performances and results, and yet we realise there is considerable room for further improvement. More men are required to interest themselves in one or other of the field events. Our greatest need for improvement is, at the moment, in the High and Long Jump events. True, we have Dodd in the former event, but it has not always been possible for him to assist us, and we have had to call on men whose performance in this event can only be described as moderate. Young Robertson is a bright hope here, however, and in a year or so should be a first-class jumper. Since Clemens moved to Manchester, we have been without an outstanding long jumper; although Gray proved in our last match of the season that he has great potentialities. It is surprising that more of our sprinters do not show an interest in this event. Scores of instances of first-class sprinters who are also good long jumpers are available; and it is an undeniable fact that almost any sprinter can jump at least 19 feet once he has discovered the right length of approach. Given a little natural ability and the determination to persevere, there is little doubt that we have several moderate sprinters who could transform themselves into good class long-jumpers, capable of gaining A.A.A. standard and their Club Honours Badge—and at the same time carry on with their sprinting activities. J. Skelley is one who shows promise in the pit, and we expect his long-jumping to improve as his sprinting powers—already well-developed—improve. With a little improvement in these two events, and studied application by all to their particular events during the Winter, we should have no difficulty in retaining the S.A.A.L leadership, and in gaining valuable points in the various match events of next season. We cannot conclude these notes without paying a tribute to the Sectional Captain, W. Sutton, for his excellent work at all times; and in particular, to his labours in arranging for our representatives to be at the various fixtures—no easy task, as a glance at the past season's fixture card will show. To him, as much as to anyone, is the credit of such a successful season due. It is good to know that he will again be at the head of affairs next season, with the capable assistance of George Powell; and, given the continued loyalty and support of our athletes, we are certain that the activities of the Field Events men will bring still more credit to the Club name. pts. pts. 1. items.sum: Percy Wright's account of the London to Brighton walk won by H. H. Whitlock in 7 hrs 53 mins 50 secs, with Surrey W.C. beating Belgrave by six points for the team prize and F. E. Bentley first Belgrave man (8th), with the result. Henderson's club is printed as Worthing and District S.C. in the text and Worthing and Dist. A.C. in the result.
