items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Report of the Coronation team and relay meeting at Broomfield Park, Southgate, on 15 May 1937, where Belgrave finished third behind Southgate and Blackheath, with handicap wins for Belgrave.
items.s: THE CORONATION MEETING AT SOUTHGATE. Report of the Coronation team and relay meeting at Broomfield Park, Southgate, on 15 May 1937, where Belgrave finished third behind Southgate and Blackheath, with handicap wins for Belgrave. On May 15th, at Broomfield Park, the local club, Southgate Harriers, entertained Blackheath H., Polytechnic H. and ourselves in a series of team and relay events. Also on the programme were handicaps open to members of the four competing clubs. We were more or less outclassed in the sprint events, Blackheath winning both the 4 x 110, and 4 x 220 yards. Also, owing to the earliness of the season, we could not field a team for the 4 x 440 yards. The 4 x 880 yards was held in conjunction with the Southern Amateur League event at this distance, and although L. W. Herbert gave us the lead over the first stage, we eventually finished in fourth place, beating Mitcham A.C. and Herne Hill H. Southgate pleased the local crowd by just beating the Poly after a very close and exciting race. In the 1 Mile Team Race, Pat Parker strode round in the lead, only to be beaten up the straight by P. E. Bull, of the Poly H. When the points had been added up it was found that Blackheath and Belgrave each scored 29, with Polytechnic 38, and Southgate 40. We also fielded a team in the 1 Mile relay open to those who had not competed before that afternoon in the match events—in other words, a reserves race—but an unfortunate blunder at the first take-over resulted in the baton being dropped and so put our team out of the race. So far, during the afternoon we had not gained many points, but along came our field event men to show the runners how it should be done! We won the Weight Putt with Grassau and Melchior, also the Javelin with George Powell and, once again, Melchior, who, by the way, materially contributed to our total of points. The result of the match was : Southgate H., 37 pts.; Blackheath H., 34½ pts.; Belgrave H., 25½ pts.; Polytechnic H., 24 pts. Our runners were more to the fore in the handicap events; mainly due to the fact that we provided the larger portion of the entries, especially in the 880 yards, which was won by Alby Bird off 8 yards. He ran splendidly to beat W. E. Lucas on the tape, so that Belgrave had the first two home. The souvenir awards which were presented to all winners and runners-up were much appreciated by the competitors, and our best thanks are due to the Southgate Harriers for promoting such an interesting and pleasant afternoon's sport. items.sum: Report of the evening match at Kingston on 27 May 1937 against Old Tiffinians A.C. and Old Mid-Whitgiftians, in which Belgrave were second.
items.s: MATCH versus OLD TIFFINIANS A.C. AND OLD MID-WHITGIFTIANS. Report of the evening match at Kingston on 27 May 1937 against Old Tiffinians A.C. and Old Mid-Whitgiftians, in which Belgrave were second. We were again blessed with a fine evening on May 27th for our match at Kingston. A very good and keenly contested meeting resulted which was very much appreciated by the spectators. I am sure, however, that the high-lights of the meeting were our Shot Putters. Grassau, Jones and Bill Sutton monopolised the crowd once they started, and apparently they had not met men of their magnificent physique before. Points were secured for us by E. L. Kealey (3rd, 100 yards); T. D. Wiley (3rd, 220 yards); A. H. Sampson (3rd, 440 yards); S. Garland and W. Ashford (2nd and 3rd, 880 yards); A. A. Bird and E. Stimpson (2nd and 3rd, 1 mile); E. L. Blyther (3rd, Long Jump); T. D. Wiley (1st, High Jump); F. Grassau and S. Jones (1st and 2nd, Shot Putt). The Relay was won by our hosts, with our team second; and final scores were : Old Tiffinians, 44 pts.; Belgrave H., 28 pts.; Old Mid-Whitgiftians, 9 points. Thus concluded another most enjoyable fixture at the Old Tiffiinian's hospitable headquarters. Grassau Grassau Jones Jones Bill Sutton Bill Sutton shot putter E. L. Kealey E. L. items.label: August 1937
items.h: THE INTER-CLUB RELAYS AT TOOTING TRACK.
items.sum: Report of the first Inter-Club Relay Shield contest of the season at the new Tooting Track, with club handicaps run at the same meeting.
items.s: THE INTER-CLUB RELAYS AT TOOTING TRACK. Report of the first Inter-Club Relay Shield contest of the season at the new Tooting Track, with club handicaps run at the same meeting. The first of the contests for the Inter-Club Relay Shield was held at the new Tooting Track. It was also the first time that one of these contests had been held on a Saturday, the usual practise being to run them on week-nights. From our point of view, however, the change was quite a success, although the track was on the loose side. Given time, we are sure this pleasantly situated ground will prove popular with the South London athletes. In the first event, the 4 x 100 yards, we fielded quite a useful team; and, with F. W. Pritchard running a fine third leg, we had the satisfaction of beating Mitcham A.C., with Epsom beating Croydon for third place. The 4 x 880 yards saw Dick Michael give us the lead on the first stage, but F. H. C. White was caught and passed by the Mitcham runner. Alby Bird went next and, running with fine judgment, soon overhauled his man, and sent L. W. Herbert off with a useful lead. Herbert ran well within himself and kept off the opposition without much trouble. Epsom again beat Croydon for third place; and their half-milers are beginning to weld themselves into a useful team. We welcomed Eddie Kealey back into the active ranks for this meeting; while S. C. Botwright also turned out for us in the 4 x 300 yards. Tom Wiley went first and gave us the lead, which F. W. Pritchard and Botwright kept, to send Kealey away with a winning margin. Croydon reversed their placings with Epsom in this event. Then came the 1 Mile Team race, and although we were without Pat Parker and Les Cohen, our team, led home by W. E. Lucas, ran well to win the team race. Harry Shields caused quite a stir by dashing into the lead when 300 yards from home and this seemed to act as a winning tonic to our team. We had a few club handicaps at this meeting and in the 220 yards for Juniors, under 19, F. J. Skelley showed he was in sprinting form by winning from the 5 yards mark. G. H. Knight, a newcomer to our ranks, gave him a close race off 15 yards, and the scratch man, B. Saunders, ran well to gain third place. In the 2 Miles Walk, E. C. A. Heather made a welcome reappearance and, with the handicapper being kind to him, won off 475 yards, with another long-marker in W. G. True, off 650 yards, second. Joe Coleman walked with plenty of strength and determination to finish third. The 880 yards handicap was interesting because of the fine effort made by L. W. Herbert, off 25 yards. He cut through the field on the second lap, and won in fine style, with E. J. Selby (75) second, and S. Garland, off 45 yards, third. Our first field event handicap of the season was the Shot Putt and E. L. Blyther (13ft. 6in.) showed improvement over previous performances by taking first place with 38ft. 8in. R. E. Stride, Snr. (16ft. 0in.) was second with 37ft. 4in. and S. Jones (1ft. 0in.) did well with 37ft. 0in. to take third place. F. W. Pritchard F. W. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1937 season in Division I of the Southern Amateur Athletic League: the 4 x 880 yards, 4 x 220 yards, 1 mile and 3 miles team races, the 4 x 440 yards relay, the coming medley relay and the field events section.
items.s: THE SOUTHERN ATHLETIC LEAGUE. Review of Belgrave's 1937 season in Division I of the Southern Amateur Athletic League: the 4 x 880 yards, 4 x 220 yards, 1 mile and 3 miles team races, the 4 x 440 yards relay, the coming medley relay and the field events section. As already mentioned elsewhere in this issue, the first of the contests in the S.A.A.L., Division I, was the 4 x 880 yards held at Southgate, on May 15th. Owing to the earliness of the season, our team was not at full strength and some of the other competing clubs were in a similar position. Southgate made an excellent debut in the 1st Division by beating the Poly in a close race. The other placings were : Blackheath 3, Belgrave 4, Mitcham 5, and Herne Hill H. 6. The next event was the 4 x 220 yards at the "Kinnard" meeting at the White City. Sprinters have never been our strong point, and we were not very optimistic about our chances here. As expected, Blackheath were winners, with Herne Hill H. second, and the Poly third. Then came Southgate H., and we just managed to beat our rivals, Mitcham A.C., for last place. So far, results had not been too encouraging, but with the longer distances to come we were confident that we would be more to the fore. The 1 Mile team race was held at the White City in conjunction with the Civil Service meeting, and without doubt was the finest event on the programme. Pat Parker soon went to the front and led the field round at a good pace. Out team were running well, and the biggest danger appeared to be Blackheath. Over the last lap Hodges, of Southgate, went in front, followed by Poole, Blackheath, and A. V. Reeve, of the Poly. Pat had dropped to fifth place but by a determined effort down the straight he pegged one back and so finished 4th. W. E. Lucas had run well to gain 8th place, and Tom Carter and Ted Stimpson finished in 12th and 13th positions. We had to wait until the judges had sorted the men out and then came the result : Polytechnic H. 35 pts., Blackheath H 36 pts., Belgrave H. 37 pts. Thus we had lost first place by two points, and yet were placed only third. A closer finish could not be imagined and although scoring one point less than last year, when we were second, we were now one place worse off! We came then to the 3 Miles team race, which was held at the Herne Hill Track. In the individual race, D. B. Pell, of Herne Hill H., ran a fine race to win from Hodges, of Southgate, with Les Cohen, of our own club, third. We seem always to be the unlucky club when it comes to close finishes in team races; and this was no exception. When the points had been totalled up it was found that Mitcham A.C. scored 31, with Belgrave 32. Of the other members of our team, Tom Carter was 6th, with Arthur Penny 7th, while Harry Shields had an off day in being placed 16th. Thus, if Pat Parker had been there it would have been "in the bag," but I seem to remember other occasions when we have had cause to think of the old saying, "there's many a slip . . . . " The 4 x 440 yards was held on a Monday evening at the new Ladywell Park track. While not being the best of days on which to hold a sports meeting, the track was also in a very loose state, and the running of the meeting left much to be desired. As to the race itself, Polytechnic H. were the winners from Southgate H., with Herne Hill H. 3rd, Blackheath 4th, Mitcham A.C. 5th, and the "Bels" last. It must be said in fairness to our lads that on the previous day they had been on the Club's outing to Littlehampton and their strenuous exertions "by the sea" had not left them in a very fit state for running. The irony of the thing is that a week later the same team, with Eddie Park, taking the place of Tom Scrimshaw, gained third place in the A.A.A. 4 x 440 yards relay! The last event in the League programme is the 1 Mile Medley Relay on August 21st, at Herne Hill. We have not been able to ascertain the correct league placings, but are informed that we lead Herne Hill H. and Mitcham A.C. by 1 point for last place. As the bottom club is relegated to the 2nd Division, it looks as if there is every possibility of the "Bels" being the unlucky one. However, the race had not been run yet, so here's hoping! Whatever the result, I am sure our boys will enter upon next season's contests with just the same enthusiasm they have shewn during the present one, which after all is the spirit we want. The results can look after themselves. As regards the Field Events Section of the League, I understand we are at present leading in this contest, but here again we have been unable to find out the positions in the table. It seems as though this season has not shewn quite the same success as in the past. By this I mean among the clubs generally; and it looks very much as if the whole position will have to be overhauled at the next A.G.M. of the S.A.A.L. items.sum: Report of the second Inter-Club relay contest at the Croydon Harriers' ground on June 1st (4 x 100, 4 x 880, 4 x 300 yards and mile team race), leaving Belgrave leading Mitcham on points.
items.s: INTER-CLUB RELAYS AT CROYDON. Report of the second Inter-Club relay contest at the Croydon Harriers' ground on June 1st (4 x 100, 4 x 880, 4 x 300 yards and mile team race), leaving Belgrave leading Mitcham on points. The second Inter-Club relay contest was held on June 1st at the Croydon Harriers' ground. Mitcham appeared to have a stronger team and seemed out to prevent a repetition of the Tooting result. In the 4 x 100 yards Mitcham were first with ourselves just beating Croydon for second place. The 4 x 880 yards saw a ding-dong battle between the "Mental Hospital" boys and our lads; and over the first leg Frank Webb was just beaten by Leadbeater. P. Dee, the Welsh "crack," went next, with Alby Bird in hot pursuit. The leader, however, was not to be caught and, running in strong style, increased his club's lead. Our Track Captain, Harry Shields, not only caught his rival, but sent L. W. Herbert off with a slight lead. Roberts, the young Mitcham runner, trailed his man well, but nearing home Herbert went away to win in convincing fashion. Our team in the 4 x 300 yards started off well, F. W. Pritchard giving us the lead which Botwright kept. We then ran G. Camkin, who was making his first appearance in these contests, but although he tried hard enough, Mitcham, and then Croydon, passed him. Tom Wiley was thus given a hopeless task in attempting to catch the leader, but running in determined style, he beat the Croydon runner down the straight to give us second place. We came then to the Mile team race and, after a good race, Mitcham beat us by two points. They had the first two home in Dee and Brickwood; and although our boys finished 4, 5, 6, 7, it was not good enough! Thus at the end of the evening the points up to date were: Belgrave H., 29; Mitcham A.C., 27; Epsom H., 12; Croydon H., 12. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Report of the club meeting on June 9th: a triangular match with Imperial College A.C. and Leigh-on-Sea Harriers, the Club 3 Miles Championship won by Les Cohen, club handicaps, a walk handicap and a novices' mile.
items.s: CLUB MEETING ON JUNE 9th. Report of the club meeting on June 9th: a triangular match with Imperial College A.C. and Leigh-on-Sea Harriers, the Club 3 Miles Championship won by Les Cohen, club handicaps, a walk handicap and a novices' mile. On this evening we had a triangular match with Imperial College A.C. and the Leigh-on-Sea Harriers. The Club 3 Miles Championship was also decided, and in addition we had two races open to unattached novices on the programme. Tom Wiley won the 100 yards match, with F. W. Pritchard third. An Imperial College man was second, with Leigh gaining fourth place. We also had first two home in the 220 yards, S. C. Botwright and F. W. Pritchard doing the needful. Pat Parker turned out for us in the Mile and won in easy fashion, with A. R. Shaw second. Towell, of Leigh, was third, with Britton, Imperial College, fourth. Eddie Pack was also a starter in the 440 yards match, but was content to take things easy after his Middlesex County win the previous Saturday. Alby Bird raced into the lead, with Pack following, and they finished in that order, with Leigh filling third and fourth places. We thus led easily on the track events, but some closer competition was seen in the field contests. F. Grassau did 37ft. 8½in. in the Shot Putt, and C. A. Melchior gained third place with 31ft. 4in. The High Jump saw Leigh and the Imperial College gaining the points; and in the Javelin, M. Bradley threw 147ft. 9in., to beat Melchior. T. C. Jones won the Long Jump match; and also proved the winner of the club Long Jump handicap. The 3 Miles club championship saw a field of 14, although Pat Parker decided not to compete. He rather wisely preferred to concentrate on the shorter distances until later in the season, and his running in the recent A.A.A. championships proved the wisdom of his decision. Ted Stimpson cut out the pace in the early stages, but a little bunch of runners soon moved up to him, and then J. C. Smart had bad luck in sustaining a fall which put him out of the race. We then saw Les Cohen, Tom Carter, and Arthur Penny move away from the rest; although Dan Patience was running well close behind. In the last lap a hectic struggle ensued. The pace proved too much for Penny, and down the straight Cohen got the better of Carter in a rousing finish. Dan Patience also sprinted past Arthur Penny near the tape, although it seemed as if the latter had thrown his hand in. 1st class standards were gained by A. W. Penny, A. H. Sampson (who ran very well over this distance), H. W. Shields and Arthur Allum. 2nd class medals were also gained by Alf Taylor and R. W. Tobin. In the club handicaps we saw F. J. Skelley run well to gain second place in the 100 yards, under 19. G. K. Talbot, with 7 yards start, proved the winner. Skelley was off 1 yard, and L. F. Barber, off 6 yards, was third. A newcomer in A. S. Blunden won the club 100 yards, off 8½ yards, with S. C. Botwright, off 7 yards (a mark he will not see again), second, and Alec Mewes, with 5½ yards, third. The latter certainly seems to run better in club handicaps than he does in open competition, but perhaps he is saving it up. Who knows? As was generally expected, W. E. Lucas took advantage of his mark to win the 880 yards in fast time. J. H. Chantler ran well to gain second place, with Tommy Morrell third. Apart from the winner, the finish was very close, a bunch of runners making a dash at the finishing line. In the 2 Miles Walk handicap, L. J. Coleman made good use of his mark; with another long marker in W. G. True, second. Charlie Redgrave made a welcome re-appearance and walked well to gain third place. With regard to the Novice events, owing to lack of entries we had to cancel the 100 yards, and only three runners turned out for the 1 Mile. The winner was N. Welsford in moderate time, and it really seems a pity we cannot get a better turn-out in these races. I am sure if only the club members would co-operate we should meet with more success. I trust that if we decide to hold these events in the future that all members will do their best to interest any of their friends who are, as yet, not attached to any recognised athletic club. items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's annual promotion of four scratch team walks (5, 3, 2 and 1 miles) at Battersea Park on June 14th, won by Woodford Green A.C. by one point from Belgrave; the 1 mile results print the fourth man's time as 7 min. 4 sec., faster than the winner's 7 min. 16 sec.
items.s: THE ANNUAL TRACK WALKS. Report and results of Belgrave's annual promotion of four scratch team walks (5, 3, 2 and 1 miles) at Battersea Park on June 14th, won by Woodford Green A.C. by one point from Belgrave; the 1 mile results print the fourth man's time as 7 min. 4 sec., faster than the winner's 7 min. 16 sec. Our annual promotion of four scratch walks at 5, 3, 2 and 1 miles was held at Battersea Park on June 14th, and nine clubs entered teams. The usual conditions were in force and two men were allowed in each event from each club, no man being allowed to turn out twice in the evening. 18 points were allocated to the winner's club, 17 points to second, and so on, downwards, in each event. The first race was at five miles and Redman (Metropolitan W.C.) and A. H. G. Pope (Woodford Green A.C.) had a spirited duel over the best part of the journey, which carried them well away from the other competitors. Both men are record-holders and their struggle was worthy of the high reputations both men bear in walking circles. Towards the end of the race, Redman drew on his reserves of strength and won by a distance. Our representatives were C. E. Churcher, who finished eighth, and A. Readman, who suffered disqualification. 1, F. Redman (M.W.C.), 37 min. 28 sec.; 2, A. H. Pope (W.G.A.C.) 38 min. 15 sec.; 3, L. P. Hancock (S.W.C.), 39 min. 4 sec.; 4, A. Foster (W.G.A.C.), 39 min. 51 sec.; 5, W. P. Everard (E.B.), 40 min. 1 sec.; 6, H. D. Neilson (Poly.) 40 min. 5 sec.; G. B. Whitlock (Met.), 40 min. 26 sec.; 8, C. E. Churcher (Bel.), 40 min. 30 sec. Points scored: Woodford Green A.C., 32 pts.; Metropolitan W.C., 30 pts.; Surrey W.C., 24 pts.; Polytechnic H., 22 pts.; Essex Beagles, 14 pts.; Belgrave H., 11 pts.; London Vidarians, 17 pts. The three miles event followed and in this Whitlock, Olympic Champion, and Cooper, A.A.A. champion, caused some excitement with the mixture of fast and slow walking they provided. Frequent bursts of speed were a feature of the first lap or so, but then Cooper went away to his usual easy win. Our representatives were Charlie Redgrave and Reg. Elson, who finished fourth and seventh respectively. 1, A. A. Cooper (W.G.A.C.), 22 min. 2 sec.; 2, H. H. Whitlock (Met.), 22 min. 24 sec.; 3, M. J. Fisher (S.W.C.), 23 min. 13 sec.; 4, C. W. Redgrave (Bel.), 24 min. 16 sec.; 5, A. Smith (W.G.A.C.), 24 min. 34 sec.; 6, A. Hart (E.B.), 25 min. 29 sec.; 7, R. F. Elson (Bel.), 25 min. 39 sec. Points: W.G.A.C., 32 pts.; Belgrave, 27 pts.; S.W.C., 27 pts.; E.B., 21 pts.; L.V., 19 pts.; Met., 17 pts. The two miles race lacked interest and we were able to help our score along by placing the first two men. Don Brown had an "easy," and Harley was not seriously troubled in taking second position. 1, D. E. Brown (Bel.), 14 min. 57 sec.; 2, A. A. Harley (Bel.), 15 min. 36 sec.; 3, W. Jones (Met.), 15 min. 50 sec.; 4, E. A. Manning (Poly.), 15 min. 59 sec. Points: Belgrave, 35 pts.; Poly, 28 pts.; W.G.A.C., 26 pts.; Met., 24 pts.; L.V., 20 pts.; S.W.C., 10 pts. The final event of the evening, a 1 Mile race, was a tussle between Percy Wright and A. H. Rayner (S.A.C.), the last-named prevailing down the straight. Our other man, G. H. Boddington, did well in finishing fourth. 1, A. H. Rayner (S.A.C.), 7 min. 16 sec.; 2, P. G. Wright (Bel.), 7 min. 17 sec.; 3, S. W Wright (W.G.A.C.), 7 min. 26 sec.; 4, G. H. Boddington (Bel.), 7 min. 4 sec. The final scoring gave Woodford Green a one point win over ourselves, and we congratulate them upon their first win. We were very glad to welcome eight visiting clubs for our "no entry fee—no award" competition and hope to see them all again next year. Our team would have been strengthened had we been able to call on A. L. Fletcher, W. A. Treacher, H. G. Churcher, J. G. Coleman and J. E. items.s: THE "DORIS" SHIELD CONTEST. Report of the annual "Doris" Shield match at Richmond on June 17th, won by Thames Valley H. from Belgrave and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C., with the handicap events for members of the three clubs. On June 17th we journeyed to Richmond for the annual "Doris" Shield match with Thames Valley H., and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. We were joint holders of the shield with T.V.H., but any hopes we might have had were rudely dispelled with the result of the 100 yards. Lester and Warner, both of T.V.H., were first and second, with Liffen, of Ashcombe-St. George's, third, and Tom Wiley fourth. In the 440 yards match we had Eddie Pack and he duly won from A. D. G. White, of T.V.H. They also had the third man in R. J. Green, and we were sadly lacking a second string in this race. Tom Wiley, who ran for us, did his best, but was clearly running beyond his distance. We fielded a useful team in the 2 Miles team race and Arthur Penny ran away from his opponents to win in 9 mins. 38 secs. J. C. Smart ran well to finish in second place, while our team was completed by H. G. Verney, the ex-Birchfield runner. The team race result was: Belgrave H., 1; Thames Valley H., 2; Ashcombe-St. George's, 3. With the last event to be decided our chances of even sharing the shield were gone, and Thames Valley consolidated their lead by winning the 1 Mile medley relay. Alec White beat Alby Bird over the half-mile stage, and although Dick Michael ran well in the 440 yards leg, Les. Bennett and S. C. Botwright could not hold the T.V.H. sprinters. Thus the final points scored were: Thames Valley H., 30; Belgrave H., 22; Ashcombe-St. George's A.C., 14. In the usual handicaps open to members of the three competing clubs, we saw J. Warner (who was second in the scratch race) receiving 7½ yards start and he won in 9 4-5 secs. A Belgrave junior in W. H. Bowers was second, off 10 yards, with a T.V.H. youngster, also off 10 yards, third. It was in every respect a long marker's race and the back men, to put it frankly, did not stand an "earthly." A small field was seen in the 2 Miles Walk, there being six Belgrave competitors and one Thames Valley man. Our Walking Hon. Sec., Alf Harley, walked well, however, to win, with Don Brown second, and Harry Churcher, off the scratch mark, third. A better race was seen in the 1 Mile handicap, and on the final lap it looked as if W. R. King, of T.V.H., off 135 yards, would be the winner. E. J. Selby, of the "Bels," off 115 yards, thought otherwise, however. Tommy Morrell, off 90 yards, also put in a spectacular finish and eventually King was placed third. Frank Webb, off 35 yards, ran well to finish a close fourth in what was quite a fast-run race. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Report and full results of the Belgrave club championship day on July 3rd, 1937, covering track, walk, field and junior events and a schools' medley relay won by Latymer Upper School.
items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP DAY, July 3rd, 1937. Report and full results of the Belgrave club championship day on July 3rd, 1937, covering track, walk, field and junior events and a schools' medley relay won by Latymer Upper School. We were certainly blesssed with fine weather on our Championship Day, and the performances, if not brilliant, were sound; and the finishes very close and keenly fought out. A new holder had to be found for the Boys, under 15, race, owing to the age limit, and A. V. Heitman, the winner, is full of promise. The newly-instituted 100 yards Junior race gave F. J. Skelley a chance to show his sprinting powers. In view of his successes at the Long Jump, we can certainly expect even better jumping, consequent upon his improved speed. In the 100 yards championship, E. Gray once again proved the best of our short distance men, and retained his hold on the "Grosvenor Cup." Tom Wiley gained one of his many place medals. He picked up four in all—quite a field day! We had been promised a good race in the 880 yards, and so it proved. Alby Bird ran finely to win in time which equalled Tommy Scrimshaw's record of 1 min. 59 1-5 sec. L. W. Herbert was a good second; and Dick Michael, the holder, had to be content with third place. For the first time we held a Junior 880 yards race, and although there was only a small field, it was a most interesting contest. H. G. Neve proved the winner. L. Marchant, who was second, is only 16 years of age, but with careful training should make them all go in a few years' time. As usual, the Mile provided the spectators with an exciting race, and a field of 18 faced the starter. Les Cohen soon showed that he was determined to keep in front; but W. E. Lucas hung on grimly, while our old war-horse, Arthur Penny, was not far behind. Round the last lap they went, but try as he would, Lucas could not get by, and down the straight Cohen strode away to win in 4 min. 33 secs. The 220 yards Junior saw the holder, B. Saunders, show a clean pair of heels to his rivals, although G. K. Talbot ran well to finish second, while R. S. Turner followed up his third in the 100, by filling the same position here. We had a surprise result in the 220 yards championship, for the holder, E. Gray, was beaten a foot by S. C. Botwright, who followed up his recent "Open" successes by annexing the "Elsie Cup." Botwright is a former club junior champion and gives promise of even better performances in the future. Owing to our date clashing with the Police championships, we were denied the sight of Eddie Pack beating the club record of 51 secs. in the 440 yards championship. The race, however, provided us with the closest finish of the day. Alby Bird and L. W. Herbert came down the straight locked together; and Alby gained the verdict by inches. Dick Michael lost another of his titles here, but ran well to finish a close third. Tommy Scrimshaw made a come-back in this race and gave us all a thrill by leading up to the home straight. We all hope to see Tommy once again racing fit, and he certainly has plenty of racing years left in him yet. The 2 Miles Walk saw the holder, W. A. Treacher, and Harry Churcher both non-starters. Don Brown, however, showed he is coming back to his best form by beating Percy Wright, with Joe Coleman pipping his young brother for third place. A feature of this race was the number of ex-runners competing (no offence meant!) and even our Percy has been seen tearing up the sprinters! Our five field event championships saw some good performances, and here again soundness of effort predominated. F. Grassau was an absentee from the Shot Putt and Bill Sutton gained first place with 35ft. 3in. Ben May gained his first place medal here and should gain encouragement from this. In the Javelin, C. A. Melchior became first holder of the "Dailey Cup" with a throw of 155ft. 8in.; and concentration on this particular event would see further improvement. The High Jump saw the holder, H. M. Quackenbos, who is our Junior Captain, retain his title with a leap of 5ft. 2in.; and here again increased height can be expected. "Bud" Hutchinson was second, and with more serious training might show us some of his Canadian form. S. Jones won the Discus Throw with Bill Sutton as runner-up. In fact one might say "the old firm" did their stuff! Another "Dailey Cup" was awarded to the winner of the Long Jump, and we are very grateful to the donor for these welcome additions to our club trophy list. F. J. Skelley, with a fine leap of 21ft. 6in., became the first holder of the cup, and E. Gray also jumped well with an effort of 20ft. 5in. The fact of Gray and Wiley being placed proves once again that speed is essential in this branch of sport. Jesse Owens is, of course, of course the most classic example, and I hope our junior long-jumpers will remember this most important factor. We had another event on our programme which proved quite a success, namely, a 1 Mile medley relay open to Schools. Six teams competed, and the Latymer Upper School ran home winners, due, in the main to a very fine run by their half-miler. This race was in the nature of an experiment and the result was gratifying to those who had urged its inclusion. We hope that next year we shall have an even bigger entry and so help develop the latent talent that these schools must possess. We trust our worthy Hon. Editor was wearing his "old school tie," and are sure he must have been pleased with his old school's victory. The number of standard medals gained in the various club championhips showed the interest that is taken in these awards, but we should like to see even greater interest, and trust that next year will see more club members entering these events. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Account of the club outing to Littlehampton on Sunday, July 4th, attended by about forty members and friends, praising Mick Walker's handling of an emergency on the journey.
items.s: THE CLUB OUTING. Account of the club outing to Littlehampton on Sunday, July 4th, attended by about forty members and friends, praising Mick Walker's handling of an emergency on the journey. A trip to Littlehampton was planned on Sunday, July 4th, and received a fair measure of support, about forty members and friends contributing to the gaiety of the occasion. Clouds threatened and a strong wind did its best to upset the party, but fortunately there was no rain. Football, cricket, rounders, swimming, rock-climbing (ask Footer!) passed the time, and contributed those aches and pains which were a feature of the next day. However, the trip was generally voted to be an excellent day out; and we record our grateful thanks to our Social Hon. Secretary for his work in connection with the outing. Deserving of special mention is the promptitude and celerity with which Mick Walker met a sudden emergency on the journey outwards. His quickness of thought and physical advantages combined to make him the man of the moment, and to transcend the now almost legendary Colley Hill incident with which the name of Shields is for ever linked. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Report of the club meeting on July 14th: a junior match with Thames Valley Harriers, won by Belgrave 3 events to 1, and club handicaps on track, walk and javelin.
items.s: THE CLUB MEETING ON JULY 14th. Report of the club meeting on July 14th: a junior match with Thames Valley Harriers, won by Belgrave 3 events to 1, and club handicaps on track, walk and javelin. On this evening we had a Junior match with our old friends, the Thames Valley Harriers, and also several club handicaps. The match events were to be on relay lines, but in the 100 yards event T.V.H. were only able to field two boys, and so we made it a scratch race only. F. J. Skelley won readily enough from W. L. Kuy, of T.V.H., with Belgrave filling the third and fourth positions. In the 880 yards Team race J. Bavage, of T.V.H., a very useful runner, won in 2 mins. 7 secs. They also had the second lad, with H. G. Neve, N. C. Shrubb, L. Marchant, all of Belgrave, in the 3rd, 4th and 5th positions. Thames Valley thus won the team race, and the score was "one all." Skelley did not jump for us in the Junior Long Jump, but the winner was a Belgrave lad, A. S. Peverell, who jumps with a good style and should certainly improve with steady training. The Thames Valley boy was second, with R. Dunford third. The final event was the 3 x 200 yards relay, and over the first leg G. K. Talbot gave us a useful lead. V. D. Wynyard went next, but Bavage, for T.V.H., slowly cut down his advantage. Wynyard held on, to send Skelley away in front of his rival. The latter ran well and did not give his opponent a chance to be on terms. We thus won the match by 3 events to 1, and are looking forward to the return match later in the season. In the 100 yards (under 16) handicap, a close final was seen, the scratch man, L. F. Barber, being beaten by inches by P. McMahon, off 8 yards; S. A. Bailey, off 1 yard, was third; with P. Kearney, Jnr., off 7, fourth. The 100 yards Veterans resulted in a win for A. V. Chetland; with H. H. Baumann, off scratch, second; and Dicky Best, third. Charlie Cook was also in the final, but did not display his customary "dash." For excitement the 880 yards handicap wanted some beating. First, Harry Shields, off 35 yards, looked like winning, but appeared to have made his effort too soon. Then A. H. Beaumont, off 65, went in front, only to be passed in the last few yards by S. Garland, off 42. The final placings were: Garland, Beaumont, Shields, with W. J. Ashford fourth. The 220 yards final was also a close affair, a few yards covering the five finalists. E. A. Keyworth, off 17 yards, proved the winner, with Alby Bird, off 12, second; and R. Shepherd, a junior, off 18, third. Dick Michael was a close fourth and Frank Webb was the other finalist. For three recognised half-milers to figure in a sprint final does not say much for the quality of our sprinters; but perhaps the handicapper was kind to them! Anyway, we will leave it at that! A good race was also seen in the club 2 Miles Walk handicap, J. A. Belchamber, a son of our past President, making good use of his 525 yards start, to lead until half-way round the last lap, where E. C. A. Heather, off 350 yards—a liberal mark—caught him although he only won by a few yards. Joe Coleman walked excellently off 175 yards to gain third place; with his brother "L.J." once again close behind him. There was a good field for the 2 Miles running handicap and another long-marker in W. F. Merryman, off 420, led throughout, to win in fast time. R. W. Tobin, off 300 yards, secured his first club prize in finishing second; and Pat Parker ran a really magnificent race to gain third place. He did 9 mins. 31 secs. all the way; form which augured well for his chance in the A.A.A. 3 Miles race the following Saturday. H. G. Verney also ran well to finish in fifth place, while Les Cohen was seventh off the scratch mark. He had to give Pat 5 yards start; but perhaps the boot will be on the other foot in the next handicap we have. Members of the running section gained first two awards in the Javelin throw handicap. S. Garland, with 65 feet allowance, was first; and Mick Walker, with 60 feet start, gained second place. Both Finneron and Melchior, also George Powell, were non-starters, otherwise the result might have been different. We are pleased, however, to see members outside the field events men themselves, taking part in these contests; and if they pay their share of the entry fees it is only right they should take their share of the prizes, too. Also on the programme was a 1 Mile Walk for Unattached Novices, but there were only two starters, the winner being W. F. Brunning, who we hope will not be discouraged by his lack of opposition. Why these novice events should fail to attract entries is really mystifying, unless, of course, there are no unattached men, all being members of the Belgrave, which is as it should be! F. J. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: G. S. Doubleday's report of the R.W.A. 50 kilos championship at Enfield, where the Metropolitan Walking Club took the Horlick Cup from Belgrave, with result.
items.s: THE R.W.A. 50 KILOS CHAMPIONSHIP. G. S. Doubleday's report of the R.W.A. 50 kilos championship at Enfield, where the Metropolitan Walking Club took the Horlick Cup from Belgrave, with result. This was held over a hilly 5-lap course from De Bohun's Farm, Enfield, nine clubs competing. It was fairly warm at the start, but cooled down considerably and a coldish wind blew towards the finish. After a couple of laps (12½ miles) the Metropolitan Walking Club had their three scoring men in seven positions, scoring 12 to our 25, but we had our seven men in the first 20 places, so we had plenty to draw upon for our three scoring men. At 18¾ miles M.W.C. led us 16—22; the Whitlock brothers being 1st and 3rd, their third man, Redman, having dropped to 10th. Fred Bentley was 6th. Fred Rickards was having a bad time, and had dropped back a little. Jack Bidgood and Colin Sutton were walking well together for our third scoring position. After 4 laps (with 6¼ miles to go), M.W.C. had a 4 point advantage. Rickards had recovered and was his old self again, and was coming along just behind Bentley. Bidgood was walking strongly two places behind. It was now seen that barring accident the M.W.C. would win, as with 1st and 3rd and only 3 to score, they held an enormous advantage. However, our men kept pegging away. H. H. Whitlock recorded his fourth successive win, being followed by D. H. Christie-Murrey, and his brother G. B. R. Then Woodford Green provided the next two men home, but their third man was well down the field. Then came our own trio, Rickards, Bentley and Bidgood, in 6th, 7th and 8th positions, scoring 21 points to the 16 pts. which the M.W.C. subsequently totalled. Of our non-scoring men, Sutton was always close at hand for our third position, but was content to finish outside first-class standard time ( 5 hrs. 5 mins.) and thus preserve his "Junior" status. His recent performances stamp him as a first-class distance walker. R. Martin, A. Readman and S. C. Roberts all gained second-clas standards (5 hrs. 15 mins.). Whilst offering the Metropolitan Walking Club our heartiest congratulations on winning the "Horlick Cup" from us (we have held it for the last 3 years), our men's performances indicate that the Cup will soon be back in our possession again. A feature of the race was that we started seven walkers (more than any other club), and that all seven finished a most difficult course. Our four men who did not take team medals, all gained second-class medals. We are grateful to our scoring trio for once again making a fine show on the Club's behalf, particularly as Bentley has been unable to train seriously owing to business difficulties, and that both Bidgood and Rickards have been off colour. items.h: BELGRAVE HARRIERS v. KENSINGTON ARGYLL A.A.
items.sum: Report of a match against Kensington Argyll A.A. at Southfields on July 10th, won easily by Belgrave, with an 880 yards handicap and a social evening.
items.s: BELGRAVE HARRIERS v. KENSINGTON ARGYLL A.A. Report of a match against Kensington Argyll A.A. at Southfields on July 10th, won easily by Belgrave, with an 880 yards handicap and a social evening. This fixture was contested at Southfields on July 10th and will not be found on our current list, but was arranged at short notice by one of the K.A.A.A. officials—none other than Percy Wright! Match events were held at 100 yards, 220 yards, 440 yards, 880 yards, Mile Walk and Mile Medley Relay. The programme commenced at 8 p.m., and let it suffice to say that Belgrave ran out easy winners, as expected. The Business House Club's athletic section is now being revived, and we were very glad to give a helping hand. In the Walk, amid strange cries, a Kensington Argyll man won easily—none other than Percy Wright! At the conclusion of a very pleasant fixture on a well-kept and nicely situated ground, we adjourned to the Pavilion for dancing, etc. Prizes were presented to the placed men in the 880 yard handicap (which attracted sixty entries from members of the two clubs and was won by N. Isaacs, with "Snake" Webb second, and E. Stimpson third) and a speech of welcome was made and seconded—by none other than Percy Wright. It may be said that all the Belgrave Harriers present enjoyed this Saturday evening fixture; and look forward to another match next season. No doubt it will be arranged and if so our gratitude will be due to none other than Percy Wright! items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes: second in Lewis's 25 Miles Outer Circle Walk, the R.W.A. 50 kilos title lost to Metropolitan W.C., a dead-heat win in the Polytechnic team walk, open handicap prize-winners and a call for cyclist attendants for the Brighton Walk. A team represented the Club in Lewis's 25 Miles Outer Circle Walk at Birmingham, and after a keen struggle with Leicester Walking Club, finished second. Our scoring men were: F. Rickards (6), J. C. Bidgood (7), C. F. Sutton (8) and A. Readman (17). Colin Sutton is proving himself a dependable distance walker, and should strengthen our Senior team next season. * * * * * As described elsewhere, after three successive wins in the R.W.A. 50 kilos Championship, we have lost the title to Metropolitan W.C. Their win was an impressive one, and their scoring three—Harold Whitlock (1), Rex Whitlock (3) and Fred Redman (11)—well deserved their gold Championship medals, and the honour of winning the first Senior Championship for their club. * * * * * In a letter of thanks for our written congratulations, the Metropolitan W.C. Hon. Secretary writes: "We are, of course, most gratified that we have won a Senior Championship at long last, and we shall always remember with gratitude the help and encouragement we have constantly received from your club." * * * * * Congratulations to Percy Wright upon obtaining an A.A.A. standard, and so qualifying for his Club Honours badge. * * * * * In Open track handicap our walkers have been prominent, and among the prize-winners have been noticed: J. G. Coleman (a double first), L. J. Coleman, P. G. Wright (twice), E. C. Heather (twice), A. A. Harley and J. Cade. * * * * * Cyclist attendants are wanted to assist our walkers in the Brighton Walk on September 4th. If you are able to assist in this way, or have a friend willing to help our men, please get in touch with our Walking Hon. Secretary. Proper assistance and careful attention can do much for a walker in this test, and it is hoped that all our men will have adequate assistance in their efforts on the Club's behalf. * * * * * In the Polytechnic H. Invitation 2 Miles Team Walk held at the Kinnaird Meeting, we dead-heated for first place with Woodford Green A.C. Our scoring team was J. G. Coleman, P. G. Wright, J. E. Rutland and C. E. Churcher. * * * * * The Winter season will soon be on us and we hope to have a successful time. We should be glad to welcome some new talent, and the Novice race held early in the season should provide an opportunity for our members who have not yet won a prize for walking; and for friends of members willing "to have a go." * * * * * All entries and enquiries should be addressed to: A. items.label: August 1937
items.sum: Review of the closing track season and preview of the remaining track fixtures and the winter cross-country programme, with entries to E. A. Duffett, Asst. Hon. Sec.
items.s: THE CLOSE SEASON. Review of the closing track season and preview of the remaining track fixtures and the winter cross-country programme, with entries to E. A. Duffett, Asst. Hon. Sec. Another track season will soon be over. (Thank Heaven! say the track captains, who are responsible for fielding teams in the various fixtures). Taken as a whole, however, I think we have done moderately well. New members have come in steadily and the club spirit is as well established as ever. As to results, after all the sport is the thing and although we are naturally pleased at any success we may gain, so long as our members enjoy their racing and the companionship of their club-mates, then we are satisfied that the club is proceeding along the right lines. As regards new members, especially the Junior ones, for Heaven's sake, if you feel that you are not making the progress you hoped, either athletically or as regards knowing your fellow-members, please get in touch with some of the club officials, who are always at Battersea Park. In a club of our size it is almost impossible to recognise every member, so I do ask you to make yourselves known, so that we can do our best on your behalf. One of the best ways of doing this is through the medium of club handicaps. By entering these you become known to the Handicapper (there are probably a few who wish they were not so well known to him!) and, moreover, you meet your fellow-members in competition and so become known to them. These remarks apply to track and cross-country alike and, with the Winter Season gradually approaching, I hope all our members will come along and sample the hospitality of "Belgrave Hall." Before coming to the start of our Winter fixtures, I would just like to comment on our remaining track dates. On August 18th we have arranged a Junior match with the Hercules A.C. (Streatham). This will be held on the Tooting Bec Track and I am sure the first meeting between us will be an interesting one. On Saturday, August 21st, we have our usual fixture with the Metropolitan Police A.C. at Imber Court. This is a fixture always looked forward to by our lads. Everything is done for the comfort of the athlete, and there is even an open air swimming bath after the serious side is finished. Unfortunately, on the same afternoon we have the 1 Mile Medley relay in the S.A.A.L., which will be at the Herne Hill Track, in connection with the Fire Brigade sports at this venue. We come then to our last track fixture, which is on August 28th, at Battersea Park. Our visitors in a series of match events will be the Cambridge Harriers and Highgate Harriers. It will be the first time we have had the pleasure of meeting Cambridge H., while Highgate are old and respected opponents. Also on the programme we have the following club handicaps: 100 yards, 1 Mile run, Discus Throw and High Jump. I trust we shall have good entries in this our last meeting of our Jubilee track season. And so off with the old love and on with the new; or, maybe, in this case it should be the other way round. I am sure we have some members who simply long for the winter to come round again. And here again a word to new members: if you are at a loose end during the winter afternoons, come along to Wimbledon and have a run out over the surrounding commons and parks. We have packs to suit all paces, and there is even what we term a sprinters' pack. This is composed of those members who do not want to do any serious racing over the country, but simply wish to keep fit until the track season comes round again. There is a wealth of wisdom in this, and for youngsters, especially, nothing can build up body and stamina more than a good steady jog over the country. We usually open at "Belgrave Hall," once known as St. John's Hall, but now re-decorated and the property of the club, about the last two weeks in September. On the first Saturday in October we hold the 3 miles running and 5 miles walking handicaps, open to all club members. The following week we have two Novice races, these being a 3 miles run and 3 miles walk. Entry is free and the races are open to all Unattached novices, and also Belgrave novices. I might mention that a prize at running does not debar you from competing in the walking event; and, of course, vice-versa. On October 23rd we have a match with the Tyrian club, which is composed of past and present members of the London University. We come, then, to the annual triangular fixture between Ashcombe-St. George's A.C., Thames Valley H. and ourselves. It is the former club's turn to stage the race, which will be held on October 30th. This race is an all-to-score affair, so the more that turn up from each club, the more the merrier is the race. On November 6th we are very pleased to welcome to Wimbledon the Cambridge University Cross Country club. With the South London Harriers, they will meet us in a triangular match over our course. Some of our lads have already had the pleasure of meeting the Cambridge athletes over their own course, as members of Mr. Holt's team in the annual match between these teams. The second Saturday in November is always the date for the South of Thames "Junior" Team race, and I hope all our members who are eligible for this (if in doubt, I will soon advise you) will do their best to turn out. We used to enter five teams for this race, but of late years, partly due to so many men getting barred, we have not done so well. By the time our next issue is before you, we shall have the Winter fixture cards printed; so I will comment on other forthcoming events at a later date. All entries, and any enquiries, to E. A. items.sum: Editorial notes: congratulations to H. Parker on his South of Thames presidency, on two weddings and on Eddie Pack's British Empire Games selection; a W. A. Rice memorial trophy; subscriptions; the coming visit of L'Union Sportive Metropolitaine and the Club Open 7 Miles Walk; and the club's representatives on outside bodies.
items.s: Editorial notes: congratulations to H. Parker on his South of Thames presidency, on two weddings and on Eddie Pack's British Empire Games selection; a W. A. Rice memorial trophy; subscriptions; the coming visit of L'Union Sportive Metropolitaine and the Club Open 7 Miles Walk; and the club's representatives on outside bodies. Heartiest congratulations to H. Parker, who was recently elected President of the South of the Thames Cross-country Association. We trust he will have the pleasure of handing the "Dewar" Shield to our team, as did W. H. Hare in 1929, when President of the Association. * * * * * Congratulations also to Alec Traquair and Pat. Parker, upon the occasion of their recent weddings. We wish them many years of happiness. * * * * * Our very heartiest congratulations and good wishes go to Eddie Pack upon his selection to accompany the team to visit Australia for the British Empire Games. The honour is well-deserved, and we are sure Eddie will fully justify his selection. Belgrave's sincerest good wishes will go with him! * * * * * A proposal that a trophy in memory of the late W. A. Rice should be purchased by his friends and presented to the Club in perpetuity, probably for the Junior 880 yards Championship, has received the Committee's endorsement. No subscription list will be circulated and no member will be asked to subscribe, but anyone among Bill's friends who would care to associate himself with the proposal is asked to get in touch with A. A. Harley, who is acting as Hon. Treasurer of this special fund. * * * * * The current year's subscriptions are now due and our Hon. Treasurer would be glad to receive all outstanding amounts. The early part of the Club year calls for heavy expenditure, and immediate payment of obligations to your Club would be very helpful. Probably the outstanding item of interest in the early part of our Winter programme is the visit of L'Union Sportive Metropolitaine to Wimbledon on Saturday, December 11th. This fixture is still subject to the approval of the governing bodies in both countries, but we are looking forward to interesting running and walking matches versus our Parisian friends. We have never yet entertained Continental visitors, but this may well be the forerunner of similar fixtures in the future. Teams from across the Channel have visited this country before for track and cross-country matches, but it must be a long while since a team from abroad contested a walking match. We write well in advance of the fixture and trust that nothing will intervene to prevent two of the most interesting team matches of recent time taking place. It is hoped that as many club members as possible will come along to assist, to give our friends a cordial welcome, and to support our teams. * * * * * Another date to remember is November 27th, when our Club Open 7 Miles Walk takes place from Wimbledon. We expect our usual fine tntry, and all those who come along may expect to see the pick of Southern walkers, and some fine walking and keen competition. The Road Walking Association have allocated the "Berman" Cup to our race, to be held for a year by the team winning the scratch team race. * * * * * It may be of interest to Club members to know the names of those representing them on the outside Committees and Associations. They are as follows :— Amateur Athletic Association (Southern Committee) : F. G. Thomson. Road Walking Association (Southern Committee) : F. G. Thomson (Past President, R.W.A.), and A. A. Harley. J. items.label: November 1937
items.h: The End of the Track Season.
items.sum: Report on the closing weeks of the 1937 track season: junior match at Richmond, the Inter-Club Relay Shield at Mitcham, the L.A.C. match, club handicaps, the Nevill Challenge Cup, relegation in the Southern Amateur Athletic League, Metropolitan Police at Imber Court and the final club meeting v Cambridge and Highgate Harriers. It closes with a review of the season, including the first share in the Waddilove Trophy and first place in an A.A.A. Relay Championship.
items.s: The End of the Track Season. Report on the closing weeks of the 1937 track season: junior match at Richmond, the Inter-Club Relay Shield at Mitcham, the L.A.C. match, club handicaps, the Nevill Challenge Cup, relegation in the Southern Amateur Athletic League, Metropolitan Police at Imber Court and the final club meeting v Cambridge and Highgate Harriers. It closes with a review of the season, including the first share in the Waddilove Trophy and first place in an A.A.A. Relay Championship. On July 22nd we had an enjoyable evening meeting at Richmond; our opponents being the Junior sides of Thames Valley H. and the Polytechnic H. Our Juniors were not so well represented as hoped, but nevertheless those that were there showed up very well. In the 880 yards N. C. Shrubb finished third, the winner being Bavage, of T.V.H., a fine young runner. The 440 yds. was won by V. D. Wynyard, of the "Bels," who ran away from his rivals in quite fast time. We also gained third place in the 220 yds. with W. H. Bowers. The final points were: Poly H. 30, T.V.H. 29, Belgrave 24; and I am sure all our boys enjoyed their evening very much. On the 28th July was held the final Inter-Club Relay Shield meeting at Mitcham. We had a good turn-out and won all four events, our boys being at the top of their form. In the 4 x 300 yds. we had Eddie Pack doing the last leg and although the shape of the track was not suitable to his huge stride, he soon put the issue beyond doubt. We had previously won both the 4 x 100 yards. and 4 x 880 yds. In the latter, Alby Bird had a comfortable run over the last stage, Dee, the Welsh crack, preferring to take things easy when he saw Alby go off about 30 yds. in front of him. The 1 Mile team race provided the large crowd with a big thrill; Les Cohen and Thorogood, the A.A.A. Indoor 2 Mile Champion, having a ding-dong battle over the last 200 yds. Cohen stayed home the better and so paved the way for a win in the team race, Arthur Penny also running extremely well. Incidentally, our score of 60 points is the best scored in the series of contests for the Shield since its inception in 1925. On Saturday, July 31st, we had as visitors to Battersea Park old friends and rivals, the London Athletic Club. They seemed to be still smarting under the partial reverse we inflicted on them at Birmingham and so turned out quite a strong side. G. R. Dowling accomplished a very fine performance in winning the 100 yds., also the 440 yds., and being placed 2nd in the 220 yds. With J. V. Powell winning the 880 yds. and 1 Mile, these two runners were mainly responsible for the L.A.C. winning the match by 26 pts. to 22. We did, however, manage to have the first two in the Shot Putt, and S. Jones with 37ft. 1in. and Bill Sutton with 36ft. 9½in. are to be complimented on the steady improvement they are showing at this branch of sport. Also at this meeting we had some Club Handicaps, one being the newly innovated 880 yds. Junior race. L. Marchant proved a ready winner and looks like being a real champion in a few years' time. A very small field turned out for the Club 880 yds. handicap, and here W. J. Ashford won, with none other than Percy Wright second, and S. Garland third. Percy showed himself to be no mean runner, so now we know why he has met with such success in the walking world! In the 220 yds. handicap A. S. Blunden ran finely to win, with H. B. Taylor second, and F. W. Pritchard third. Blunden and Pritchard have also been well to the fore in our sprint relay teams and it certainly looks that at last we have some sprinters worthy of the name. In the 2 Miles run, J. C. Edwards made good use of his 350 yds. start with H. G. Verney showing some of his old-time form by securing second place. R. W. Tobin also showed continued improvement by gaining third place, and should prove an asset to our cross-country teams. On Wednesday, August 11th, we had our usual evening meeting and in the 100 yards handicap J. C. Bright showed promising form to win. S. C. Botwright, off 2 yds., was second, with Dicky Best, off 19 yds., third. The 1 Mile handicap was won by a newcomer, J. O. Goodman, and the manner in which he won made quite a few people open their eyes! He is as yet very inexperienced; but he is definitely one of the most promising track runners we have had for some time. Second place was taken by J. T. Beer, who is only just out of the junior stage, but who shows steady improvement; while F. H. C. White ran extremely well off 60 yds. to gain third place. This was Fred's first appearance in "miles," but he was more than satisfied at the result. The 440 yds. was very poorly supported, and S. C. Botwright made good use of his liberal mark to win, with Eddie Pack doing inside 50 seconds to gain second place. R. G. Michael was third, but the main feature of this race was Pack's fine running from the scratch mark. In the 2 Miles Walk Handicap the long-markers predominated, and J. A. Bellchambers was the winner, with Reg. Elson second, and E. G. Cornish third. We also had two field event handicaps and in the Shot Putt the winner was, yes! Frank Webb. He made good use of his 16ft. start to win with 37ft. 6in., with Bill Sutton 37ft. 1½in., and George Powell 36ft. 10½in. In the Long Jump, F. W. Pritchard was first with 21ft. 2in, Tom Wiley 20ft. 9in., and Micky Walker third. You will notice how our non-field event members keep popping up in the placings, so come on, you field event wallahs and do your stuff! On the 18th August we had a team running for the "Nevill Challenge Cup" and they did very well to gain second place, being beaten by a strong Achilles team. Most of the other London clubs were competing and our runners are to be complimented on their fine showing against such opposition. The final event in the Southern Amateur Athletic League—the 1 Mile medley relay—was held at Herne Hill on August 21st. Owing to holidays we were devoid of any of our recognised half-milers, and so Bill Lucas was pressed into service. With Pell running for Herne Hill, and Eeles for Southgate, also Williams of Poly., our chances of beating these clubs were slight. To make matters worse, at the last moment Eddie Pack was forced to cry off, and so Fred White had to be asked to do the 440. Actually Fred was there to run in the 1 Mile open, so that to ask him to do a quarter in such company was—well, you ought to have heard what he said! Nevertheless he ran, and although handing over last we must thank him for helping us out of a hole. Our sprinters gained slightly on the other clubs, and Bill Lucas went off just behind Eeles, but well behind the main bunch. Eeles set a scorching pace, but Bill followed him through and our hopes began to rise. At the bell Pell went in front and soon had the race in hand, but Lucas was now feeling that fast first lap, and although overtaking Poole of Blackheath, he was unable to gain any further places. With Herne Hill and Mitcham, who were our nearest rivals in the league table, gaining first and third places, this left us "holding the baby," and so next season will see us in the Second Division. They say the second division is not so bad (I mean, of course, in "jail"), so let us hope we shall find it the same in the league, and I am sure our boys will do their best to make their stay as short as possible. On the same day we had a fixture at Imber Court with the Metropolitan Police and although our forces were very much depleted, those who did go enjoyed the afternoon's sport. Thanks to our walkers and field events section, we put up quite a good showing, but hope that next season this fixture will not clash, as apart from whether we do well or badly, we do at least like to show our hosts the common courtesy of turning out a full side. We had our final club meeting on August 28th, at Battersea Park, our visitors being Cambridge Harriers, and the Highgate Harriers. Some good running was seen in the match events, the 440 yards having quite an exciting finish when L. W. Herbert came with a late burst to win on the tape. W. E. Lucas won the match 880 yds. and also gave us the lead over the same stage in the relay. Alby Bird came over from Tooting, where he had run in the Inter-Counties match to do the 440 yds. in the relay, and we won comfortably. Herbert had also been running for his County at Tooting, and we admire the club spirit which prompted these members to undertake such a strenuous afternoon's work. Our Juniors also had the same clubs in opposition in three junior events. We won both the 3 x 100 yds. and 3 x 200 yds. races; while the 880 yds. team was won by Cambridge H., with the "Bels" second. We would like to thank our opponents for providing us with a very interesting meeting, and would particularly like to thank the Cambridge Harriers' officials who came along and helped. At this period of the year, not only is it difficult to field teams, but even the officials must take their holidays some time. At this meeting we held a few club handicaps and in the 100 yds. G. K. Talbot, one of our junior members, proved the winner. H. B. Taylor was second, with W. Timberlake third. The 1 Mile was won by J. T. Beer, who improved upon his second place at the last meeting. Jack Flower showed a welcome return to some of his old form by gaining second place, with R. W. Tobin third. The way Jack came down the finishing straight was reminiscent of some of his best performances, and we hope he will also find his form over the country. The High Jump handicap was won by L. Jackson, who is our new Field events Vice-Captain, with C. A. Melchior second, and Frank Webb third. Frank certainly supports these field events very well and I am sure no one grudges him his successes. In the Discus Throw, G. R. Crawley made good use of his allowance to win, and his success is not out of turn. S. Jones was second, with L. Jackson bagging another by being third. We seem to be getting the right fellows in our field events. With Bill Sutton as Captain and Jackson to assist him—not forgetting George Powell, who although handicapped by his hours of work, still contrives to come along and give our young members the benefit of his great experience—we should eventually build up a section second to none. So ends another track season and, although on first thoughts we might appear to have had a bad season, actually, on performances it is one of our best to date. True, we lost our place in the S.A.A.L. 1st division, but against this we won the Inter-Club Relay Shield with the highest total of points ever scored. We also gained our first share in the "Waddilove" Trophy; and what is more important, our first place in an A.A.A. Relay Championship. We also had more Junior matches than ever previously, and the results prove that we have as fine a lot of junior runners as any club in the land. It is the junior of to-day who is the senior of to-morrow and the motto of any club should be "look to the juniors." We have been particularly well blessed in having H. M. Quackenbos as Junior captain, and we all regret the fact that owing to exams., etc., he will not be able to devote so much time during next summer as previously. But the seed has been well sown and we hope that next year will see our juniors more to the fore than ever, and so make us realise our ambition of seeing Belgrave as strong a club on the track as they are over the country, and in the walking world. items.s: The Annual General Meeting. Report of the club Annual General Meeting held on 23 September 1937 at the club hall at Wimbledon, with life memberships and the sub-committees appointed at the first Committee meeting. This year's A.G.M. was held on September 23rd, at our own Hall at Wimbledon. A fair number of members attended, and the reports of Hon. Secretary and Hon. Treasurer were well received. The Balance Sheet revealed a satisfying state of affairs, and gave evidence of the Club's progress in the matter of the acquisition of its own quarters. The election of Officers, headed by that of W. L. Bayliss, who will again serve the Club as President and Hon. Secretary, proceeded, and a full list of those responsible for the government of the Club during this season will be found in the Club Handbook and Winter Fixture List. Incidentally, if you have not yet received your copy, a line should be sent to the Hon. Secretary. The Meeting unanimously elected G. H. Powell and F. Rickards to Life Membership, upon the recommendation of the Committee. Several matters were raised under "Other Business" and referred to the new Committee for their attention, and a Vote of Thanks to the Chairman closed the Meeting. * * * * * At the first Committee meeting, J. R. McKay was re-elected as an Hon. Auditor, and the Hon. Editor and Assistant Hon. Editors were re-elected. The following Sub-commtitees were appointed : FINANCE : Messrs. Hare, Harley, Parker, Thomson, and Executive Officers ex-officio. SOCIAL : Messrs. Bennett, Carter, C. E. Churcher, Harley, the Social Hon. Secretary, and Executive Officers ex-officio. items.label: November 1937
items.sum: Summary, given at the A.G.M., of the club's achievements and disappointments in its 1936-37 Jubilee Year across track, cross country and walking.
items.s: Our Jubilee Year. Summary, given at the A.G.M., of the club's achievements and disappointments in its 1936-37 Jubilee Year across track, cross country and walking. For those unable to be present at the Club's Annual General Meeting, we give a summary of the happenings in our Jubilee Year. We have set ourselves a high standard in recent years and of necessity must expect an occasional disappointment. Our greatest disappointment came in the shape of relegation to Division II of the Southern Amateur Athletic League. Some perfectly sound reasons could be given for this failure, but we will content ourselves with saying that we hope to regain our status next season. Our Jubilee Year was notable for several excellent performances. Harry Churcher walked seven miles in an A.A.A. Championship, faster than any Englishman had ever done previously; and Jim Ginty is the first Belgrave man to be placed in the English Cross-country Championship. Eddie Pack recorded 49 1-5 seconds in finishing fourth in the A.A.A. 440 yards Championship; and for the first time on record, a Club team was placed third in an A.A.A. Relay Championship. Over the country our team recorded its "lowest ever" on points in the English Championships, and failed to win by four points only. For the first time, a Belgrave team went abroad, at the invitation of L'Union Sportive Metropolitaine, and scored a very fine win in a well-contested race. The Surrey Junior and Senior Championships were won by our teams, and the Brighton Relay lost by a bare yard. Our walkers maintained their usual prominence and team positions in the most important races were : R.W.A. Junior Championship, 3rd; R.W.A. Senior Championship, 3rd; R.W.A. 50 Kilos Championship, 2nd; and Brighton Walk, 1st—a very fine record. In many respects, we enjoyed our best track season yet. Our members were very prominent in the A.A.A. Championships and other races, and we were gratified at sharing the "Waddilove Bowl" with the L.A.C. on our first visit to the Birchfield Harriers' annual meeting. The "Inter-club Relay Shield" was won by a decisive margin, and a special word of thanks is due to H. W. Shieds on his efforts in arranging teams. Our Field Events men were well up to their usual standard, and we were pleased to witness J. Dodd's win in the A.A.A. Pole Vault Championship. Skelley and Finneron were also prominent during the season. In track walking, H. G. Churcher was prominent, as already mentioned, and D. E. Brown and P. G. Wright were third and fourth respectively in the A.A.A. 2 Miles Championship. So much for performances. The Club carried through its Winter and Summer season most successfully, although the absence of reasonable dressing accommodation at Battersea Park was a severe handicap. However, the newly-equipped Pavilion is now in use, and will be fully appreciated next season. Innovations in our Jubilee Year were the introduction of Junior Championships (under 19) at 100 yards, 220 yards and 880 yards, and the award of standard medals in connection with our Field Events Championships. We would express our gratitude to Mr. Daily for the presentation of trophies for our Long Jump and Javelin Championships. The Club promoted the usual 7 miles Open Walk in November, and Inter-Club scratch walks in June. A most successful Jubilee Dinner and Dance was held; and numerous Socials, Dances and a Summer Outing contributed much towards the social life of the Club, for which our thanks are due to our Social Hon. Secretary. Probably the most important event of all during the year, however, was the fact that the leasehold deeds of Belgrave Hall were handed over to the Club. Thus an ideal, present in the minds of many members for years past, became a reality, and now we seek to consolidate our position and plan further improvements. To conclude, we can look back upon our Jubilee Year as one in which much was accomplished, and the Club's sincerest thanks are due to those who have served it in any way. items.sum: Look back at the October and November 1927 Gazettes: W. H. Hare elected President, T. W. Green's Brighton Walk debut, a club road run and the Club Open Walk.
items.s: Ten Years Back. Look back at the October and November 1927 Gazettes: W. H. Hare elected President, T. W. Green's Brighton Walk debut, a club road run and the Club Open Walk. A glance ten years back to our "Gazette" of October, 1927, is of interest. This was the first issue to appear in the now familiar claret and gold cover, and was edited by B. J. T. Knifton. In this issue we read of the Club's sorrow at the passing of its President, R. W. Ricketts; of an A.G.M. at which W. H. Hare was elected President, and W. L. Bayliss took over the Hon. Secretaryship, in succession to F. G. Thomson. T. W. Green had just made his first attempt in the Brighton Walk and had finished second to the Italian, Giani. The Belgrave team (Green, Rathbone, Manning) was successful in the team race by one point, from Surrey Walking Club. An interesting debûtant in our Three Miles Road Run at Wimbledon was T. H. Scrimshaw. With 1 min. 50 sec. allowance, he finished next to last! W. G. Webb ran in his first Club race on that day, finishing 8th, and beating the Hon. Editor by one second. Scratch man was E. A. Duffett, who finished fifth. F. H. Elson's name appears for the first time. The November issue contains the present Hon. Editor's first contribution to our Gazette—an alleged humorous article entitled "The New Terror," dealing, if you please, with the menace of an Hon. Editor who stalks the land demanding articles for the Club journal! Belgrave easily won the triangular fixture v. Thames Valley H. and Ashcombe A.C., E. A. Duffett leading the field home. The same issue shows T. W. Green winning the Club Open Walk, with a Belgrave team (Green, Fletcher, H. F. King and Scamell) winning the scratch team race. These were the happenings of ten years ago! items.label: November 1937
items.sum: Report of the London to Brighton Walk on 3 September 1937, won by Harold Whitlock for the fourth successive year, with Belgrave regaining the Edward Knott Memorial Shield and Fred Rickards winning the Club Long Distance Walking Championship.
items.s: The Brighton Walk. Report of the London to Brighton Walk on 3 September 1937, won by Harold Whitlock for the fourth successive year, with Belgrave regaining the Edward Knott Memorial Shield and Fred Rickards winning the Club Long Distance Walking Championship. Eleven Belgrave walkers entered this year's race to Brighton, and all eleven were present at the start, at 7 a.m. exactly, on September 3rd. Due to the presence of an unknown quantity in the race, W. Cummings, champion of British Guiana, the pace in the early stages was very fast. Our visitor began to fall back at seven miles, however, leaving Harold Whitlock in the lead, which he retained to the end. At Redhill, Whitlock was two and a half minutes in front of record, and gained yet another minute before Horley was reached. From this point he slowly lost ground and at Handcross was behind his 1935 figures. Eventually he finished the course in 8h. 2m. 38s. and scored his fourth successive win—a really splendid record worthy of the heartiest congratulations. J. F. L. Henderson, winner of the London—Brighton and Back Walk earlier in the season, walked steadily throughout to finish second. Third came our Fred Rickards. With six miles to go, Fred was in second position, but a bad time in the last three miles enabled Henderson to take second place. Fred's time was, however, within a few seconds of his previous best, and his wonderfully fine performance at 39 years of age should inspire many of our younger members. Our next to finish, in eleventh position, was Colin Sutton. He completed the course in 8h. 49m. 40s.—a wonderfully fine first attempt. Throughout Colin walked well within himself, and at an even pace, as though he were a veteran in experience on the Brighton road. No less meritorious was the walking of W. Urry, who followed Sutton. He, also, was making his first attempt in this race and showed fine judgment. It is most unusual for two men to finish in the first dozen at their first attempts, and we heartily congratulate Sutton and Urry. Our team was completed by R. Martin, who finished in 17th position. Bob has served us well in Brighton Walks on many occasions, and again he contributed his part towards another Belgrave win. Our score of 43 points gave us a reasonably easy win over Woodford Green A.C., and we regained our hold on the "Edward Knott Memorial Shield." Third were Leicester W.C., and the promoters, Surrey Walking Club, fourth. E. L. Reeve, remembered by many as a prominent Club walker in years past, was our next to finish. He was 42nd, and followed by D. Willis. A comparative newcomer, Harry Thaxter, did well to finish 46th, and beat ten hours at his first attemptt. S. Bicknell, a member we see but rarely, and G. S. Doubleday, taking a holiday from marathon running, both pluckily finished the course despite badly blistered feet. A. A. Harley and B. H. Clark retired from the race at Crawley, when recording useful times, and both will, no doubt, find this year's experience of use in future races. Among those finishing the course were two second-claim members, W. E. Ives, whose time was 10h. 24m. 3s., and A. H. G. Pope, who finished 5th in 8h. 34m. 37s. The Club Long Distance Walking Championship was decided in conjunction, and the "Belgrave Cup" and championship medal goes, of course, to Fred Rickards. C. F. Sutton takes second medal, and W. Urry third. Incidentally Urry also won the prize for the first unplaced "Service" athlete to finish. A pleasing feature of the race was the fact that we entered more walkers than any other club. We were very glad to regain the Team Shield, particularly as our chances were not considered too rosy by outsiders, in the absence of old stalwarts in J. C. Bidgood and F. E. Bentley. It did prove conclusively that we have young walkers capable of keeping up the high standard our walkers have set in past years. Once again, our very sincere thanks are due to all who helped our walkers as attendants. Without the sympathetic co-operation of this gallant band of workers, the walkers would find it very difficult indeed. When thinking of our team win and the excellent performances of our walkers, we are all reminded of those who helped to make it possible—the attendants. A happy party made the journey homewards in the Club bus. Supporters, walkers, attendants, and Frank Thomson only knows how many cycles, were allocated positions. We hear that one or two decided that inside, perhaps, after all, was best! And so homewards, with another Brighton team win to our credit. h. m. s. 1. H. H. Whitlock (Met. W.C.) 8 2 38 2. J. F.
