items.s: The Three Miles Road Race. Report and full result of the club Three Miles Road Race handicap on 1 October 1938 over a new hilly course, won by Lionel Penny from N. C. Shrubb, with Arthur Penny fastest in 15 mins. 5 secs. 1st October, 1938. This year a different course was used. Instead of going out to the Windmill and home via that rough road across the Common and through the village, a lap of the hills was done. The actual times of the runners would suggest that the course is a little longer than the old one. Our old friend, George Still, started first, the last to start was Arthur Penny, who, although not on the scratch mark, gave proof of his fitness by clocking 15 mins. 5 secs. to record the fastest time. A. W. Jerman give us a good performance, being second fastest. The first to arrive was Lionel Penny, who was followed home by our promising junior, N. C. Shrubb. Then came our old friend, Bert Lindsey, to whom this race must have seemed like a sprint after his marathon efforts. Bert Smith was fourth. No doubt this will urge him on in his next handicap to gain those few seconds and so gain a place. Lionel's win was, no doubt, a great satisfaction to Arthur, whose years of experience, and his proven ability, enable him to give much useful brotherly advice. As regards the result as a whole, well, nobody can really expect fast times from everybody; some are fit, whilst others use this race as a loosener for the more serious work to come. RESULT. Pos. items.sum: Report on the two three-mile road novice races, open to Belgrave and unattached novices, which brought in new members.
items.s: Novice Races. Report on the two three-mile road novice races, open to Belgrave and unattached novices, which brought in new members. These races were open to both Belgrave and unattached novices and were both held on the road over three miles. They were instrumental in bringing us new members, which is, after all, the object of them. Many of the competitors gave useful performances, which they will soon be improving on if they are given the necessary encouragement and training. It is now up to them, for they have now only to report to their respective captains or vice-captains. We welcome them to the Club and wish them every success in their future races.

items.label: December 1938
items.sum: F. A. Walker's report of the season's first cross-country race, against Ealing H. from the Ballot Box, Perivale, won easily by Belgrave with A. R. Shaw first home; the printed result skips 14th place and its team scores do not match the club letters in the list.
items.s: Run v. Ealing H.—15th October. F. A. Walker's report of the season's first cross-country race, against Ealing H. from the Ballot Box, Perivale, won easily by Belgrave with A. R. Shaw first home; the printed result skips 14th place and its team scores do not match the club letters in the list. By F. A. Walker. Our first cross-country race of the season was against Ealing H. from their headquarters, the Ballot Box, Perivale. The team we sent was a strong one—good enough to win a "National"—if all were fit! The course was a fairly fast one. The Ealing fellows got away very fast at the start, having about a dozen men in the lead for the first three-quarters of a mile. After that they faded away one by one, then our lads had a "social" run amongst themselves. About two miles out we came across a miniature Everest which we had to climb, and what a climb! A. R. Shaw was the first man home, closely followed by six more Bels.; then two Ealing lads came in to split up the rest of our boys from the leaders. As we had the next five home we ran out easy winners. items.s: Match v. London University A.C. Report of the race over the club's 5 miles course at Wimbledon on 22 October against London University A.C., run with a club sealed handicap, led home by Arthur Penny, Bert Footer and Dan Patience. H. M. Quackenbos was second London man; A. T. Harper won the handicap; full club placings follow. The text names A. E. Smith third in the handicap where the table prints A. Smith. On Saturday, October 22nd, at Wimbledon, we entertained the members of the London University A.C. to a race over our 5 miles course. They were using this fixture as a trial for their runners, while we had our club sealed handicap in conjunction, so that a field of about 85 turned out. As most of our seniors were running they naturally soon went to the front, and eventually a small bunch of 3 runners drew away from the rest of the field. These were Arthur Penny, Bert Footer and Dan Patience. In the run home Arthur just beat Bert, with Dan third. We then had 10 more more "Bels" before the first London man, who was Alonzo, a member of the Blackheath Harriers. The second London man was none other than our own Junior Captain, H. M. Quackenbos. For the purpose of team scoring we deleted all our seniors, and this made W. E. Lucas—who was actually 7th in the race—first home, with G. Murdock and Tom Morrell next. We were easy winners on points, but trust our opponents enjoyed their run over our course. Our club handicap was won by A. T. Harper, who finished 20th in the actual race, and with 4-20 start he returned a net time of 27m. 27s. M. F. Edwards was second, his net time being 27m. 32s. Third place was taken by A. E. Smith. whose net time was 27m. 40s. We were pleased to see our prospective South of Thames Junior teams running well to the fore, and a newcomer in V. L. Green showed promising form. He comes to us from the Portsmouth A.C. and we hope he will enjoy his membership with the "Bels." Jimmy Kemp also displayed good form and we hope that he will retain it throughout the season, as so often Jimmy begins the season well and then fails to make our teams when the real "tests" come along. It was also good to see George Still "still going strong" (no pun), and even at his time of life he managed to beat a few of the young' uns. items.s: Match v. T.V.H. and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. October 29th. A. S. Lindsey's report of the five-and-a-half-mile match at Cranford against T.V.H. and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C., where "A" men paced prospective South of the Thames juniors and Belgrave won by a big margin. Ashcombe took the first three places but were third; the result lists club letters and team scores as printed (Belgrave's nine places add to 102, not the printed 82; the results list jumps between 34 and 37 out of order). By A. S. Lindsey. The fact that over 30 of the Bels. travelled to Cranford for this fixture shows that it is still as popular as ever. There was an extra interest in the race, as a scheme by the Cross-country Captain, whereby an "A" team man took charge of two prospective "South of the Thames" juniors for the purpose of team packing and keeping an even pace throughout the race was tried out. From the finishing positions of many Juniors, it can be seen that the scheme had a good deal of success. Especially in the case of Rispin, who ran strongly all the way to finish in the first dozen. Owing to some "A" men not turning out, Footer had more than his share of men to take along. At one stage of the race he looked like a pocket size standard-bearer going into action, surrounded by a high wall of stalwarts. The five and a half miles course was a two lap one, mainly flat grassland with about three-quarters of a mile of woods. Ashcombe led the field home with the first three men, but were third in the team race, nine a side scoring. Although our "A" men were concentrating on getting their charges along they all packed well and we enjoyed a big margin win. Nutty Penny gained a medal given by the home club for being the first scoring man of the visiting teams. RESULTS. TEAM SCORES. Belgrave H. (4, 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17) ... ... ... 82 pts. items.label: December 1938
items.sum: "Ubiquitor's" lively account of the race across the Aldershot Command sports fields on 5 November, with forty starters of whom ten were Belgrave Harriers. Dan. Patience won from Hutchings of the Command and Belgrave won 102—108.
items.s: Match v. Aldershot Command—Nov. 5th. "Ubiquitor's" lively account of the race across the Aldershot Command sports fields on 5 November, with forty starters of whom ten were Belgrave Harriers. Dan. Patience won from Hutchings of the Command and Belgrave won 102—108. By Ubiquitor. On the afternoon of the hottest November day for 97 years, forty starters raced across the well manured sports fields of the Aldershot Command and it is slightly to be regretted that only ten were Belgrave Harriers. In the opening rush black vests were well to the fore, but when the runners turned down Golf Lane, Frank Webb jumped to the lead to remind us that once he could show us the way round. But that was before the advent of youngsters like Arthur Penny & Co. It was here the runners picked up the famous "Aldershot horse" that acts as guide, and Jerman went ahead and collected a short lead all to himself. The field was very bunched, with black shirts (vests, I mean) all over the place. After about a mile, Jerman fell back and Kemp led a tight pack for a while along a road, until Charlie Smart decided that the road was obviously made for speed, and speeded. Jimmy Kemp thought it over and decided to help him along, so he moved up as well, but for the next couple of miles could not make up his mind whether he was running with Charlie Smart in the lead, or with Hutchings of the Command or even whether he was defintely third. But at half-way these three had a sixty yard lead from Dan. Patience, followed by a nasty black patch. Then came Arthur Penny in a sweater, trying to "kill" a cold and looking like a grease spot. Tobin had caught Frank Webb and they were having a regular argument, because Tobin could run uphill and no one can catch Frank going down, and the course was full of short, sharp ups and downs with a real pull here and there. Behind were Syd Ring and Verney, who was just settling down, Jerman and good-natured Alex Patience, who took upon himself the thankless task of being last man in the team. With about a mile to go the first three were fighting a ding-dong battle for the lead, when Dan. Patience evidently thought that someone should show how to run—and passed the lot! Hutchings hung on best and was rewarded with a second place. Kemp and Smart came in "all friendly like." Then there was a black outlook, slightly lightened by by Arthur's white sweater. Then, fortunately, Bels. showed they also could pack. With Verney running through to 11th, Ring pipping Tobin and Webb for 12th, Tobin (13) doing the dirty on Webb (14) (a real Knifey finish), Jerman (17), and Alex Patience (19) beating the last scoring Command man. All 10 men scored, and we won by the sporting margin of 6 points, 102—108, and admitted over an eggs and bacon tea that the race was good. The tea was very good and the sight of a sweat-covered and lathered horse gave a satisfaction not ordinarily enjoyed after racing. RESULTS. Belgrave H. items.s: South of Thames Junior Race. Report of the South of Thames C.C. Association's annual Junior Team race at Dartford on 12 November, with 34 teams and 243 runners, four of the teams Belgrave. Herne Hill Harriers won; Belgrave's "B" team was 4th and "A" team 7th after two "A" men blew out; teams and team positions follow. Tom Morrell is named in the "A" team but not in the printed team lists. On the 12th November the South of Thames C.C. Association held their annual Junior Team race at Dartford. 34 teams faced the starter, and four of these were representing the "Bels." There was a field of 243 runners and they made a fine sight streaming across the country. Unfortunately our "A" team were drawn on the extreme outside, and owing to the spectators encroaching at the start they found themselves badly away. Bill Lucas soon worked his way into the first half-dozen runners, but the others were always fighting hard to get through the large field. It was a course of three laps, and as this included a fairly steep hill, it was not exactly an easy run, but a good feature from our point of view was that practically all our men gained ground each lap. This was especially noticeable in the final lap, but unfortunately their fine efforts proved to be in vain. We had 7 runners in the first 31 home in the race, and when it will be seen that Herne Hill Harriers won the team race with their fourth man scoring 34th, it must be wondered why we had no team placed in the first three. Well, it all resolved upon that very ticklish question, "team selection." As stated, we had four teams entered and our "B" team beat the "A" while E. H. Herbert, who was actually in the "C" team, finished 27th and beat all but two of the "A" team. All the talking in the world will not alter the result now, but to put the matter frankly, it was a question of two of our "A" team men, namely, V. L. Green and Tom Morrell, "blowing out" while our "B" team actually ran above all their previous form and so put the "cat among the pigeons." Whatever the team result, we can console ourselves with the fact that our Juniors proved themselves the best of any other club, and as most of them are young in years, as they grow older and gain more experience we can look forward to the future of our senior teams with every confidence. e: Belgrave v. Cambridge University Hare and Hounds
items.s: Match v. Cambridge University Hare and Hounds. November 19th. Harry Shields' report of the new fixture against Cambridge University Hare and Hounds on a 7½ mile course from their headquarters on the Cam, which Cambridge won 30 pts. to 52 against seven Belgrave men, Dan Patience finishing second to D. C. Chamberlain; the printed Cambridge placings add to 29, not the printed 30. By Harry Shields. It was a pity that for this new and attractive fixture only 7 men, with Harry Parker as team manager, could manage to make the journey. However, it was a cheerful party that met on Liverpool Street Station and caught the train to Cambridge, where they were met and escorted to the University's headquarters on the bank of the River Cam. The course consisted of one 7½ mile lap containing about 3 miles of plough and two hills and as can be well imagined, was a good testing course. Getting off to a very fast start, the Cambridge men for the first mile were predominant but after settling down Dan Patience went up with the leaders whilst Tom Carter, Alf Shaw and Harry Shields also occupied prominent positions. The plough, however, soon proved the fitness of the Cambridge men—enabling them to run out easy winners as shown below. The result, however, is far from discouraging, bearing in mind the time of the year, the far heavier defeats that Cambridge have inflicted on other teams, and the fact that we were far below full strength. Dan Patience's running against D. C. Chamberlain, admittedly one of the fittest men in England, bore the mark of International honours to come. Tom Carter shows a gradual return to form, whilst the running of Herbert and Quackenbos, both of whom have done very little training, was very creditable and points to them being very useful team members in the New Year. An excellent tea wound up a pleasant afternoon with a sincere hope from all that this enjoyable fixture will be long continued. RESULTS. Cambridge U. (1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9)... ... ... 30 pts. Belgrave H. items.label: December 1938
items.sum: H. E. F.'s exhortation to younger cross-country members to keep training and racing through the winter after the South of Thames Junior race, as a foundation for the track season.
items.s: In Terrorem. H. E. F.'s exhortation to younger cross-country members to keep training and racing through the winter after the South of Thames Junior race, as a foundation for the track season. There is a feeling among the younger members of the Cross-country Section of the Club, that once the South of Thames Junior race is over their season has finished. This is a fatal mistake. For instance, when you are transferred from one class at school, or one department at business, to another—can you sit back and take things easy? No! You have to jump to it! To concentrate, to study, and work hard to maintain that position. Therefore, to those of you who aspire to become potential track champions, don't slacken off now, or those joints will become rusty again. Keep fit! Keep training and you'll find, as the season progresses, you will desire to go faster and further than any previous years over the country. All of you can safely race at least once a month over seven miles up to February, and then indulge in some long steady spins before reverting to the track, as no serious work on the track can be done until the light evenings come round, which is time enough to think about speed work, etc. Give yourself a proper preparation—get stamina—which means strength of limb, muscular development of stomach—and wind—that is, lung capacity, using the chest to its utmost, all of which hard running over the country enforces you to do whether you want to or not. Don't forget that your time and facilities for training are limited, whereas when the time arrives for serious work, the Service and University type of athlete can train for hours nearly every afternoon in the best conditions, while you rush your training through in those brief few hours of the evening. Study the records. you will find that many track champions have also shone over the country—Sydney Wooderson and Reg. Thomas are two such—and remember that strength and speed make the champion every time. Some of you can make it! Who is it going to be? Those who have come off or those who this time have failed? You all have an equal chance, but it will require "guts." So to it, you fellows! H. E. F. H. E. F. H. E. items.s: Ten Years Back. Column recalling club happenings of ten years earlier from the Gazette: triangular matches with Ashcombe A.C. and Thames Valley H. at Feltham and Wimbledon, the South of the Thames Junior win at Epsom, open walks and club championships. Let us have a peep at the happenings of ten years ago. Our Gazette of this time records the results of one of the triangular matches between Ashcombe A.C., Thames Valley H. and ourselves, held at Feltham. We were successful with 77 points, to 275 of Ashcombe and 276 of T.V.H. Percy Bicknell, of the Valley, was the individual winner, followed by Cohen (Ashcombe) and Mick Pyer (Belgrave). Three weeks later a similar fixture was held at Wimbledon over a five miles course, and ninety runners finished. First man home was Cohen (Ashcombe) with Footer (Belgrave) second, and J. E. Flower (Belgrave) third. Once again we had an easy win in the team race, and the sealed handicap was won by S. Drake (3m. 15s.) with H. E. Footer (15sec.) second. Belgrave entered four teams in the South of the Thames Junior race held at Epsom, and our "A" team gained an easy win. It consisted of W. W. S. Mitchell (2), A. Penny (3), A. Allum (4), and W. A. Rice (13), and our enthusiasm was high. The first Open Walk of the season, promoted by the R.W.A. attracted 231 starters and we were successful in winning the scratch team race and "Berman" Cup. The Belgrave Open Walk had 246 entrants, and the scratch team race resulted in a dead heat between Herne Hill Harriers and ourselves with 41 points each. Our team consisted of T. W. Green, J. G. Scammell, R. D. McMullen and F. H. Elson The Club Junior Walking Championship for the "Horwood" Cup was won by Frank Elson, J. E. Field and J. Rathbone finishing second and third. The Seven Miles Cross-country Championship for the "Backstaffe" Shield was won by E. A. Duffett, with A. Allum and W. G. Webb in the minor positions. These were the happenings of ten years ago! items.label: December 1938
items.sum: E. A. Duffett's preview of the club's winter fixtures, from the Boxing Day track meeting at Battersea Park through the county, South of Thames and Southern championships to the English C.C. Championship at Worsley on March 11th.
e: South of Thames 7 Miles C.C. Championship
items.s: Forthcoming Fixtures. E. A. Duffett's preview of the club's winter fixtures, from the Boxing Day track meeting at Battersea Park through the county, South of Thames and Southern championships to the English C.C. Championship at Worsley on March 11th. The half-way stage of the Winter season has already been reached, although the big races have yet to come. This, of course, is as it should be; for with the gradual strengthening process, our runners should now be approaching that stage when they feel fit to take on all and sundry. The only possible snag is that with all the races taking place in the New Year, it is a question of the "cracks" indulging in races almost every other week. Only the very fittest can expect to stand up to this strain, and so it is essential to do the long steady training, which although at times may seem irksome, is the only way to reach the front rank of runners in the cross-country world. As a break from all this country training, we have on Boxing Day morning, at Battersea Park Track, a club track meeting starting at 11 a.m. There are three events, all on handicap lines, these being: 120 yards, 2 miles Run, 3 miles Walk. These are usual races at this meeting, which is very old-standing, and we must judge by the entries we receive as to whether our members still wish this meeting to continue. It may seem strange to some that we have a sprint event at this time of the year, but we have several sprinters out every Saturday from Wimbledon, and these men at any rate must be in a fair state of fitness. As to the other races, I am sure most of our distance men will welcome the break to shorter distances, and although they may be a little lacking in speed, remember it is a question of everyone being in the same "boat," so don't forget to enter and come along and enjoy yourselves on the "morning after the night before." After the holiday period is over we get back to our cross-country fixtures, and on December 31st we have the pleasure of welcoming the Junior members of the Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. This should give our junior members a chance of measuring their chances in regard to the coming Junior Championships, and I trust we shall have a good turn-out for this race. On January 7th we have the County Senior Championships, and the Surrey race is being held from the quarters of the Ranelagh H. at Petersham. This should prove a good cross-country course, and I look to our men to reverse their position with the Mitcham boys of last season. Now that the latter's Welsh members have acquired a residential qualification, it will be seen that our lads are faced with stiff proposition, more especially as our forces have to be split in these County races. Our members who run for the Cadogan A.C., in the Middlesex race proved to be winners last season, and we trust they will carry on the good work, and, on his present form, Dan Patience should go very near for individual honours. On January 14th we are staging the Surrey County Junior Championship from the "Belgrave Hall" at Wimbledon. Our 5 miles course will be used, and on their own "midden" I hope our juniors will succeed in carrying off team honours; while in E. H. Herbert we have a youngster who should trouble the best in the race. I would like to ask as many old members as possible who are free on this day to come along and give us a hand in staging this race, as many pointsmen will be needed, owing to the ban on laying a paper trail over the Common. On January 28th we are holding the Club 10 miles C.C. Championship at Wimbledon, while this season we are also holding the Club 5 miles Junior Championship on the same day. These will be two separate races, our 5 miles course being used in each case, with the Juniors doing one lap and the Seniors two. In conjunction with the senior race we shall have a Club sealed handicap, so I hope that all our members will support this race, as no matter what their position in the race, they should all stand a chance for the handicap (at least, this is what the Handicapper says). On February 11th there will be held the South of Thames 7 Miles C.C. Championship, and the venue for this will be Camberley. It is intended to use the R.M.C. quarters for dressing accommodation, so that all the runners should have no grouses in this respect, although this is not always the case with cross-country races. Then on 25th February we have the Southern Counties C.C. Championships at Apsley. This is near Hemel Hempstead and the palatial quarters of Messrs. John Dickinson & Co. Ltd., will be used to house the hundreds of competitors. There will be two races, the Senior race over 10 miles and the Junior race over 5 miles. At this stage of the season we can only hope for the best, but we have the men and if "Dame Fortune" will only smile on us for once, I am sure we can come out on top. I trust that Pat Parker will be at his peak by then, and with Art Penny, Bert Footer, Dan Patience and Tom Carter, to mention just a few, surely we are justified in feeling confident that we shall regain this championship, which we last held in 1934. We come then to the English C.C. Championship which will this year be held in the North, the venue chosen being at Worsley, near Manchester. As usual with these Northern venues, I expect the course to be a tough one, and I hope that as many of our supporters who can spare the time to make the journey will do so. Our boys will need all the vocal encouragement that they can possibly get. So make a note of this date, March 11th, and do your utmost to travel up to Manchester with our boys. No doubt a special train will run from London, and full details of this will be given at a later date. All entries and enquiries to— E. A. Duffett, Running Hon. Sec., 76, Greenside Road, W. Croydon. items.s: Field Events. W. H. J. Sutton's field events notes: Wednesday evening training at Wimbledon under F. Stampfl, a Boxing Day match against the Metropolitan Police, S.A.A.L. results and S. Jones winning the Harry Wright Shield. By W. H. J. Sutton. The evening training at Wimbledon on Wednesdays is going strong, averaging about fourteen members each session. The Club has purchased a medicine ball, two gym. mats, a High Jump bar, and a twelve-pound shot, and Alf Taylor has made a hurdle for indoor training. Under the training of F. Stampfl, the session starts with a one and a half miles warm-up round the Common, then about thirty minutes' strenuous exercises, followed by Hop-step-and-jump and High jumping, and instruction in the different technique for each event. Another Field Events match against the Metropolitan Police at Battersea Park on Boxing Day has been arranged. T. C. Jones, the Field Events Captain, will notify the men selected for the teams. The events are Discus, Javelin and Shot. The complete S.A.A.L. results now issued show that we have obtained 24 out of 69 of the first three places in the 23 events held, showing our individual performances, as well as team results, to be among the best. S. Jones has won the Harry Wright Shield for his excellent performance in the Shot—39ft. 1in. It is possible that the rules governing this competition will be rearranged to be based on the Finnish table of calculation which was used for the Olympic Decathlon. Enquiries to T. C. items.sum: H. M. Quackenbos's notes on the junior section: cross-country form and prospects in the junior championships, then a look back at a successful junior track and field season.
items.s: With The Juniors. H. M. Quackenbos's notes on the junior section: cross-country form and prospects in the junior championships, then a look back at a successful junior track and field season. By H. M. Quackenbos. So far this season very satisfactory form has been shewn by our cross-country men, and Beard, Shrubb and Herbert deserve special mention for their good running in the South of the Thames Junior Of the various junior championships our chances seem most favourable in the Surrey. We have a potentially strong four, including Boyden, in addition to the three above, and it will be surprising if we can't win the title, especially as the race will be held over familiar country from Belgrave Hall. The Southern Junior team will be weakened because Herbert and Boyden will be too old, but fortunately Edwards and Bradnum come in here. Lomas, Marchant and Scarfe represented us in the Surrey Youths' race and finished in position 21, 22 and 23. The first-named is a very keen newcomer who will do very well when he matures. Now for a word about the Track (and Field) season, which should have been mentioned in the last issue but wasn't, and on whom the blame rests only I know. Anyhow it was a most successful season and, if memory serves me, we won every match except one. The most gratifying thing, however, was the enthusiasm shown and at a match at Richmond, so many men turned up that they all could not be given a run, although would-be half-milers turned out in the sprint relay. Turner, Scott, Bowers and Shepherd formed a sprint relay team which was placed in both Southern and A.A.A. Junior Championships. Turner and Scott have both been close to 10.5 sec., while Shepherd has beaten 24sec. in the furlong and does a good quarter as well. Knight always runs a strong race in this latter event and with perseverance and a more relaxed style he should soon be doing about 53 seconds. In the half, Mumford, Marchant and Shrubb have all been running about 2min. 8 sec. and Reynolds hasn't been far behind. In the mile Bradnum has beaten 4min. 45sec. and has gained another standard medal in the A.A.A. junior steeplechase. Lastly, our two Field Events men, Butcher and Holloway, have been joined by a talented recruit, Harvey, who at the age of thirteen has jumped 4ft. 11in. Dunford and Cooper have both tried long jumping, with some success, but our star in this event, Peverell, had the misfortunte to break his ankle early in the season. items.s: 5 Miles Handicap (Walk). 1st October, 1938. Report and full result of the club 5 miles walking handicap on 1st October 1938 over a slightly altered course, won by H. G. Churcher (Harry Churcher) from scratch. The field for this was not as large as it might be, as most of our Police stalwarts were unable to turn out. The limit man, W. Brunning, started off up Lauriston Road, followed by the rest at varying intervals. A slight alteration was made in the course and this new course will be used in future races and training spins. Instead of turning left at Woodhayes Road, keep straight on along Ernle Road. This road bends to the left and joins Copse Hill; turn right and proceed as usual. This route shortens the course slightly. Brunning kept in front until Cambridge Road, when Charlie Speechley and Eddie Heather went into the lead. At the top of the hill Harry Churcher went in front and went on to win by over half a minute. This performance shows us that Harry means business in the coming "opens." Harry Thaxter and Charlie Speechley had a ding-dong battle down Lauriston Road for second place, Thaxter gaining the verdict by a very small margin. RESULT. H'cap Time. Allce. Act. Time. 1 H. G. items.s: The Highgate "Open." Report and result of the Highgate open walk, where Belgrave won the scratch team with 18 pts. and Harry Churcher beat Vic Stone (Poly.) by fifteen seconds; a few printed handicap times (H. G. Clayton, P. G. Wright, F. H. Elson, W. G. True) do not agree with actual time less allowance, and Clayton's team column is printed "1" where others have I, A or B. With our four scoring men in the first seven positions, we registered a win in the first "open" in no uncertain manner. Harry Churcher continued his unbeaten record of last season, to win by fifteen seconds from Vic Stone (Poly.). Both these men strayed off the course at three miles; as our man was leading he went further off than his rival. On regaining the course, Harry was a few yards to the bad; these he made up and won as stated. One interesting feature of the race was the performance of the R.A.F. (Halton) team. Making their début in "opens," they provided the winner of the individual handicap (who finished 8th) and took second place in the team handicap. Perhaps their success will prompt other sections of the forces to encourage road-walking. Their progress will be watched with interest by all. We were pleased to see our old friend Bert Field competing. He had come down from Birmingham with the Dunlop W.C. Our teams were unsuccessful in the handicap, perhaps that's just as well, for if we monopolise the handicaps, we shall soon all be on scratch! RESULTS. Winner of Handicap: W. A. items.s: The Enfield "Open"—12th November. Report and results of the Enfield open walk on 12th November, won by Harry Churcher, with Belgrave winning the scratch team race (the handicap team table prints third place twice). Our run of success in "opens" was continued in the Enfield "Open" race. Harry Churcher led the field home to win comfortably from Joe Coleman. Colin Sutton and Percy Wright completed our team in fifth and sixth positions. Charlie Churcher was hot on Percy's heels in seventh position—it seems that to be in one of our winning teams in an "open," you must make sure of your place by getting in the first four. Hard luck, Charlie! Leicester W.C. deservedly gained second place. The third place went to our "B" team, which, as far as the scoring went, consisted of "Juniors" Eddie Heather, Syd Roberts, Charlie Speechley and Harry Thaxter. This certainly augurs well for the "Junior" next March. Frank Elson deserves our congratulations on the way he is fighting to attain the speed which he had a few years back. items.sum: Walking notes on the good start to the road season, Harry Churcher's form, the coming R.W.A. Junior Championship and forthcoming walking fixtures.
e: London Tram and Trolley Bus S.A. Open
items.s: With The Walkers. Walking notes on the good start to the road season, Harry Churcher's form, the coming R.W.A. Junior Championship and forthcoming walking fixtures. The Road season has started well for us and gives us hopes that we shall again win all the Open 7 and 10 miles scratch team races. Numbers, too, are good, and it is gratifying to see that even if our first four men home were eliminated, we should still have men prominent enough to challenge, and even win, team honours. * * * * * Harry Churcher has found his form, and may well repeat last year's record when he won every "7" and "10" in the London area. We hope he will crown his athletic career by winning the A.A.A. 7 miles title next April, and so become the first Belgrave man to win an A.A.A. Championship. * * * * * Our strength at the moment is shown in the Enfield A.C. Open race result, where it will be seen that our Captain, Charlie Churcher, finished seventh and yet did not score in the winning team. We finished nine walkers in the first eighteen places, and our "B" team was placed third in the scratch team race. * * * * * To be strong and successful now is very pleasing, but how shall we be placed in a few years' time? All the indications are that we have among our young walkers many who will do extremely well in a few years' time, but we would again emphasize the necessity of introducing and training new walkers. * * * * * At this early date it is impossible to form any accurate opinion of our chances in the R.W.A. "Junior" Championship, to be held next March in the Manchester area. It is certain, however, that we shall have a worthy team, and one which may well gain our second successive win. Clayton, Heather, Roberts, Thaxter, Doubleday, Bridger, Goold, Elliott, East, Snell and others have great potentialities, and with conscientious, steady training, we may expect a team which will represent the Club with credit. * * * * * Walkers are reminded of the Club Junior Championship at 7 miles for the "Horwood" Cup, open to all Club members possessing the R.W.A. "Junior" qualifications. This will take place on December 17th, and a sealed handicap will be held in conjunction. This event has been postponed a week from the date originally planned, December 10th. * * * * * A three miles Walk handicap will be included in the Boxing Day meeting to be held at Battersea Park. Entries have been poor in recent years, and unless numbers improve, this race may disappear from our programme. Those with a "distance" interest will be competing in the Godstone and back race (18¾ miles) on Boxing Day. Full particulars may be had from the Walk Hon. Secretary. In the New Year we have the Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. Open 7 miles race on January 21st. The "Berman" Cup, which we hold, will be awarded to the winning scratch team. The following Saturday we hold the Club 10 miles Championship, and in conjunction with this event will be a sealed handicap and match versus Metropolitan Police W.C. and Surrey A.C. The third successive Saturday's racing will find us at Bellingham, participating in the Open race promoted by the London Tram and Trolley Bus S.A. On February 18th we shall compete in the Valentine's S.C. Open 10 miles race from their quarters at Chadwell Heath. A fortnight later follows the Junior Championship at 10 miles at Manchester. All entries and requests for information should be addressed to— A. A. HARLEY, 39, Roxborough Avenue, Isleworth, Mx. items.label: December 1938
items.sum: L. G. Bennett reviews the sprinters' 1938 season (Inter-Club relays, Southern Counties sprint relay, Middlesex standards) and invites sprinters to winter training with coach F. Stampfl.
items.s: The Sprinters And The Future. L. G. Bennett reviews the sprinters' 1938 season (Inter-Club relays, Southern Counties sprint relay, Middlesex standards) and invites sprinters to winter training with coach F. Stampfl. It is with great pleasure that, on entering into my twelfth season with the Club, I can look forward with so much confidence and optimism, so far as the Sprinters are concerned. The confidence in this section, which I expressed in a 1937 Magazine was not, in view of last year's results, in any way over-optimistic. I really must congratulate every man who represented the Club in 1938, also those who entered the handicaps and put up such good and enthusiastic showings. The spirit existing in the Sprinting Section is enthusiastic to a degree, and this has been shown by the keen competition to gain places in the teams. Now a word or two regarding last season's results. First of all the Sprinters gained maximum points in the Inter-Club Relay matches. This is, I think, the first time this has been accomplished by Belgrave. The times were remarkably good and justified the large margins by which the Club won each race. Next, a weakened team entered the Southern Counties Sprint Championships. True, the Club were lucky to reach the final, but here we finished fourth, with inches separating us from second and third positions, after having drawn lane, one which was waterlogged after heavy rain. As our first attempt this was a fine effort. Congratulations to Messrs. Skelley, Mewes, Pritchard and Blunden, who formed the team. (Congratulations also to Skelley on having his shorts passed by a Southern A.A.A. representative!). Remarkable results were obtained in open relay races. The sprinters all did their part, showing what fine Club-men they are. I must have a croak about Cadogan A.C. In the Middlesex County Championships four sprinters—Botwright, Wiley, Pritchard and yours truly, Bennett—entered and all gained County Standards. Botwright and Wiley also gained Southern Standards. These two, not forgetting Pack, were chosen to represent Middlesex County. The junior sprinters have shown a great improvement in ability and enthusiasm, and I do welcome most warmly those who have now reached the senior stage. You are the members who, by your example, strict training, and keenness will help to keep the Club at the top of the tree in athletics for many years to come. Your responsibilities are heavy. Well, let us look at the lessons we have learned during the past season. First of all, we must train strictly, regularly and with enthusiasm if we want to gain places in the Club teams. Secondly, we must all indulge in baton-changing practice. At the end of the year the teams had improved a great deal, but not enough. Now, I must pass on to Winter training. Here I recommend you to come over to Belgrave Hall every Saturday between 2-45 and 3 p.m. The sprinters have a special pack and a short cross-country run is enjoyed by all. This is one of the finest ways in which a sprinter can keep fit during the Winter. I have encouraged cross-country running for sprinters for several seasons past, and now the famous coach to the Club, Herr. F. Stampfl, has given his endorsement to this. Sprinters may also make use of Herr Stampfl's services if they go to Belgrave Hall on Wednesdays at 7-15 p.m. Ordinary road training facilities are also available on Tuesdays and Thursdays at the "Rising Sun" at 7-15 p.m. This Winter training has proved very useful to the following members, who ran so well last season: S. Botwright, S. Blunden, T. Wiley, A. Mewes, W. Timberlake, F. Simmonds, "Tubby" Smith, Laing, Reynolds and many others. Come over next Saturday and enjoy the good-fellowship which is fostered so much on these runs. To new members, I say that if I can be of any assistance to you, please write and let me know. Here's wishing you the best of luck, and I hope that you will all attend our Socials and Dances, which are announced elsewhere. L. G. BENNETT, 30, Applegarth Road, W.14. L. G. Bennett L. G. items.sum: Notice of Herr Stampfl's Wednesday exercise classes at Belgrave Hall for track and field men.
items.s: Winter Training. Notice of Herr Stampfl's Wednesday exercise classes at Belgrave Hall for track and field men. This is essentially for, but not confined to, track and field events men, whose Winter training is usually restricted. The Club has engaged Herr Stampfl to conduct an exercise class at Belgrave Hall on Wednesdays at 7-30 p.m. The exercises are designed not only for keeping fit, but to educate oneself to achieve greater athletic efficiency. Herr Stampfl, although he has been in this country only a short while, has established himself as a coach of the first rank. Having been a champion in recent years, he is well acquainted with the modern ideas for training. He is himself popular with those with whom he has been in contact, and those who have attended his classes were soon affected with his enthusiasm, and attend regularly. He will be unable to attend after January, but the Hall will be open on Wednesdays for the exercises to be continued until the evenings permit the normal outdoor summer training. F. Stampfl Herr Stampfl coach engaged by the Club Herr Stampfl Belgrave Hall

items.label: March 1939
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the English Cross-country and R.W.A. Junior wins, the Southern, international selections, new members, new field and track captains and F. G. Thomson's A.A.A. election.
items.s: The Hon. Secretary's Commentary. The Hon. Secretary's notes on the English Cross-country and R.W.A. Junior wins, the Southern, international selections, new members, new field and track captains and F. G. Thomson's A.A.A. election. The Hon. Secretary's Commentary. As we go to press comes wonderful news of the winning of the English Cross-country Championship at Manchester. A week earlier our walkers had won the R.W.A. Junior Championship, also at Manchester; and we congratulate both our runners and walkers upon their Championship successes in the North. Justice will be done to these races in our next issue. Meanwhile, well done! * * * * * Heartiest congratulations to Ted Stimpson and Arthur Penny upon being selected for the English Cross-country team to participate in the International event at Cardiff. Our best wishes go with them * * * * * Since our Annual General Meeting we have elected many new members. To R. G. Griffin, R. E. Jeal, H. N. Little, K. J. Winton, H. J. Dickinson, C. H. Dennis, W. M. Butt, J. F. Appleby, B. C. Leeden, J. F. Harding, C. H. Lloyd, A. H. Lomas, J. R. Gibb, J. McDonald, W. D. Buckley, W. E. Budden, P. W. Edwards, A. W. Edwards, L. D. Harris, C. G. Herridge, S. D. Richards, R. E. Duffett, H. B. Halls, K. Moe, J. S. Rowell and A. P. Stevenson we extend a very cordial welcome, and trust they will be with us for years to come. Some of the foregoing have already shown they have ability, and good fellowship, and by now are well established Belgrave Harriers. We would single out for a special welcome, Knut Moe, a Norwegian visitor, who will be with us only for a few months. * * * * * Congratulations to Harry Churcher upon continuing his amazing sequence of successes in Open Walks. Influenza prevented him from competing in the Valentine's Open Walk, or undoubtedly Harry would have scored another win and completed two full seasons without defeat in Open road walks. * * * * * Our spirited attempt to regain the "Southern" Cross-country title did not succeed but we had the satisfaction of taking third place and finishing within nine points of the winners, despite the fact that we were not at full strength. Tom Carter and Ted Stimpson gave a splendid display of running and should appear in England's team later in the year. A word of praise also to our Captain, Bert Footer, who travelled to the race as a reserve, but when circumstances forced him to turn out, called upon his store of experience and determination with such good effect that he was our fourth man to score, in 25th position * * * * * Our walking teams have managed to win scratch team race after race, and we hope to have similar success in the Championship events. Our all-round strength during the last two seasons must be without parallel, and if present enthusiasm and ability continue, we should have many further years of success in store. * * * * * We have a new Field Events Captain in Charlie Jones, who will receive capable assistance from L. Jackson, W. Sutton, H. M. Quackenbos, R. E. Jeal, S. Jones and others. With a new season about to begin, it is hoped that all members will co-operate with T. C. Jones and help him to build up a section from which champions and A.A.A. standard men will flow, and that they will continue to represent the Club with distinction and in keeping with the reputation the Club has earned in other branches of our sport. * * * * * A new Track Captain in Frank Webb will also require the help and consideration of all members. At the present moment our Summer programme is being planned, and it is likely to be a very heavy one. All track men are asked to support the Club handicaps. New members are invited, and requested to make themselves known to the Club officials and their fellow-members. Any member invited to represent the Club and unable to do so MUST notify the Captain in good time. It is a duty he owes himself as well as the Club. These points should be borne in mind by every Club-member. If every member resolves that he will not fail in these respects, we may expect the progress that the efforts of the Committee and the Club's hard workers deserve. * * * * * We were pleased that the Club's nomination to the Southern Committee of the A.A.A.—Mr. F. G. Thomson—was again duly elected, finishing seventh in the list of twenty successful candidates on this occasion. We are sure Mr. Thomson's efforts are appreciated at Crown Court Chambers, as is his work on behalf of the Club. * * * * * The Club is represented on other governing Athletic bodies as follows :— Road Walking Assn.—F. G. Thomson (Past President), A. A. Harley (Committee). Southern Counties C.C. Assn.—H. Parker (Committee). South of the Thames C.C. Assn.—W. H. Hare (Past President), H. Parker (Past President), E. A. Duffett (Committee). Surrey County A.A.A.—F. G. Thomson (Vice-President), H. Parker (Committee), J. G. Coleman (Committee). Middlesex County A.A.A. (as members of Cadogan A.C.)—A. A. Harley (Vice-President and Vice-Chairman), F. R. Webb (Committee). * * * * * The Club Track programme is rapidly taking shape. The dates allocated to us by the L.C.C. appear elsewhere. The Inter-Club relays v. Epsom H., Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. will take place on May 10th, and the "Doris Shield" Competition v. Ashcombe St. George's A.C. and Thames Valley H. on June 7th. The Club 3 miles Track championship will probably take place on July 31st. We have a very full programme of inter-club fixtures to fulfil on other grounds, and a series of Division II Southern Amateur Athletic League track races and Division I Field Events in which to participate. Additionally, we shall be represented in all the principal track competitions, such as the "Reading Gazette Trophy" competition, the "Waddilove Bowl" Competition at Birmingham, the "Kinnaird Trophy" Competition, and many other events of importance. It is hoped to issue the Club Summer fixture list towards the end of April. Members are particularly requested to note the date of the Ponders End Fête and Gala—July 15th—as at this meeting last year we won two trophies—for the Mile Relay and Three Miles Team Race—and we shall try and defend these with our strongest teams against all comers. * * * * * A suggestion has been made by Surrey Walking Club that we should meet them at cricket on one evening during the Summer. The Hon. Secretary would be glad to hear from any members who are interested. * * * * * The National Fitness Organiser of the Amateur Athletic Association, Mr. C. F. R. Hilton, has arranged for an athletic camping site to be open in Devon from July 3rd until the end of August. The site is situated 8 miles from Exeter and 5 miles from Dawlish and transport will be provided free from these towns to the Camp. The charge, including board and accommodation, will not exceed £1 per head per week. There will be a staff in attendance to do all cooking, etc., but those attending will be expected to perform some duties in connection with the maintenance of the Camp. A qualified coaching staff will be in attendance. Members interested should get in touch with the Hon. Secretary. items.label: March 1939
items.sum: Club notes on Christmas fixtures lost to snow, the Hon. Editor being pulled in a walk, Harry Churcher's walking wins, other clubs' magazines, Belgrave men in the Inter-Counties and a clash of walk dates. Includes a letter of thanks from Tommy Scrimshaw.
e: London Business Houses Road Walking Championship
items.s: This And That. Club notes on Christmas fixtures lost to snow, the Hon. Editor being pulled in a walk, Harry Churcher's walking wins, other clubs' magazines, Belgrave men in the Inter-Counties and a clash of walk dates. Includes a letter of thanks from Tommy Scrimshaw. The Clerk of the Weather has not been any too kind towards our fixture list. By giving us a White Christmas the following races had to be cancelled : Match v. Ealing H. and Metropolitan Police, the Boxing Day Handicaps, and the Croydon-Godstone and back Walk. The latter, as I understand, will be held later on. As regards the match on Christmas Eve, some of the Ealing and Police runners enjoyed a social run with our own lads; the only regret being that they had to soil the virgin snow with their footprints. I'm sure that they will always remember this run whenever they hear that well-known verse of "Good King Wenceslas." * * * * * To the cries of "You ought to go back to running, your Hon. Editor was challenged to place on record the fact that he was "pulled" in the Club "Junior" Championship. Having also been guilty of walking in a running race (Poly Marathon) my perversity would appear to be complete. I take comfort, however, in the knowledge that I must be "pulled" another five times before I can even think of calling myself a walker. * * * * * The appearance in the local press (re our Dance on November 26th), of a question asking whether we needed exercise, might be interpreted to indicate the inadequacy of our training, or that we had taken a leaf from the book of the local "Keep Fit Campaign." To this comment on our activities might be added the fact that many members (don't ask me why !) walked many miles home in the small hours of the morning. At a slightly larger hour they met again. What for? Oh, just for a training stroll! Harry Churcher gained further honours in winning the London Business Houses Road Walking Championship (7 miles). Eddie also gained distinction in this race by being the first man home from the West End Business Houses, thereby earning the crown which once belonged to Percy Wright. * * * * * I have recently had the pleasure of reading the official organs of other Clubs. One was from one of the oldest, "The L.A.C. News." In the three numbers which I perused were detailed reports of their activities, interspersed with articles by such well-known athletes as F. A. R. Hunter, J. E. Lovelock, B. F. McCabe, J. V. Powell and P. D. Ward; whilst there was an article by D. H. A. Christie-Murray on walking. The other was from one of the younger Clubs, "The Southgate Harrier." This gazette only came into existence last year, but it has already attained an excellent standard, and a high degree of enthusiasm supplies the undercurrent to the reports of the sterling performances by their members in matches and club races. I am sure that all readers of the "Belgravian" will wish for its continued success. Both these magazines make very good reading, and I am sure that their readers look forward to each issue. * * * * * In the Inter-Counties Cross Country Championship, held at Harpenden (Herts.) on January 21st, C. T. Carter and A. W. Penny scored in the winning Surrey team. D. Patience and H. W. Shields helped Middlesex to be runners-up, whilst E. S. Stimpson also appeared in the Middlesex team, but was not in the scoring. * * * * * The new date for the Surrey W.C. Croydon-Godstone and back walk, postponed from Boxing Day, is April 22nd. This, unfortunately, coincides with our own twenty miles road-walking championship, so that Belgrave vests will be absent from the Eastbourne road on that day. * * * * * One can quite truthfully say of Harry Churcher that "he takes the cake," for he was awarded a cake by the Editor of the J. Lyons & Co. Sports Sheet. This prize is awarded to the man (or woman) who has the most meritorious sporting performance of the week to their credit. Harry's award was in respect of his win in the Ashcombe-St. George's open race. That a first-class walking performance was thus recognised will be a source of gratification to all interested in athletics; as only one award is made each week, and all sports and games are taken into consideration before the recipient is selected. * * * * * Support the Brighton Relay on April 8th. I have much pleasure in reproducing the following letter, as its contents will be of interest to many of our Club folk. Its non-inclusion in our last issue was unfortunate but unavoidable. 3b, Cranbrook Road, S.W.19. 29th October, 1938. Please convey my thanks to the members of the Club for the extremely useful present they have presented to me. It will always remind me of the very pleasant times I have had with the fellows. Wishing the Club every success in the future. Sincerely yours, TOMMY SCRIMSHAW. Harry Churcher Harry Churcher won London Business Houses Road Walking Championship (7 miles); awarded J. Lyons & Co. items.sum: H. W. Shields's report and full result of the club 7 miles cross-country championship of 10 December 1938, won by C. T. Carter, with the handicap won by J. R. Shotter and Belgrave H. beating Cadogan A.C. on team scores.
items.s: 7 Miles C.C. Championship. H. W. Shields's report and full result of the club 7 miles cross-country championship of 10 December 1938, won by C. T. Carter, with the handicap won by J. R. Shotter and Belgrave H. beating Cadogan A.C. on team scores. 10th December, 1938. The long-sought cure for the alleged slow starts of our teams in championships can be said to have been found. Whether it was design or accident has not yet been discovered, but the struggle of Belgrave's manhood for supemacy in the race to a camera some 200 yards down the course could only be described as on a par with the Gold Rush. The office of photographer to the teams should carefully be looked into! Settling down to serious work after this very fast start, Pat Parker forged ahead with Tom Carter, Dan Patience and several others in close attendance. This order was maintained until the hills were reached, when Tom Carter went strongly to the fore, and at the end of the first lap had established a useful lead, with Dan Patience, Charlie Smart and Pat Parker following. This order was maintained to the finish, with the exception of Arthur Penny (who must have done fastest time in the second lap) who beat Parker for 4th place. Congratulations to J. R. Shotter, who closely won the handicap held in conjunction with the championship, from L. Penny. Both of these, with careful training, should prove very useful acquisitions to our future championship teams. Micky Walker obtained 3rd place in the handicap and will, no doubt, get much encouragement from his fine run. Several of our younger members gave sterling accounts of themselves : Beard, Rispin, Shrubb and others, who will prove their worth in later races. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. Pos. Name. items.h: Junior Match v. Blackheath and Old Croydonians H.
items.sum: E. A. Duffett's report and result of the junior cross-country match of 31 December against Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. at Belgrave Hall, won by Belgrave with 31 points to Blackheath's 37 though M. W. Jenkins of Blackheath took first place.
e: Junior Match v. Blackheath and Old Croydonians H.
items.s: Junior Match v. Blackheath and Old Croydonians H. E. A. Duffett's report and result of the junior cross-country match of 31 December against Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. at Belgrave Hall, won by Belgrave with 31 points to Blackheath's 37 though M. W. Jenkins of Blackheath took first place. On Saturday, December 31st, we had the pleasure of entertaining the Junior members of the Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. It was the first time we had met these clubs in a cross-country match and I hope they enjoyed their visit to Belgrave Hall. A field of just under 30 runners faced our President, who acted as starter, but owing to the Old Croydonians being rather short of men, it was decided to score 5 aside. After the usual fast start our boys soon forged to the front, and when they came to the Kingsmere and turned towards the Windmill and home, it was seen that E. H. Herbert was leading, with W. E. Beard next, followed by B. Rowe, who is a newcomer to our ranks. Leading a small bunch of black vests was M. W. Jenkins, of Blackheath, and he displayed fine judgment in moving up to his opponents, so that by the time the runners had passed the Windmill, Herbert only led him by a mere 10 yards. Beard and Rowe were next, but our other men seemed rather a long way back. Jenkins soon had the measure of our lad and eventually ran home an easy winner in quite good time for this course. Herbert was a good second with Beard close behind, and then came Rowe, who had quite surprised us by his form in his first club race. As, however, both the Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians wear black vests, what had seemed at first a most formidable bunch of opponents just behind our boys, turned out to consist of three "Heathens" and two "Old Boys." Thus scoring five aside, we came out narrow winners by the margin of 6 points from Blackheath. We sincerely hope that next season we shall renew our sporting rivalry over the country with our opponents on this occasion. RESULT. Pos. Name Club Time 1 M. W. Jenkins Bkh. 31 31 2 E. H. items.sum: T. C. Jones's report of the Surrey County Senior cross-country championship at Petersham, won by Mitcham from Surrey with Belgrave third and C. T. Carter third individually; the text puts Herbert 28th at half distance while the result lists L. W. Herbert 18.
items.s: Surrey County Senior Championship. T. C. Jones's report of the Surrey County Senior cross-country championship at Petersham, won by Mitcham from Surrey with Belgrave third and C. T. Carter third individually; the text puts Herbert 28th at half distance while the result lists L. W. Herbert 18. The Surrey County Championship was run over the Ranelagh Harriers' course at Petersham this year—a slightly hilly course. Our team was not so strong as in former years, owing to the absence of Footer and Cohen, but we had hopes of at least repeating our performance of last year in finishing second to Mitcham. The draw for positions was not too favourable to us and our boys did not get away too well, Kemp being the only one in the first dozen after about a mile. When the runners were next seen, at about half distance, Carter was in the first three, together with Brown (Mitcham) and Hines (Surrey), with Penny (7th), Kemp (25th), Lucas (27th), Herbert (28th) and Mick Walker (30th) completing our scoring six. Mitcham seemed to be leading Surrey by a few points with ourselves third, and it looked as if we would have to put in a lot of running in the second lap to gain the points required to put us close up to Mitcham and Surrey. About a quarter of a mile from the finish Brown (Mitcham) led, followed by Close (Surrey) about 40 yards behind, who was closely followed by Carter, and so the first three stayed until the finish. A quick check-up of the scores showed that although we had gained a number of points in the last lap, both Mitcham and Surrey had gained points and kept well in front of us. Mitcham eventually ran out winners, to add to their success of last year, but only by a few points from Surrey, with ourselves filling third place. Congratulations to Tom Carter on his excellent showing and to all the rest of the team, and further congratulations to Carter and Penny on being selected to represent the County in the Inter Counties Race. items.s: The Middlesex Cross Country Championship. Report of the Middlesex cross-country championship, in which Belgrave's Middlesex-qualified members ran as Cadogan A.C. and beat Thames Valley Harriers and Polytechnic Harriers, with Ted Stimpson second. In this event our members who possess qualifications for this County ran for Cadogan A.C. Although they were without the assistance of J. C. Smart, A. E. Taylor and H. G. Verney, they scored a convincing win over Thames Valley Harriers and Polytechnic Harriers, who were much fancied by the newspaper prophets to win easily. Ted Stimpson gave a first-class performance to finish second individual. The rest of our team packed very well—D. Patience was 4th, H. W. Shields 7th, A. Allum 14th, R. Tobin 15th and F. R. Webb 17th. The next Cadogan man home was A. Smith, who gave one of the best performances of his career to finish 58th. Although just missing inclusion in the scoring six, Bert can claim satisfaction in the knowledge that had his performance been required for the team, they would still have won. Another feature of our win was the fine running, on a very heavy course, of two veterans, A. Allum and F. R. Webb. J. Daly was Cadogan's only other representative in this race and, no doubt, he was as pleased with carrying the colours of a winning team as though he were one of the scorers! He finished 96th. The positions given of our scoring men are their scoring positions, and not their actual positions. J. C. Smart J. C. Smart absent A. E. Taylor A. E. Taylor absent H. G. Verney H. G. items.label: March 1939
items.sum: Report of Belgrave's convincing team win (27 pts.) in the Surrey Junior cross-country championship on Wimbledon Common from the club headquarters, led home by E. H. Herbert in fourth, ahead of Surrey A.C., with Surrey Beagles and Mitcham A.C. tied third.
items.s: The Surrey Junior Cross-Country Championship. Report of Belgrave's convincing team win (27 pts.) in the Surrey Junior cross-country championship on Wimbledon Common from the club headquarters, led home by E. H. Herbert in fourth, ahead of Surrey A.C., with Surrey Beagles and Mitcham A.C. tied third. Our Juniors scored a most convincing win in this race, which was held from our own headquarters. They had the advantage of knowing the country, but the margin of their win outweighs any suggestion of "Horses for Courses." With the exception of F. S. Bradnum, who unfortunately had to drop out, they showed good packing and team work, as can be seen by glancing at their finishing positions. It was hard luck indeed that Bradnum was unable to give his usual sound performance. The fact that they excelled themselves in a Championship race shows that they have been training wisely. The day was rather muggy, and a large crowd of young runners started out on their tour of Wimbledon Common. Our lads soon found themselves in useful positions and our hopes were fairly bright when they left for the open country. E. H. Herbert led our lads home, finishing in fourth position, thus confirming the good form which he has been showing. Lionel Penny proved his consistency by finishing eighth, one place ahead of another promising runner, W. E. Beard. Len Marchant, 15th, completed the scoring four. To these four lads we give our heartiest congratulations on their well-earned honours. Our non-scoring men, R. Boyden 18th, J. R. Shotter 23rd, N. C. Shrubb 24th, have every reason to be pleased with themselves; for having the non-scoring men well placed adds relish to our win. R. V. Reynolds ran as an individual and finished 36th. Our Juniors can well be proud of themselves for doing their bit in upholding the Club's prestige. The Club, in turn, is proud of them and hopes to see them graduate to further honours. items.label: March 1939
items.h: "A Fight to the Death" or "Through Mud to Glory" or "The 10 Mile Championship."
items.sum: Ubiquitor's humorous account and full result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship of 28 January 1939, in which Arthur Penny retained his title after a close struggle with Tom Carter and G. Murdock won the handicap.
items.s: "A Fight to the Death" or "Through Mud to Glory" or "The 10 Mile Championship." Ubiquitor's humorous account and full result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship of 28 January 1939, in which Arthur Penny retained his title after a close struggle with Tom Carter and G. Murdock won the handicap. "A Fight to the Death" or "Through Mud to Glory" or "The 10 Mile Championship." On Saturday, 28th January, the Club 10 Miles Championship resulted in Arthur Penny retaining his title after one of the best struggles that we have seen in a race famous for its keen struggles. The field was almost the smallest for several years, there being notable absentees, including Bert Footer. As usual, they started over the circuit of the field at a cracking pace, all in a bunch with Ted Stimpson, Penny and Harry Shields leading, but by the time they were back at the start (1 mile) there were three distinct packs with six in the fast, eight in the medium and I lost count of the slow. But half a mile later across the golf links they had to "paddle" a small lake (to the amusement of the spectators, but not the runners) and here Arthur Penny, with a determined expression, moved away from the others with Tom Carter hard on his heels. These two set a fast pace through the woods, and up the hockey field they had a lead of 25 yards from Stimpson, Shields and Dan. The sixth of the original fast pack, Jerman, was back another 50 yards with Tobin, Arthur Allum, and Murdock, on his heels. But the rest were already well spread out, breathing hard, some looking distressed, and it was here that I saw Jimmy Kemp collecting rude answers by standing on one side and telling everyone: "Only another 7½ miles!" Up to the pond Penny eased off a bit and seemed to be having a bad time and Carter took up the running, but he was unable to get away, and at half distance he led by a yard from Penny, with Stimpson 100 yards back, Dan another 50, and Harry tagging on behind. There was a gap of 150 yards before Allum came along just ahead of Jerman, Mick Walker and Alf Shaw, with Murdock and Tobin just behind. At this point I was pleased to notice the fine style and high position of "Champ" Smith. The waterlogged course was taking toll, and several dropped out here (ya yeller!), but Tom and Arthur went on relentlessly fighting each other across the golf course and its lake (very funny!) and they went down through the "forest" at a terrible pace, Tom trying desperately to get a lead. They were now well over 200 yards ahead of Stimpson, who had now been challenged by Dan Patience. Harry Shields was another 70 yards away and no one else was in sight. Going much slower up the hockey field, Tom still had his yard lead, but both looked whacked to the wide and were only going by will power. They stayed the same up to the pond, where Arthur made his supreme effort and burst away into a lead of 40 yards, which he held home. Neither had anything left and the time is a true testimony of their splendid efforts. Meanwhile Dan led Stimpson up the hockey field, fell 70 yards behind going up the hill, caught it up and was leading again half a mile from home; but he was unable to hold his gallant effort to the finish. Over the last mile they were both catching up on the leaders, although they finished over a minute behind Penny. Shields pounded along by himself and finished strongly, Mick Walker did well to finish 6th and Murdock is to be congratulated on a very good performance and his first handicap win in the club. While we are presenting bouquets, a special word of praise is due to Messrs. Stride (12) and Boyden (14), who showed splendid promise on graduating from the junior section. Good luck to them both; and a special word for George Still, who at 62 can cover ten miles at what seems to us a phenomenal pace—we expect him to win the race when he has had a little more experience! Finally, the handicapper did his usual fine bit of work—but don't tell him I said so, he knows it already! RESULT. Pos. Name Act Time Start H'c'p Time Pos. in H'c'p 1 A. W. items.sum: Report and result of the club 5 miles junior cross-country championship for the "Savage" Shield at Wimbledon on 28 January 1939, won by E. H. Herbert from L. K. Penny.
items.s: Club Junior C.C. Championship. Report and result of the club 5 miles junior cross-country championship for the "Savage" Shield at Wimbledon on 28 January 1939, won by E. H. Herbert from L. K. Penny. On Saturday, January 28th, at Wimbledon, we held the Club 5 miles Junior C.C. Championship for the "Savage" Shield. We were sorry the donor was not able to be with us owing to illness, and we take this opportunity of wishing him a speedy recovery to good health. Last year's holder was now too old to compete, owing to the age limit of 21 for this race, and a dozen Juniors faced the starter, each keen to be the one to annex the trophy. Lionel Penny led the field along at a fast pace over the first small lap and was still leading when they went out into the country. A small bunch, which included Beard and Herbert, had settled down some 30 to 40 yards in the rear, and in the long steady pull up to the Kingsmere, Herbert put in some telling work to overhaul the leader. On the run home via the Windmill, Herbert had now taken command of the race and was some 50 yards in front of Penny, with Beard about 30 yards behind the second man. At this point Shotter was putting in some very strong running but had left his effort rather too late, while Edwards and Shrubb were also running well. Marchant was not reproducing his Surrey Junior form but in view of his age this runner has many years left in which to win this race. We were sorry that B. Rowe, our young runner at Glasgow University, was unable to be present, while we must also congratulate J. McDonald on his plucky running after going off the course at one stage of the race. items.sum: H. Parker's report and result of the juniors' cross-country match against the Guards Depot at Caterham on 4 February 1939, won by newcomer W. Hewitt, with Belgrave winning the eight-a-side team race 69-76.
items.s: Match v. Guards Depot (Caterham). H. Parker's report and result of the juniors' cross-country match against the Guards Depot at Caterham on 4 February 1939, won by newcomer W. Hewitt, with Belgrave winning the eight-a-side team race 69-76. On Saturday, February 4th, an enthusiastic party of Juniors journeyed to Caterham to meet the Guards Depot in an inter-team contest. All were optimistic as to what the result would be, although the strength of the Depot was an unknown quantity. Our spirits were a little damped when the Sergeant Major told us that the course was a tough one. It was both hilly and heavy, two of our lads losing their shoes, whilst another arrived home carrying one! Afterwards they all agreed that they had had an enjoyable race! A newcomer to most of us, but one who has already made a name for himself in the North, W. Hewitt, ran home a very comfortable winner. We hope that he will carry our colours right to the front in the South. His time for the five miles was 33 min. 52 sec. Lionel Penny was the next to arrive in 34 min. 30 sec., followed by the first soldier, Sgt. Nelson, in 34 min. 40 sec. N. Shrubb was fourth, R. Boyden sixth, L. Marchant eighth, R. Johnson ninth, B. Martin fourteenth, A. T. A. Jordan twenty-fifth, J. Daly twenty-sixth, and P Stevenson, a newcomer from Glasgow, who lost both the way home and his shoes! completed our little band. The result of the team race, scoring eight aside, went in our favour 69—76. We have to thank the soldiers for the very splendid tea with which they provided us; but what was most appreciated was the MUG of hot tea which was awaiting the runners at the finish of the race. items.label: March 1939
items.h: The South of Thames Senior, Royal Military College, Sandhurst.
items.sum: Ubiquitor's report and our men's result in the South of Thames senior cross-country race at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, on 10 February 1939, won by T. A. Cattell, with Blackheath first team and an under-strength Belgrave sixth of 23 teams.
items.s: The South of Thames Senior, Royal Military College, Sandhurst. Ubiquitor's report and our men's result in the South of Thames senior cross-country race at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, on 10 February 1939, won by T. A. Cattell, with Blackheath first team and an under-strength Belgrave sixth of 23 teams. 10th February, 1939. R. I. P. When I first saw our team I thought that it looked quite promising, but when I found that Jerman had hurt his eyes (fortunately only temporarily) and could not run, that Kemp had a gammy hip, that Tommy Morrell was convalescent and that E. Herbert was not fit, I did not think it quite so good! Bels. were well drawn for once and Kemp made a clean start and the large field went away over the first lap round the very charming College Field (1 mile), and as they went by we had quite a few lying well up: Murdock 12, Tobin 20, Kemp 26, and E. Herbert 30, with brother Herbert not far away. Three-quarters of a mile later, when the runners disappeared into the wood, the position had not greatly changed, for Murdock was 13th, Tobin 18th, Kemp 26th, and although E. Herbert had dropped to 65th, Stride was running really well and had come up to 40th. After Herbert there was quite a patch of claret and gold. Johnson and L. Herbert were together 74 and 75, and another group of Messrs. Boyden, Smith and Rispin 84—86, while Mitchell at 112 was just two places ahead of Tommy Morrell. The course on the big lap was hilly, rather sandy, and loose in places, but quite dry, and the leaders began to go away from the rest of the field. I am afraid that some of our leaders lost a few places here, and half-way round the lap Kemp was our first man in 22nd, Tobin 23, Murdock 43, and then the rest of the team all within striking distance of one another. It was here that there was a steepish hill (ask the runners!) which I believe caught Kemp's hip rather badly, for he began to lose ground, but Murdock passed both Tobin and Kemp and made up several places. At the end of the first big lap the positions were: Murdock 19, Tobin 24, Kemp 32, Stride 46, E. (Young) Herbert going steadily at 71st, then a little pack having a friendly fight, Johnson 80, L. Herbert 81, Boyden 85, Champ Smith 86, and Rispin 87, with Mitchell still just ahead of Morrell a little further back. There was little alteration in positions over the second lap in the country, except for the steady dropping of Kemp, who was caught and passed by Stride at the top of the hill, but I did notice that the junior members of the team were running very steadily, and show promise of doing well, with a little more time and experience. Coming back on to the sports field, with only three-quarters of a mile to go, Murdock was 18th, Tobin 19th, Stride had run through to 37th, but looked rather tired, while Kemp was back at 54 and the brothers Herbert, L. and E., were 72 and 75. Our friendly pack all seemed to have decided that they had run together far enough, but as they all tried to get away from one another at the same time they were not very successful. Moral: start earlier next time! We were not in danger of being one of the first three teams, which was fortunate, as we lost several useful places over that last lap, as can be seen from the positions below. We did not even get the "12" shield for the first club to finish twelve men, usually a strong point with us, so it was perhaps a little disappointing, but I am sure that had we had a complete and fit team we should have had much more to sing about. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. 23 teams closed in. We are greatly indebted to Bill Sutton, whose details of placings during the race were most helpful. The conditions were excellent for running and the afternoon was warm, bright and sunny, and we, the spectators, had a very good time, with a pleasant coach journey through a beautiful part of Surrey for the moderate fare of 2/3. Why don't a few more people treat themselves to a really good afternoon to give the lads a cheer? m. s. 1 T. A. Cattell (S.L.H.) 46 22 2 G. Lucas (G. & D.) 46 43 3 R. F. Towndrow (Ash.) 47 9 19 G.
